jobs.title: PhD student in Materials Engineering - hybrid manufacturing and additive repair of gas turbine components
jobs.department: IEI - Department of Management and Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Your work assignments

In a net-zero energy system, gas turbines running on hydrogen-based and renewable fuels face increasingly aggressive operating conditions in hot gas path components. Extending component life through hybrid manufacturing and additive repair, rather than replacement, reduces material consumption and lifecycle emissions.

The PhD project will focus on the mechanical integrity and lifetime of hybrid structures in which a novel superalloy is deposited by directed energy deposition (DED) onto turbine superalloys. The work will involve developing specimen concepts and test methods for thermomechanical fatigue (TMF) and fracture mechanics, and using them to study crack initiation, crack transition across interfaces and crack propagation in hybrid and repaired material. You will also assess the interface integrity and link interface evolution and damage mechanisms to lifetime prediction and qualification methods for industrial use.

The PhD project is funded by the Swedish Energy Agency on hybrid manufacturing and additive repair of gas turbine components for future low-carbon energy systems. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with Siemens Energy and RISE.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in mechanical engineering, materials science and engineering, applied physics or a related field or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in mechanical engineering, solid mechanics, or materials science. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.  The requirement for a degree must be met no later than the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

The ability to write and communicate in English is a requirement. As a person, you are goal-oriented, analytical and persistent, and you enjoy experimental work and solving problems of industrial relevance. You can work independently and take responsibility for your project, and you collaborate well with colleagues and industrial partners.

Knowledge of high-temperature mechanics, high-temperature materials, physical metallurgy, fatigue, thermomechanical fatigue and fracture mechanics is a merit.

Your workplace

The Division of Engineering Materials conducts research as well as undergraduate and postgraduate education in mechanical engineering with a focus on materials. Our research covers engineering materials, mechanical testing and simulation, manufacturing and materials characterisation, in close collaboration with Swedish and international industry. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates. Read more: Engineering Materials (KMAT) - Linköping University

The employment

The employment will subsequently be renewed for periods of maximum duration two years, depending on your progress through the study plan. The employment may be extended up to a maximum of five years, based on the amount of teaching and departmental duties you have carried out. Further extensions can be granted in special circumstances.

jobs.title: PhD student in Communication-Efficient Distributed Inference
jobs.department: ISY - Department of Electrical Engineering
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a highly talented and motivated Ph.D. candidate to join our research team in scalable and secure distributed inference. This project, “Communication-Efficient Synchronization of Predictions for Distributed Intelligent Systems (CESP)”, is funded by the Swedish Research Council (VR).

Your work assignments

The project aims to establish a theory for communication-efficient cooperation among distributed predictive agents, with a focus on synchronization of predictions under mismatched local contexts and models for robust decisionmaking. The project will combine tools from information and communication theory, signal processing, and statistical learning. It is suitable for a candidate who is interested in developing rigorous foundations while also validating ideas through modern distributed generative and agentic AI systems.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Applied Mathematics with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or Applied Mathematics. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way. The requirement for a degree must be met no later than the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

Applicants must demonstrate strong mathematical maturity, solid programming skills, and an excellent ability to communicate in English, both orally and in writing. You must also be able to work independently, be goal-oriented, communicate clearly, and collaborate effectively with others.

We especially welcome strong applicants from backgrounds such as information theory, communication theory, signal processing, optimization and learning, applied probability and statistics, and distributed systems.

Your workplace

You will be based in the Division for Communication Systems (KS), Department of Electrical Engineering (ISY), Linköping University. The Division for Communication Systems carries out research, undergraduate and postgraduate education in communications engineering, statistical signal processing, network science, and decentralized machine learning. Welcome to read more about us at: https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/isy/ks.

For more information about working at ISY, please visit: https://liu.se/en/article/open-positions-at-isy.

You will become a key member of a dynamic and ambitious research team led by Asst. Prof. Khac-Hoang Ngo. The team currently consists of 4 PhD students working on massive connectivity, point-cloud transmission, distributed inference, and AI security. Check the website https://khachoang1412.github.io/ and our recent relevant work, including:

• Type-Based Unsourced Federated Learning With Client Self-Selection, IEEE ICC 2026.

to Multi-Target Localization, IEEE Trans. Wireless Commun., 2026.

Linköping University is ranked 43rd globally in AI research, 12th in Europe, and is recognized as a leading university in Sweden in this field, according to Vinnova’s report on strategic technologies for Sweden. In addition, Linköping has been awarded “Student City of the Year” in Sweden three times.

jobs.department: ISY - Department of Electrical Engineering
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student in automatic control at the Department of Electrical Engineering (ISY).

Your work assignments

This PhD project is part of a close collaboration between Linköping University and Lund University within the ELLIIT programme (https://elliit.se/) and aims to develop the next generation of intelligent sensor systems capable of providing reliable situational awareness in complex and dynamic environments. The research is driven by applications where current technology is insufficient, such as large-scale biodiversity monitoring in natural environments, smart agricultural and ecosystem applications within AgTech (https://agtechsweden.com/), search-andrescue operations in challenging terrain, and intelligent surveillance for societal security. By combining machine learning with model-based methods, the project enables systems that can detect, distinguish, and track multiple simultaneous events or objects using sensor information from, for example, radio, audio, and vibration signals, even under uncertain and disturbed conditions. The goal is to develop robust and scalable solutions that can form the basis for future technological breakthroughs in areas ranging from environmental monitoring and emergency response to security and biodiversity conservation.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

mentioned above. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way. The degree requirement must be met no later than at the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

jobs.title: PhD student in Business Administration
jobs.department: IEI - Department of Management and Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Would you like to explore how working life can become more inclusive for employees with disabilities? Join a doctoral research project focused on dignity, equity, and employee well-being through relational care and full inclusion.

Your work assignments

You will undertake doctoral research within the project Transforming Disability Management through Relational Care and Full Inclusion: Advancing Dignity, Equity, and Employee Well-Being in Working Life. The project examines disability management through the perspectives of full inclusion and relational care ethics, placing the lived experiences and knowledge of employees with disabilities at the centre of understanding organisational practices and relationships.

The project takes an interdisciplinary approach to organisational research, bringing together knowledge from business administration, organisational behaviour, leadership, sociology, psychology, philosophy, and ethics. Throughout your doctoral studies, you will be encouraged to adopt a curious and exploratory mindset, broadening your knowledge across these fields while developing your own research focus within the project’s broader scope of organisational research.

Your doctoral research will contribute to exploring how organisational practices and everyday workplace relationships can support dignity, equity, and employee well-being. The project uses a qualitative, interpretive approach combining case studies, ethnographic research across multiple sites, and the co-production of knowledge with participating actors. Within this research setting, you will develop your doctoral study in dialogue with your supervisors and contribute to the project’s empirical and theoretical work.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have been awarded a degree at advanced level in a field relevant to research in business administration and organizational research, or you have completed courses totalling at least 240 higher education credits, including at least 60 credits at advanced level in business administration or the equivalent. Other subject areas may be considered if they are closely related to the research area in question. Alternatively, you may demonstrate knowledge in the field by other means. The requirement for a degree must be met no later than the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

You have a particular interest in organisational research with an emphasis on working life, especially in understanding the interplay between work organisations, policies, and management methods. You are interested in how these shape everyday working conditions, workplace relationships, and individuals’ experiences of working life, as well as their implications for society at large. You have strong proficiency in spoken and written English, which will be the primary language for communication, academic writing, and research throughout your doctoral studies.

You demonstrate strong intellectual ability and scientific curiosity, with a capacity for analytical thinking, critical reflection, and exploring complex questions from different perspectives. You are motivated to develop new knowledge that contributes to socially sustainable working life and societies. You are keen to deepen and challenge your understanding and engage openly with different ideas. You are able to collaborate effectively with the research group and other members of the academic community, as well as plan and conduct research activities independently. You are ready to approach doctoral studies as the foundation for your professional development as an academic, actively engaging and collaborating with the research group and with national and international research communities. You are willing to receive, reflect on, and constructively respond to critique and feedback, using these exchanges to strengthen your research and academic development.

Please include a statement of intent with your application. Describe your academic background, research interests, and motivation for pursuing doctoral studies, and explain how these relate to the advertised project. Outline a research question or area you would be interested in exploring within the project and explain why it interests you. Reflect on how you would like to develop as a researcher and contribute to a collaborative research environment. The statement should communicate your initial ideas and motivation; a fully developed research proposal is not required.

Your workplace

You will be based at the Department of Management and Engineering (IEI) at Linköping University. The department brings together research in fields including business administration, economics, law, and engineering, providing a broad disciplinary setting for the project.

Your doctoral research will be situated within business administration and organisation studies, with a focus on the ethical and relational dimensions of organising, inclusion, and working life. Within the project, you will explore these questions through an interdisciplinary approach and develop your research in dialogue with your supervisors, the research group, and wider research communities.

The employment

jobs.title: PhD student in Environmental Science
jobs.department: TEMA - Department of Thematic Studies
jobs.description_html:
We are now looking for a PhD in Environmental Science with focus on chemical characterization of effluent organic matter.

Your work assignments

You will be a part of a national transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, co-production of new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities, Linköping University and Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, as well as about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system (www.biogasresearchcenter.se). It also has support from the Swedish Energy Agency. This position is announced as part of the research area "Substrates,  Processes, and Products" within BSRC.

Processing of biomass residues for material and energy recovery generate effluents containing complex organic mixtures. The main purpose of the PhD project is to investigate molecular complexity of effluent organic matter from sources such as agricultural, municipal and industrial activities and to assess their characterization and transformation where these materials are processed, with emphasis on anaerobic bioprocessing technologies. Current understanding of the dynamics of effluent organic matter mainly refers to change of bulk properties. The proposed research aims to advance this science to knowledge of transformation processes at the molecular level using advanced analyses like nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and high-resolution mass spectrometry (MS). This knowledge will enable defining strategies to promote the utilization of effluent organic matter as potential valuable products.

Understanding the molecular complexity of effluent organic matter has a particular relevance due to the significance of these material streams as biofertilizers and sustainable sources of nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon. The PhD project intends to assess utilization of effluent organic matter as biofertilizers for enhancing the soil health and carbon stock, promoting circular bioeconomy principles for sustainable food production.

As a PhD student you will be expected to conduct independent research in line with the research focus. The work assignments particularly relate to the focus area on interplay between physicochemical and microbiological parameters with dynamics of organic matter in anaerobic bioprocesses. Also, it includes the management and feeding of biogas reactors with the focus of production of specific organic molecules of interest. This includes responsibility for research that involves planning, sampling, reactor maintenance, overall laboratory work connected to biogas processes, data processing and writing scientific articles.

As a doctoral student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research project of which you are a part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time.

Your qualifications

Relevant subjects for eligibility include, for example, analytical chemistry, environmental chemistry, chemical biology, chemical engineering, or an equivalent field. You have graduated at Master´s level or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be on advanced level. Alternatively, you have gained corresponding knowledge in another way. Special qualifications: 90 credits of your total credits should be in a subject of central importance to the research area.

Documented practical experience and theoretical knowledge in advanced chemistry, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and the planning and execution of laboratory studies are particularly merited. Documented practical experience and theoretical knowledge in the operation and monitoring of bioreactors are merited.

Great importance will be placed on personal qualities and suitability. You are independent, responsible, and meticulous, with the ability to structure and drive your work forward. You have a strong focus on quality, pay close attention to detail, and regard accurate laboratory documentation as an important part of your work. We also expect you to have the willingness and ability to learn new techniques and concepts, particularly in chemistry, and to apply them in an interdisciplinary research environment. You have good collaboration skills and contribute to a supportive and open working environment. You readily share knowledge and information and enjoy collaborating with others on joint projects. You are attentive and respectful in your interactions with others and communicate clearly and naturally, both individually and in groups.

Your workplace

Environmental Change carries out research and education on the interaction between environment and society in an analytically innovative way. Third cycle and first cycle studies specialising in environmental science are carried out at the department. First cycle studies include a bachelor's and a master's programme, as well as stand-alone courses and teacher-training courses in environment science, thematic natural science and geography.

The employment

When taking up the post, you will be admitted to the program for doctoral studies. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University

The employment has a duration of four years’ full-time equivalent. You will initially be employed for a period of one year. The employment will subsequently be renewed for periods of maximum duration two years, depending on your progress through the study plan. The employment may be extended up to a maximum of five years, based on the amount of teaching and departmental duties you have carried out. Further extensions can be granted in special circumstances.

jobs.title: PhD student in computer science with focus on Automatic Formal Verification of Cyber Physical Systems (CPS).
jobs.department: IDA - Department of Computer and Information Science
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student in computer science with focus on Automatic Formal Verification of Cyber Physical Systems (CPS).

Your work assignments

As a PhD student in formal verification of embedded software, you will advance state of the art in the fast-moving field of formal verification of AI-generated solutions.

Background: The project is funded by ELLIIT: The Excellence Centre at Linköping – Lund in Information Technology. It focuses on agentic applications that generate embedded software involving neural network (NN) components. Agentic applications are fundamentally changing entire businesses. This raises unprecedented challenges in terms of understanding and reasoning about the safety and the security of generated solutions. We specifically focus on formally proving correctness of solutions obtained via agentic applications producing embedded software incorporating NN components.

Objective: The objective of the project is to address how we can formally reason about, and automatically generate and validate proofs and assumptions on, the correctness of NN-based embedded software generated by agentic applications. Current verification techniques are incapable of handling very large neural networks and those powering LLMs and agentic applications are way out of reach even for the latest NN verification techniques. Instead, we build on existing formal verification techniques for software and computer systems and leverage on the promising capabilities of modern AI to help with generating code and proofs.  

The main research challenge is to provide means to establish relevant formal guarantees for realistic and useful classes of software that is dynamically generated by agentic applications for embedded and safety critical systems.

Assignments: Your tasks include identifying and generalizing applications of AI generated formal proofs for NN-based software generated by AI-agents. You will build a framework that enables trade-offs between generality of the generated software and the formal guarantees it can provide. This will require from you to continuously reason about, and propose, approaches to formally handle complex logical formulas. You will also have to develop new abstraction and verification techniques, and to finetune and adapt modern LLMs.

As a PhD student, you will devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You should have graduated with a Master’s level in Computer Science / Software Engineering / Artificial Intelligence or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced levels in Computer Science / Software Engineering / Artificial Intelligence. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

We are looking for a committed and enthusiastic PhD student to join our research group. You should enjoy working with, and learning from, co-workers as well as sharing your knowledge and experience with them. You are expected to support the activities of the group and to engage with the group members and with colleagues.

The project targets fundamental contributions to a fast-moving field. It will require from the PhD student a deep scientific curiosity and a strong drive for independent and critical thinking. The candidate must show excellent communication skills in written and spoken English.

The candidate must also demonstrate programming skills, preferably with cyber physical / IoT systems. An excellent base in discrete mathematics and logic is fundamental, and experience with formal verification is a merit. Expertise with advanced AI techniques such as fine tuning LLMs or orchestrating agents’ work in software development is a merit. Having published in relevant international and leading conferences and journals is also a merit.  

Your workplace

The Department of Computer and Information Science was founded in 1983, but its roots go back to the early 1970s. It is one of the largest computer science departments in northern Europe. Our research covers a broad spectrum of fields, from core to applied computer sciences. Its vast scope also benefits our undergraduate and graduate programmes, and we now teach courses in several engineering programmes at bachelor’s and master’s levels, as well as the programmes in statistics, cognitive science and innovative programming. Read more at https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida.

As part of the Department of Computer and Information Science (IDA), the Division of Software and Systems (SaS) conducts research, undergraduate and postgraduate education in areas such as software technology, programming environments, system software, embedded software and hardware systems, computer system technology, cyber security and real-time systems.

The Embedded System Laboratory (ESLAB) conducts world-class research on developing system-level design and optimization techniques for various CPS applications and architectures, including automative and edge applications.

As part of the ELLIIT project, you will be jointly supervised by Assoc. Prof. Ahmed Rezine at ESLAB (Linköping University) and by Assoc. Prof. Amir Aminifar (Lund University). You will be located in Linköping with regular collaboration with Lund.

jobs.description_html:
Your work assignments

The doctoral project addresses ethical questions about age as a basis for priority setting in health care, with a particular focus on the challenges posed by an ageing population. The project should have a clear ethical focus but may also include empirical approaches.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your main task as a PhD student is to work on your thesis under the supervision of our staff. As a PhD student, you will take courses corresponding to 60 higher education credits. These courses aim to deepen your expertise in your specialist areas and strengthen your overall competence in philosophy. Courses are normally taught in English.

This doctoral position is a collaboration between the Division of Philosophy and Applied Ethics (Faculty of Arts and Sciences) and the National Centre for Priorities in Health (Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences). The PhD student is therefore expected to spend approximately half of their time at each division. A workspace will be provided at both units.

As a PhD student, you are expected to contribute to the research environments at both units. You will actively participate in their research seminars and relevant research activities. Your duties may also include teaching, course development and other teaching-related tasks. As a PhD student, you are expected to be present on site on a daily basis.

The doctoral project is also linked to an interdisciplinary research group comprising several PhD students and senior researchers in ethics, health economics and law, including the supervisors. The group consists of researchers from the Division of Philosophy and Applied Ethics and the National Centre for Priorities in Health at Linköping University, and the Centre for Research Ethics & Bioethics and the Department of Law at Uppsala University.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

At least 30 higher education credits, or the equivalent, must consist of second-cycle courses in philosophy, practical philosophy, applied ethics, bioethics, medical ethics or theoretical philosophy, or equivalent subjects, including a thesis of at least 15 credits.

Important personal skills include good collaboration and organisational skills, as well as the ability to work under supervision, independently and in a team. You take responsibility for your tasks, organise your work independently and take initiative to make progress. Great importance will be attached to personal suitability for the position.

Selection will be based on the above criteria and the documents submitted with the application. The selection process also includes interviews and reference checks.

Your ability to conduct independent research will be assessed primarily on the basis of published research (including articles) or course papers. These may be submitted as 1–2 writing samples. Evidence of the ability to plan, carry out and coordinate research projects, as well as to obtain research funding, may be advantageous but is not required. 

Fluency in English is a prerequisite for participating in the research activities and other duties described above. Knowledge of Swedish is an advantage.

Your workplace

The Division of Philosophy and Applied Ethics (see also https://liu.se/artikel/filosofi) offers courses in philosophy at first-cycle, second-cycle and doctoral levels. The division has eight permanent members of staff. Our teaching covers all major branches of philosophy: logic, epistemology, philosophy of science, history of philosophy, ethics, aesthetics, philosophy of religion and more. We also offer courses in other areas of the university, for example at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences and the Faculty of Science and Engineering. We hold an advanced research seminar that meets on average twice a month, featuring invited Swedish and international speakers or our own academic staff. In our many interdisciplinary collaborations, we use a variety of methodological approaches and work actively with several other departments at Linköping University.

One such interdisciplinary collaboration is with the National Centre for Priorities in Health, within the Health Care Analysis Unit, Division of Society and Health, Department of Health, Medicine and Caring Sciences at Linköping University. The National Centre for Priorities in Health, the second workplace, is a national knowledge centre focusing on how limited health care resources should be prioritised. The centre is multiprofessional and, in addition to its research remit, has a strong external engagement profile, with staff advising government agencies, regions, municipalities and other actors in health and social care. The centre and its sister centre (the Centre for Medical Technology Assessment, CMT) have a combined staff of around thirty, including approximately ten doctoral students. There is an active doctoral seminar, as well as other seminars and meetings that provide opportunities for an active exchange of knowledge on issues relating to resource allocation in health and social care. The centre organises a national conference on priority setting in health and social care every two years.

jobs.title: PhD Student in Technology and Social Change
jobs.department: TEMA - Department of Thematic Studies
jobs.description_html:
We are now looking to recruit a doctoral student in Technology and Social Change.

Your work assignments

As a Phd student, you will devote your time to your doctoral studies and the research project of which you will be part. Your duties may also include teaching or participation in other departmental assignments, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time working hours.

You will collaborate with other researchers, while also being expected to carry out independent research in line with the project's focus. The position involves writing academic articles that will form part of your doctoral thesis, as well as presenting research findings at conferences and project meetings.

The aim of the project is to investigate how socio-technical systems change when biogas, which has previously been legitimized primarily through its function as an energy technology, is increasingly valued for several potentially competing functions. The Phd student will study how the multifunctionality of biogas affects socio-technical configurations, policy and institutional relations, and governance processes, with a particular focus on how different interests and values are negotiated across sectors and policy areas.

The research will focus on the Swedish biogas sector and will involve analysing the connections between biogas and areas such as agriculture, waste management and the circular economy, environmental governance, energy, and preparedness and resilience. The research findings will shed light on how emerging functions interact with established structures, and how new forms of governance and institutional relations develop as the role of biogas changes.

The successful candidate will be part of the national interdisciplinary competence centre Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). The centre generates new and relevant knowledge through co-creation and collaboration across different academic disciplines, as well as between researchers and practitioners from the private and public sectors. BSRC brings together researchers and support resources from two universities, Linköping University and the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU), as well as around 50 private and public organisations representing all parts of the biogas system. The centre also receives funding from the Swedish Energy Agency.

The position includes completing the coursework component of the doctoral programme, comprising 66 credits, equivalent to approximately two semesters of full-time study. You will also participate in one of the weekly seminars at tema T – Technology and Social Change.

A central part of the work will involve writing academic texts in English, both independently and potentially in collaboration with others. Your doctoral thesis may take the form of a monograph or a compilation thesis based on a number of academic articles.

Your qualifications

To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master's) degree, completed courses corresponding to at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits are at second-cycle level, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The specific entry requirements are met by applicants who have knowledge corresponding to 90 credits in a subject of central relevance to the theme.

Documented research experience and proficiency in qualitative methods is considered a particular merit. Documented experience of interdisciplinary research is also considered a merit. A good command of spoken and written Swedish is considered a particular merit. A good command of spoken and written English is a requirement for the position. Experience of collaborating with stakeholders outside academia is considered a merit.

Relevant academic backgrounds for this position include human geography, environmental science, urban and regional planning, political science, sociology, or related fields.

We are looking for someone with good interpersonal skills who is attentive and communicative, and able to build and maintain professional relationships. You work independently, take responsibility and drive your work forward with commitment and energy. You can organize your work and manage processes in a structured and goal-oriented manner. You are committed to the objectives of the research project and contribute to its development. In addition, you are creative and innovative – you recognise opportunities, think outside the box and translate ideas into practice.

In addition to the documents you wish to submit in support of your application, you must also include a statement of intent (explaining why you wish to pursue doctoral studies), of no more than one page, together with a research proposal of no more than three pages.

The research proposal should outline a possible research project within the scope of the position and should primarily provide an insight into your research interests and the direction you might wish to pursue. The proposal is not intended to constitute a definitive doctoral project; the final research project will be developed and refined as part of your doctoral studies.

The research proposal may, for example, address the following questions: What questions are relevant to ask, and why? What theoretical approaches could inform and inspire the research? What types of material or empirical data could be studied?

Your workplace

Technology and Social Change (tema T) is a nationally and internationally leading research and educational environment, where social science, humanities and interdisciplinary perspectives on technology, science, medicine and social change are central.

Research and teaching focus on how people create and use technology, and how technological change is intertwined with knowledge, politics, practice and ethics.

Tema T offers doctoral studies as well as undergraduate and Master's-level education, focusing on issues relating to technology and social change. At undergraduate level, tema T offers Bachelor's and Master's programmes in Urban and Regional Planning, as well as courses in areas such as philosophy of science and the history of technology.

Technology and Social Change is part of the Department of Thematic Studies. Read more about the department here.

The employment

jobs.title: PhD student in Computer Science with focus on cybersecurity and privacy
jobs.department: IDA - Department of Computer and Information Science
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student to conduct research on cybersecurity and privacy in next-generation immersive and networked systems. The position is part of SENSE-VR, an international research collaboration involving Linköping University and partners in the United States, aimed at developing efficient, secure, and privacy-preserving multi-user virtual reality (VR) systems.

Modern VR systems continuously collect and exchange sensitive information, including head movements, eye gaze, hand gestures, and other user interactions. Such information can reveal user identities and sensitive personal attributes, even when communications are encrypted. Furthermore, observable communication patterns may reveal information about user behavior. Protecting against these privacy risks while preserving responsiveness, functionality, and user experience presents important research challenges.

The research will focus on developing and evaluating novel privacy-enhancing mechanisms for networked and immersive systems, combining techniques from cybersecurity, machine learning, networking, and performance-aware system design.

Your work assignments

As a PhD student, you will develop and evaluate novel privacy-enhancing methods for immersive and networked systems. Depending on your background and interests, potential research directions include:

  • Privacy leakage and client-side defenses: Investigating privacy risks associated with motion, gaze, and other user data, and developing defenses that preserve application functionality and user experience.
  • Traffic analysis and privacy-preserving communication: Investigating information leakage through observable communication patterns and developing practical defenses that balance privacy, overhead, and performance.
  • Secure and encrypted processing: Exploring techniques such as homomorphic encryption for processing sensitive data on edge and cloud servers without exposing its contents.
  • Privacy-aware resource optimization: Optimizing privacy, latency, and resource usage across devices, edge servers, and cloud infrastructure.

Your research will combine the design and analysis of novel methods with practical implementation and experimental evaluation. You will collaborate with researchers in Sweden and internationally, including partners in the United States, and publish your findings at leading international conferences and journals.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in computer science, computer engineering, information technology, software engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field, or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in a relevant field. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

We also welcome applications from students who are currently completing their Master's studies, including their Master's thesis. The eligibility requirements above must be fulfilled no later than the time when Linköping University makes its decision to employ you.

You should have a solid technical background, good analytical and programming skills, and an interest in cybersecurity and privacy research. We value candidates who enjoy exploring new ideas, solving challenging problems, and combining analytical thinking with practical implementation and experimentation. Good proficiency in written and spoken English is required.

Experience or knowledge in one or more of the following areas is considered an advantage:

  • Cybersecurity, privacy, or network security.
  • Machine learning, data analysis, statistical modeling, or algorithm design.
  • Computer networks, distributed systems, or performance evaluation.
  • Practical system development, experimental measurements, or research-oriented programming.
  • Privacy-enhancing technologies, such as traffic analysis defenses, homomorphic encryption, or privacy-preserving machine learning.

We are looking for a curious and motivated person with a genuine interest in learning and conducting research. You should enjoy working both independently and collaboratively, and have an ambition to develop your research skills and contribute to high-quality scientific research.

Your application should include a brief statement of motivation (approximately one page) describing your interest in the position, relevant technical experience, and which aspects of the proposed research you find most interesting. We encourage you to highlight your main strengths and interests, including relevant experience from coursework, projects, or your Master's thesis.

Your workplace

The Department of Computer and Information Science was founded in 1983 but its roots go back to the early 1970s. It is one of the largest computer science departments in northern Europe. Our research covers a broad spectrum of fields, from core to applied computer sciences. Its vast scope also benefits our undergraduate and graduate programmes, and we now teach courses in several engineering programmes at bachelor’s and master’s levels, as well as the programmes in statistics, cognitive science and innovative programming. Read more at  https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida

You will join the Cybersecurity Division (CYBER) at Linköping University, working under the supervision of Professor Niklas Carlsson and alongside a team of PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and senior researchers. Our research spans cybersecurity, privacy, computer networking, performance evaluation, multimedia systems, and applied data analytics. We combine theoretical and experimental approaches to address challenging research problems and regularly publish our findings at leading international conferences and journals.

You will be part of a positive, supportive, and internationally recognized research environment, with opportunities to develop into an independent researcher, publish at leading international conferences and journals, and collaborate with academic and industrial partners in Sweden and internationally.

The employment

jobs.title: PhD Position in Cybersecurity for Decentralised Energy Systems
jobs.department: IDA - Department of Computer and Information Science
jobs.description_html:
We are announcing a PhD student position in Computer Science at the Division of Cybersecurity (CYBER), Department of Computer and Information Science (IDA), Linköping University. Your research will make decentralised critical infrastructure such as the power grid more secure and resilient using trustworthy AI-supported methods.

Your work assignments

Power grids and other critical infrastructure are becoming decentralised and digitalised with thousands of remotely controlled distributed energy resources (DER) and assets such as solar panels, batteries and EV chargers. This adds a new entry point for attackers and attacks can spread across many systems at once. Your doctoral research will develop trustworthy AI-supported methods that help such critical infrastructure assess these risks and their consequences, detect potential attacks, reason about response, and keep operating safely.

Within this area, your thesis can build on the following research directions:

  • threat modelling, attack-path analysis and risk reasoning for critical infrastructure
  • AI-supported, robust, and privacy-preserving (for example federated) intrusion and anomaly detection for distributed and cyber-physical systems
  • cyber resilience and decision support that turn security insight into indicators and actions operators can use

The work is carried out in national and European research projects together with academic and industrial partners. You will work closely with researchers and engineers in Sweden and Europe, publish in leading security and energy-systems venues, and make research visits to partner organisations. Over the four years you will shape your own research questions within the directions above.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You hold a master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering or a closely related field, or you have completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be advanced courses in computer science, computer engineering, or electrical engineering. Alternatively, you have gained corresponding knowledge in another way.

For this position you are required to have:

  • good knowledge of cybersecurity
  • knowledge or experience of machine learning, for example for anomaly detection
  • programming skills, for example in Python
  • excellent oral and written communication skills in English

It is a merit if you also have knowledge or experience of:

  • research, for example through a Master’s thesis or scientific publications
  • intrusion detection or network security monitoring
  • basic electrical engineering, power systems or smart grids
  • large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI
  • threat modelling, attack graphs or frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK
  • privacy-preserving, federated, explainable, and trustworthy machine learning

Scientific curiosity and the ability to think independently are essential personal qualities. You should enjoy working in a team and together with researchers and industry partners in several countries. Motivate in your personal letter why you are interested in this position and why you are especially qualified for it.

Your workplace

We are now recruiting a PhD student for a research project on biogas solutions in a flexible, resilient and sustainable energy system. The holder of this position will be a part of a national transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). It also has support from the Swedish Energy Agency.

Your work assignments

You will conduct research in collaboration with senior researchers and other PhD students. The research will primarily focus on biogas solutions and their role in developing a flexible, resilient, and sustainable energy system. The work will involve techno-economic analyses, mathematical modelling, and case studies focusing on the value of flexible biogas production, as well as the contribution of biogas to self-sufficiency and regional resilience. The analyses will account for uncertainties related to, among other things, policy instruments and market conditions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with industry and public-sector organizations.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Flexible X-ray detectors represent a future technology that can benefit applications spanning several scientific, medical, and technological fields. jobs.description_html:
by

2026-11-30

  • Temporary position
  • 100%
  • Umeå

Umeå University is one of Sweden’s largest higher education institutions with over 41,500 students and about 4,600 employees. The University offers a diversity of high-quality education and world-leading research in several fields. Notably, the groundbreaking discovery of the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing tool, which was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, was made here. At Umeå University, everything is close. Our cohesive campuses make it easy to meet, work together and exchange knowledge, which promotes a dynamic and open culture.

The ongoing societal transformation and large green investments in northern Sweden create enormous opportunities and complex challenges. For Umeå University, conducting research about – and in the middle of – a society in transition is key. We also take pride in delivering education to enable regions to expand quickly and sustainably. In fact, the future is made here.

Are you interested in learning more? Read about Umeå university as a workplace

The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Information Processing’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026.
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description 

The project will develop ultrafast optical logic and memory concepts using spatiotemporal metamaterials. The doctoral candidate will design metamaterial structures coupled to quantum emitters for ultrafast information processing and investigate how structured ultrashort light pulses can control optical and magnetic properties on femtosecond timescales.

The research will focus on developing sub-10 fs protocols for all-optical logic operations, data processing, and spatiotemporal magnetic memories. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, quantum emitters, ultrafast optics, and light–matter interaction, with the aim of creating new routes for information processing beyond conventional electronic approaches.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 3-month industrial secondment at NKT Photonics in Denmark, focusing on vectorial ultrashort pulses, and a 6-month research secondment at Imperial College London in the United Kingdom, focusing on nanofabrication and characterization.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Professor Riccardo Sapienza at Imperial College London and from an industrial mentor at NKT Photonics. The position provides the opportunity to work in a stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a prestigious European training network.

Fluency in English is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, metamaterials, magnetism, or related experimental or theoretical methods is meritorious.

Project description

The project will create spatiotemporal polaritons through ultrafast light–matter interactions in engineered metamaterial systems. The doctoral candidate will explore wide-bandgap semiconductors and high-quality excitonic or molecular emitters coupled to time-modulated gratings, with the goal of realizing hybrid light–matter states whose properties can be controlled on femtosecond timescales.

The research will combine ultrafast pump–push–probe experiments with sub-10 fs resolution, finite-element simulations, and quantum models extending the Tavis–Cummings Hamiltonian. The aim is to demonstrate coherent control of spatiotemporal polaritons and to design spatiotemporal metamaterial platforms supporting new forms of hybrid light–matter dynamics. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum optics.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. Umeå University is offering a PhD position in Computing Science with a focus on machine learning for graph transformations. The project investigates a hybrid approach that combines deep learning with grammatical inference to develop models that are interpretable, efficient, and mathematically verifiable while leveraging the flexibility of neural methods. If successful, the work has the potential to advance applications such as automated theorem proving, knowledge-graph inference, and causal analysis.

The Department of Computing Science has experienced rapid growth in recent years, with a strong emphasis on fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and bottom-up-driven research environment. Our workplace brings together a diverse community of individuals from a wide range of nationalities.

As a PhD student with us, you benefit from comprehensive career development support, opportunities for networking, and access to robust administrative and technical services—all within a setting that offers attractive employment conditions.

To learn more about the department, please visit: https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-computing-science/

Project description

Graphs are a fundamental way of representing structured information from sentences and computer programs to social networks and they are becoming increasingly important as generative AI systems move beyond text. To keep such systems safe and reliable, we need mechanisms that can ensure their outputs follow the right rules, much like guardrails that prevent language models from producing harmful content or incorrect code. This project introduces a new idea: instead of relying on opaque, heavy machine-learning models, it learns transparent, rule-based rewriting systems that can transform graphs, check the correctness of AI-generated structures, and even guide neural networks during inference. By combining techniques from grammatical inference, reinforcement learning, and efficient search algorithms, the method can automatically discover both the rules and probabilities needed to model complex graph behaviors, offering a more interpretable and verifiable alternative for future AI systems.

The student will collaborate closely with the PI and her research group at Umeå University to investigate the proposed learning approach. The PhD student is expected to produce research outputs relevant to the fields of theoretical computer science and symbolic machine learning.

Admission requirements

The general admission requirements for doctoral studies are a second- cycle level degree, or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits, of which at least 60 ECTS credits are at second-cycle level, or have an equivalent education from abroad, or equivalent qualifications.

To be admitted to doctoral studies in the field of computer science, the applicant must have completed courses totaling at least 90 higher education credits in computer science or in subjects directly relevant to the specific specialization.

Solid analytical and mathematical abilities Experience with machine learning Experience with formal language theory or automata theory Strong communication skills and proficiency in English The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively

Meritorious Qualifications

It is considered an advantage if you have:

Experience with academic writing Strong programming skills, particularly in Python Familiarity with knowledge graphs Experience with graph neural network

Personal Qualities

We value candidates who are:

Intellectually curious Self-motivated and well-organized Eager to engage with the scientific community

About the position

The position provides you with the opportunity to pursue PhD studies in Computing Science for four years, with the goal of achieving the degree of Doctor in Computing Science. While the position is mainly devoted to PhD studies (at least 80% of the time), it may include up to 20% department service (usually teaching). If so, the total time for the position is extended accordingly, resulting in a maximum of five years.

The procedure for recruitment for the position is in accordance with the Higher Education Ordinance (chapter 12, 2§) and the decision regarding the position cannot be appealed.

The expected starting date is January 12, 2027 or as otherwise agreed.

Application

A cover letter including a description of your research interests, your reasons to apply for the position, and your contact information A curriculum vitae Reprints / copies of completed BSc and/or MSc theses and other relevant publications, if any Copies of degree certificates, including documentation of completed academic courses and obtained grades Documentation and description of other relevant experiences or competences.

The application must be written in English or Swedish. Attached documents must be in pdf format. Applications must be submitted electronically using the e-recruitment system of Umeå University, and be received no later than December 7, 2026.

The Department of Computing Science values gender diversity, and therefore particularly encourages women and those outside the gender binary to apply for the position.

jobs.title: PhD Student in Applied Geophysics
jobs.description_html:
Offer Description

Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? As a doctoral student with us, you will work closely with leading researchers in a strong, international research environment, with access to advanced laboratory equipment and solid funding opportunities. You will be offered secure employment, high-quality supervision, and room to grow, both as a researcher and as a person.

We are recruiting a PhD student for a research project on regional exploration in Norrbotten, Sweden. Project is aiming to create a regional 3D geophysical model of the subsurface to guide mineral exploration and provide hints for possible deposits. Take the opportunity to study for a PhD in interdisciplinary, dynamic, international research environment in close collaboration with industry and leading universities worldwide.

Subject description
Applied Geophysics is a topic based on physical laws and practices, which combined with geological information can be used in a variety of applications. Geophysical research at the Division of Geosciences and Environmental Engineering includes both basic and applied research in exploration, environmental and engineering applications.

Project description
Rex project focuses on a full multi-scale geophysical prospecting for mineral exploration with added value of regional scale surveying for exploration targeting. Previous D-Rex project showed that by conducting geophysical surveys across regional-to-deposit scale it is possible to identify regional patterns, structures and anomalies that can be used to guide deposit-scale exploration.

Geophysical images transcending from continental- to deposit-scale can provide a better understanding of the geology of the region and how mineral deposits were formed and distributed. While allowing the identification of potential mineral deposits at a continental scale, and then focusing on specific areas for detailed exploration, they also lead to improved accuracy of mineral exploration by providing a more complete picture of the subsurface geology.

Duties
As a PhD student you are expected to perform both field work and theoretical work within your research studies as well as communicate your results at national and international conferences and in scientific journals. The majority of your working time will be devoted to your own research studies. You will work primarily with geophysical (magnetotelluric) data. 3D geophysical data modelling/inversion is a key focus of this PhD. You will work on development and extending our MR3Dmod modelling/inversion framework. In addition, you will have the opportunity to try the teacher role. As a PhD student, you work as a neutral party in many contexts, which provides a great opportunity to be involved in challenging development projects.

Qualifications
You must have academic credentials and recently completed your M.Sc or equivalent degree in geophysics, mathematics, physics, geology or other relevant subject. Good understanding of theory and numerical methods used in modelling and inversion is required. Experience in software development (Python in particular) and management of large data sets is important. You are expected to work in a team and are open to collaborate with colleagues and external partners. Fluent written and spoken English is required.

For further information about a specific research subject see; General curricula for the Board of the faculty of science and technology

Most employees in the research subject exploration geophysics are currently men therefore provided that the qualifications are the same, the underrepresented gender will be given priority.

jobs.description_html:
Offer Description

Malmö University is an innovative, urban, and internationally-oriented academic institution that, thanks to its committed and experienced staff, contributes to societal development. Here, teachers, researchers, and other employees with various competencies work together to conduct high-quality education and research. All professional categories and roles are important. You are welcome to apply for a job with us!

Here you can learn more about what it's like to work at Malmö University: Work with us

We are looking for   

Doctoral student in History and History Didactics at the Faculty of Education and Society.

Work duties   

Those appointed to an employment as av doctoral student shall primarily devote themselves to their studies. Those appointed to an employment as a doctoral student may, however, work to a limited extent with educational tasks, research, artistic research and administration, however, duties of this kind may not comprise more than 20 per cent of a full-time post (Chapter 5, Section 2 of the Higher Education Ordinance). 

The doctoral project will be part of the project “Modern Siddhas Along the Bay of Bengal: Tantric Pilgrimage, Vernacular Archives, and Transregional Networks” (VR 2026–01946), which investigates Siddha traditions along the Bay of Bengal from the eighteenth century to the present, offering a new framework for understanding South Asian religious history. The full project description can be requested from Manon Hedenborg White (contact details below). The project applies a connected histories approach and combines historical-critical textual analysis with ethnographic fieldwork to trace how Siddha-oriented communities and practices have circulated and continue to circulate along the eastern coast of India, within Bangladesh and in wider South Asia.

Applications for a PhD project dealing with any region associated with Siddha histories are welcome, although special preference will be given to a PhD project proposal that focuses on post sixteenth-century Siddha contexts in northwestern India or the Himalayas (including Pakistan, Nepal, Tibet/China), or in Hindi-, Odia-, or Telugu-speaking areas. 

Qualifications   

To be admitted to doctoral studies, the applicant must meet the general and specific entry requirements of the subject in question. Moreover, the applicant must be deemed capable of assimilating the education. 

General entry requirements for doctoral studies and study programmes (HEO Chapter 7 Section 39) have those who: 

  • been awarded a second-cycle qualification
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or 
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.  

Specific entry requirements for doctoral studies and study programmes have those who: 

Specific eligibility applies to those having obtained the command of language required by the education as well as having presented an approved independent thesis within History, Historical Studies or another relevant subject, comprising at least 15 second-cycle ECTS credits, or having been assessed by Malmö University as possessing equivalent knowledge.

Selection criteria 

Selection among applicants who meet the general and specific entry requirements shall be made with regard to their capacity to assimilate the education (HEO Chapter 7 Section 41). 

Selection among eligible applicants is based on the extent to which candidates are deemed capable of benefiting from the education and achieving its objectives. In assessing the ability of eligible applicants to benefit from the education, consideration is given to the applicant’s independence and planning in previous work; the applicant’s previously demonstrated ability to complete work satisfactorily; the applicant’s ability to formulate areas of inquiry and research problems relevant for the project “Modern Siddhas Along the Bay of Bengal”, both in previous work and in the research proposal for the planned doctoral project; the level of methodological and scholarly maturity demonstrated in previously completed work and in the research proposal, particularly qualitative methods including at least one historical research method; and the applicant’s communication skills, both written and oral, including evidence of training in Sanskrit and Indic vernacular language(s) associated with the Siddha contexts studied in the project.

In the admission process, consideration is also given to the language proficiency required for successful participation in the programme. It is a particular advantage if the research proposal clearly demonstrates the significance of the proposed project for the research environment in History and History Didactics, see the description under Faculty, Department and Research environment.

Interdisciplinary experience of perspectives derived from History of Religions, Religious Studies, or South Asian languages and/or literatures is considered meritorious.

Faculty, Department and Research environment   

The Faculty of Education and Society offers professional education programmes in the fields of education, culture, leisure, and sport. The faculty houses one of Sweden’s largest teacher education programmes, where students choose one of four professional qualifications: preschool teacher, primary school teacher, subject teacher, or vocational teacher. In addition to programmes leading to qualifications as sports scientists, historians, teachers, special educational needs coordinators, special education teachers, and career guidance counsellors, the faculty offers Master’s and doctoral programmes, as well as stand-alone courses, continuing professional development, and commissioned education. The faculty is characterized by innovation in the design and collaboration of our education programmes with schools, municipalities, organizations, and industry. Our research is conducted in close cooperation with the wider community. We are based in the Orkanen and Scylla buildings at Hjälmarekajen, next to Malmö Central Station.

The Department of Society, Culture and Identity (SKI) is a multidisciplinary environment that conducts a range of education programmes as well as research activities within the humanities and social sciences. History is a particularly strong research area within the department, which offers doctoral education in History and History Didactics. Alongside this, there are research groups in Religious Studies, Sociology, and Work and the Labour Market.

SKI maintains a Master’s Programme in History, a Bachelor’s Programme in History with a specialization in Cultural Heritage Studies, several specializations within teacher education, a one-year Master’s Programme in Work Science, and a Bachelor’s Programme in Study and Career Guidance. In addition, the department offers a range of stand-alone courses, including courses in History, Montessori Education, and Religious Studies.

Through its various educational programmes and several ongoing research projects, the department maintains extensive collaboration with, among others, schools and heritage institutions. SKI also collaborates with the Swedish National Agency for Education in the development of national history examinations and in the provision of various commissioned education programmes.

Application   

You apply for this position via Malmö University's recruitment system by clicking on the "Apply" button. As an applicant, you are responsible for ensuring that your application is completed in accordance with the job advertisement, and that it is submitted to the University no later than 2027-01-11. The application must be written in Swedish, English or any of the Nordic languages. As an applicant, you are responsible for the application and its appendices being translated.   

The application must include:

  • A brief research plan presenting the focus of research and a thesis concept, and how this relates to the specific post (max 4 pages). The research plan must contain an overall purpose, questions that the project intends to answer, an account of the methodological approach, a description of material collection and type of research material and an account of the theoretical framework 
  • Independent work at advanced level (including master thesis or equivalent) 

Miscellaneous   

Preparation of admission to postgraduate education and employment as a doctoral student take place in parallel. Only those who are or have been admitted to doctoral level courses and study programmes at a higher education may be appointed to doctoral studentships (HEO Chapter 5, section 3).

The doctoral studentship is a fixed-term position comprising four years of full-time studies, in accordance with the HEO Chapter 5, section 7. A doctoral student shall be employed for an indefinite period but for no longer than until a specified date, and never for longer than a year after the doctoral degree or artistic doctoral degree has been completed. The first appointment must be limited to one year at the most. The appointment can be extended by a maximum of two years at a time.

Malmö University actively promotes gender equality and equal opportunities in order to offer a workplace and a university characterised by an open and inclusive approach.  

As part of this:

  • Applicants of an underrepresented gender are given priority for admission, if they are equally able to benefit from the programme.
  • Doctoral students with permanent disabilities are given the opportunity to receive support and adaptations during their studies, so that everyone can study on equal terms in a good study environment.

Employees who do not speak Swedish should learn Swedish in the long term so that they can participate in the daily and ongoing work of the institution or department. 

Malmö University applies salary setting for doctoral students in accordance with a local agreement on salary setting for doctoral students.

If the admitted person requires a residence permit to live in Sweden and pursue their studies, the University reserves the right to revoke the admission decision if the admitted person cannot present a valid residence permit as required on the date they are due to commence their education.

jobs.description_html: ID: 26.198 Pre-Doctoral Researcher (m/f/d) Leibniz ScienceCampus Europe and America in the Modern World The Leibniz ScienceCampus Europe and America in the Modern World is a joint platform of the University (UR) and the Leibniz Institute for East and Southeast European Studies (IOS). jobs.description_html: The Department of Computer Science (Dialog Systems and Machine Learning) at Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf is seeking a PhD Student in Natural Language Processing (m/w/d) Job-ID: J000000684 Working hours: Full time Location: Düsseldorf Start date: 01.01.2027 Limited until: 31.12.2027 Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-L Organization: Mathematisch-Naturwissen­schaftliche Fakultät Job Category: science / research / teach Apply till: 02.12.2026 The Dialogue Systems and Machine Learning group at Heinrich Heine University investigates fundamental questions in human–computer interaction, at the intersection of Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning. Our research focuses on building intelligent dialogue systems that can learn, reason, adapt, and interact effectively with humans in dynamic and uncertain environments. We develop principled methods for dialogue modelling, representation learning, reinforcement learning, knowledge acquisition, and user simulation. Our mission is to advance the foundations of machine intelligence towards dialogue systems that are adaptive, trustworthy, and genuinely useful to people. Main tasks The goal of Prof. Milica Gasic' DFG project “Curriculum learning in natural language generation” is to develop a deeper understanding of how and why hallucinations arise in neural natural language generation models. Rather than treating hallucinations solely as an undesirable property of the final output, we investigate them as a phenomenon emerging from the interaction between data, learning objectives, representations, and the mechanisms by which models acquire and use knowledge. A central goal is to identify the conditions under which hallucinations emerge and, ultimately, develop principled approaches for reducing their magnitude and severity. The project will investigate learning mechanisms underlying reliable language generation, with particular emphasis on curriculum learning and learning from feedback, exploring approaches such as inverse reinforcement learning and their connection to Theory of Mind. Your Profile The candidate must hold or be close to obtaining a master’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Computational Linguistics or a related field. The master’s thesis must have been submitted by the time of application. Some exposure to Natural Language Processing or Machine Learning is desirable. Excellent programming skills are essential. The candidate should be fluent in English with good writing skills. Knowledge of German is not required, but a willingness to learn German is desirable. Our Offer The position comes with a salary representative in academia (EG 13 TV-L, starting at € 4,759.37; classification depends on prior professional experience). The position is initially a one-year fixed-term contract, with the option of extension based on satisfactory performance. There will be no teaching duties in the first year. It is a qualification position in the sense of the Act of Academic Fixed-Term Contract (Wissenschaftsvertragsgesetz-WissZeitVG), which is to promote the scientific qualification of the employee. The start date is negotiable, but the preferred start would be on 1st January 2027. Do you want to conduct basic research that can inform solutions for sustainable agriculture? Join our group (EDGE) at the University of Vienna as a PhD student within the MSCA Doctoral Network Agripolys and apply environmental analytical chemistry to investigate the enzymatic degradation of polymers in agricultural soils. 

Your personal sphere of influence:

Polymers are important for numerous agricultural applications. To avoid the accumulation of polymers in soils and other environmental systems, soil biodegradability is a key desired feature for many polymers. To inform the development of soil biodegradable polymers, a fundamental understanding of the activity and specificity of soil enzymes is needed. Rooted in environmental analytical chemistry (centered around high-resolution mass spectrometry), this project (Agripolys DC6) aims to decipher biodegradation pathways of several promising polymer classes and thereby shine light on the degradation potential of soil enzymes.

Our research group is part of the Centre for Microbiology and Environmental Systems Science (CeMESS) at the University of Vienna, Austria. We are dedicated to conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of (bio)chemistry, microbiology, and environmental science.
