jobs.description_html:
About

The Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) is looking for highly qualified candidates with Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees to apply for our PhD program. We offer fully funded PhD positions in Astronomy, Biology, Computer Science, Chemistry & Materials, Data Science & Scientific Computing, Earth Science, Mathematics, Neuroscience, and Physics in a world-class research environment on the outskirts of Vienna.

 n 2019, ISTA was ranked #3 in the world-wide Nature Index ranking (normalized). In 2018, ISTA was ranked within the top ten of Nature Index Rising Stars “Top 30 academic institutions under 30” list.

All students are offered 5-year contracts, they receive internationally competitive salaries, and full social security coverage. 

The application deadline is January 8, 2027 (15:00 CET) for a PhD program start date in September 2027.

APPLY NOW

Your tasks

-----------------------------------------------

Join our Virtual Student Open Day on November 18th!
 

The Virtual Student Open Day is a great opportunity to explore our programs and campus virtually, wherever you are located. The program includes a range of live sessions from the Graduate School Office, academics, and students.

You can find out about our PhD program, the ISTA research experience, support services, the ISTA campus and much more by attending one of the talks.

-----------------------------------------------

International and Diverse Scientific Community
Our scientists, from professors to postdocs to students, hail from all corners of the world, representing over 80 different nationalities, and build on research and degrees earned from the finest global scientific institutes and universities.

English-Speaking
We use English throughout the Institute as the language of instruction and communication.

Interdisciplinary
 Our Graduate Program is characterized by modern comprehensive training with a special interdisciplinary focus.

Cutting-Edge Research Training
Students work closely with outstanding faculty within small research groups and have access to first-rate facilities. Students spend the first year completing coursework and rotations before affiliating with a group.

This first phase of exploration allows students to ensure that the research topic, as well as the research group, are the best match for them before embarking on in-depth thesis research in the second phase.

Entry with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree
We welcome students with a Bachelor’s or a Master’s in science to apply for our PhD program.

Funding
All PhD students are offered 5-year contracts. All students making reasonable progress are fully funded until the time of their thesis defense.

ISTA relies on diverse funding sources to support all its researchers. Our Grant Office supports ISTA scientists who would like to apply for external funding. Students also receive financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops.

Careers
Our distinguished alumni have gone on to successful careers after their PhD studies at ISTA.

PhD students receive support through our mentorship and career development programs which focus on training in transferable skills for academia and beyond. Throughout their studies, PhD students are supported by Career Services, which provide career development advice and training.

We also provide xista, an in-house science venture that supports researchers in the commercial development and use of their research results.

-----------------------------------------------

Your profile

Skills/Qualifications

ISTA welcomes students with different academic backgrounds who can bring their skills and experiences to the scientific setting.

Students with a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Astronomy, Biology, Computer Science, Chemistry & Materials, Data Science & Scientific Computing, Earth Science, Mathematics, Neuroscience, and Physics are encouraged to apply.

 

Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion

ISTA cherishes diversity in personalities, backgrounds, experiences and thoughts among all our employees. Diversity creates a workplace that enables employees to gain new ideas and insights and that will take science into exciting new directions.  

ISTA is committed to equal opportunities and social equity, regardless of age, gender (identity), ethnicity, race, social/cultural background, creed, religion, sexual orientation, and physical/cognitive abilities. Please see our Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion web page for more information. 

 

WHAT ARE THE SELECTION CRITERIA?

The selection committee uses a collection of indicators to evaluate the applicant’s preparedness, motivation, and potential. The following will be considered:

Scientific Promise:

  • Undergraduate performance: overall, with a special focus on relevant field-specific courses
  • Reference letters provided by professors and senior scientists: one letter from industry is acceptable, but letters from an academic background are given priority. Referees are asked to address analytical capabilities, technical proficiency, ability to work independently and motivation/commitment
  • Statement of purpose: the applicant’s past research experience and motivation for applying to this particular PhD program: is it a good academic fit? Does the program contribute to the candidate’s future career plans?, etc.
  • Additional relevant skills (field-specific): demonstrated by internships and/or participation in research projects, participation in science Olympiads, programming languages, lab 

Your benefits

Background:

Quality of the undergraduate background
Transferable skills: communication skills, experience with working in teams, previous mobility and international experiences, leadership experience as demonstrated in student organizations, etc.
Diversity: e.g. a woman in computer science/math/physics; an applicant who switched fields, etc.
ISTA processes applications for its PhD program once a year. To apply, you have to create an online account, which will allow you to track your application through its various stages. 

Your application

WHAT APPLICATION MATERIALS ARE REQUIRED?

We ask you to upload the following documents to the application portal:

  • CV
  • Statement of purpose that explains your research experience and your motivation for applying to the ISTA PhD program. It should be 1-2 pages maximum. In your statement, specify up to three research groups you find the most interesting. At this stage you do not need to contact potential supervisors.
  • University transcripts and diplomas of all degree programs and all years you have attended and/or are currently enrolled in (in English and in original language).
  • Contact information of 3 referees
    All documents must be submitted in English. Copies of university transcripts must be in both English and in their original language.
  • The application deadline is January 8, 2027 (15:00 CET).

jobs.description_html:
The DIW Graduate Center (GC) at the German Institute for Economic Research welcomes applications from highly qualified students from around the world to enroll in its structured doctoral program in Economics.

The goal of the DIW Graduate Center is to provide outstanding doctoral students with a research environment and a training structure that will allow their talents to fully develop. The program equips them with a deep understanding of economic and social processes while offering them the opportunity to apply their knowledge at the largest economic research institute in Germany.

We are looking for Doctoral Students for the DIW Graduate Center PhD Program in Economics The DIW Graduate Center offers a five-year program of in-depth training in Economics leading to a PhD from one of Berlin’s universities. Students will complete a rigorous coursework curriculum and receive on-the-job training in DIW Berlin’s research departments. Students' research may be theoretical or applied in nature. Most work at the GC, however, has a strong empirical component. The program also encourages funded internships at prestigious institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and government ministries, as well as research stays at renowned universities around the world.

The DIW Graduate Center offers five years of funding with a standard stipend of 1,650 euros per month in the first year and a work contract in subsequent years. After completing the first year, doctoral students will join one of the research departments at the institute.

Requirements: Applicants to our PhD program must hold a master’s degree or diploma in Economics. Applications may also be submitted while the degree is still in progress, provided it is completed before the program starts. Degrees from other related fields (such as statistics, quantitative social sciences, mathematics or engineering) may also fulfill requirements for the program if the applicant has a sufficient background in Economics.

Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency unless they hold a degree from a university in an English-speaking country or can document at least one year of studies in an English-speaking degree program. A high score on the TOEFL or IELTS test is considered sufficient evidence of English proficiency. Knowledge of German is not required for a successful application, but students are encouraged to learn German and improve their language skills over the course of the program

Application and Information: We value diversity and therefore welcome all applications—regardless of gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic and social background.

Please apply only online through our application portal by January 15, 2027, quoting the reference number GC-1-26-Stip-e and include the following application documents:

  • Motivation letter (max. 2 pages) explaining your reasons for applying and briefly outlining your major research interests;
  • Detailed curriculum vitae (without photograph);
  • Two academic letters of recommendation, to be submitted directly by senior academics (e.g., professors, postdoctoral researchers) via our application site;
  • Copies of academic transcripts and other certificates;
  • Completed application form (can be found on our application site);
  • IELTS or TOEFL scores, if applicable;
  • GRE General Test – Test Taker Score Report (PDF), if applicable. Please also attach your GRE Test if you have already submitted it to the Institutional Account.
You can access the application portal via our GC website under application site.

Please note that only applications submitted through the application portal will be considered and that the application is to be completed in English.

Do you have any questions about this call for applications or the online application? You may find your question already answered on our GC website, particularly in the FAQ section of the application site — please take a look before contacting us.

If you still have questions after reviewing our GC website, please contact gradcenter@diw.de for content-related inquiries and recruiting@diw.de for technical questions regarding the online application.

Founded in 1925, DIW Berlin (the German Institute for Economic Research) is one of the leading economic research institutes in Germany. The Institute analyzes the economic and social aspects of topical issues, formulating and disseminating policy advice based on its research findings. DIW Berlin is part of both the national and international scientific communities, provides research infrastructure to academics all over the world, and promotes the next generation of scientists. A member of the Leibniz Association, DIW Berlin is independent and primarily publicly funded.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in organometallic chemistry

jobs.description_html:
Description of the research environment

We are seeking a doctoral student in organometallic chemistry at the Department of Chemistry, Lund University. Ola Wendt’s research group is part of the Centre for Analysis and Synthesis (CAS), an established research environment with expertise in organic, inorganic and organometallic chemistry. The group conducts research in transition-metal organometallic chemistry, with particular emphasis on reaction mechanisms. Its focus is on pincer complexes of the late transition metals and their applications in carbon dioxide activation and hydrogen-transfer reactions.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed by Lund University.

Doctoral studies train you to adopt a scientific approach. In brief, this involves developing critical and analytical thinking, learning to solve problems independently by choosing appropriate methods, and developing an awareness of research ethics. This training takes place primarily through work on a research project, but also includes courses. You will receive guidance from your advisor throughout your studies. If successful, doctoral studies conclude with a thesis and the award of a doctoral degree.

Mer om att vara doktorand vid den naturvetenskapliga fakulteten på naturvetenskap.se. Read more about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se.

Subject and project description

The project aims to develop transition-metal complexes that can be used in homogeneous catalysis. Activation of small molecules and strong chemical bonds are central themes in the research group. One area of particular interest is dehydrogenation reactions, for example in the context of hydrogen storage using so-called liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs).

Within this research, we also seek to understand the chemistry and reactivity of metal hydrides.

We use specialised synthetic techniques, including high-vacuum and Schlenk techniques and glovebox work under an inert atmosphere. Structural characterisation is carried out mainly using multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. In our research, we aim to understand reaction mechanisms in as much detail as possible, including through kinetic measurements and spectroscopic identification of reaction intermediates. Organic synthesis is also an important part of our work, as we prepare the ligands used in our metal complexes ourselves.

The project is suitable for someone interested in synthesis, keen to learn how to handle air- and moisture-sensitive compounds under an inert atmosphere, and interested in investigating reaction mechanisms using, for example, kinetic studies, NMR spectroscopy or other experimental techniques.

The project offers considerable freedom to explore new ideas and to take the research in the directions suggested by our findings.

Duties

You will primarily devote your time to doctoral studies, the main component of which is writing a doctoral thesis.

Your main duty is to conduct research within the doctoral project and complete your doctoral education.

You are also expected to participate in doctoral courses, research seminars, scientific conferences and research collaborations.

In addition to your studies, a maximum of 20% of your working time may be devoted to teaching and other departmental duties.

Qualifications

To be admitted and employed as a doctoral student, you must meet the requirements below.

Entry requirements

You meet the general entry requirements for third-cycle studies if you have:

  • been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • completed courses comprising at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits were awarded at second-cycle level, or
  • acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The specific entry requirements for chemistry are met by applicants who have:

  • In order to benefit from the programme, applicants are required to have completed first or second-cycle courses worth at least 120 credits in the relevant subject. Relevance is defined by the research specialisation of the project, which generally means chemistry courses, but may also refer to courses with a significant element of, for example, molecular sciences, mathematics, life sciences, materials science or physics. In addition, documented proficiency in spoken and written English is required, sufficient to enable the third-cycle student to participate actively in the research environment, comprehend scientific literature, and present and communicate research findings in an international context. This requirement essentially corresponds to a language level comparable to CEFR level B2 and is deemed to have been met by passing English 6 (English B/English Level 2), or by other documented evidence demonstrating equivalent proficiency in English, such as an internationally recognised language test (e.g. IELTS Academic overall score of at least 6.0). The specific entry requirements can also be fulfilled through an equivalent programme. This is assessed on a case-by-case basis.

Other requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Very good command of English, both spoken and written
  • Good ability to cooperate
  • A strong background in synthetic and mechanistic chemistry
  • A Master’s degree in organic, inorganic or organometallic chemistry (required upon admission; the degree may still be in progress at the time of application)

Selection criteria

Selection among eligible applicants will be based on their ability to benefit from doctoral studies, assessed according to the following criteria:

  1. Knowledge and skills relevant to the thesis work and the subject of study.
  2. Assessed ability to work independently and to formulate and address scientific problems.
  3. Ability to communicate in writing and orally.
  4. Other experience relevant to third-cycle studies, such as professional experience.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority, which means that you will receive special benefits, generous annual leave and a favourable occupational pension.

Mer om att jobba på Lunds universitet på lu.se.Read more about working at Lund University at lu.se. https://www.lu.se/om-universitetet/jobba-hos-oss

Terms of employment

This is a full-time, fixed-term position starting on 1 March 2027 or as agreed. Doctoral studies at the Faculty of Science take four years of full-time study. The period of employment is extended correspondingly if teaching or other departmental duties are undertaken. Regulations governing employment as a doctoral student are set out in Chapter 5, Sections 1–7 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100).

Mer om anställningsvillkor för doktorander på Lunds universitets medarbetarwebb. Read more about the terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staff Pages. https://www.medarbetarwebben.lu.se/forska-och-utbilda/stod-till-forskning/utbildning-pa-forskarniva/anstallningsvillkor-doktorander

How to apply

Your application must be written in English and include:

  • a curriculum vitae (CV), including a list of publications, if applicable
  • a letter of motivation (1–2 pages) explaining why you are interested in the position and how the research project matches your interests and educational background
  • copies of degree certificates and transcripts of records demonstrating that you meet the general and specific entry requirements for doctoral studies and have the subject knowledge required for the project
  • a brief summary of previous research experience (e.g. degree project, 1–2 pages, 12-point Palatino)
  • contact details for two academic or professional referees

jobs.title: Doctoral student in chemistry
jobs.department: Lund University
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Department of Chemistry at Lund University does research and education across all chemistry disciplines at both the Faculty of Science and the Faculty of Engineering, LTH. It is located at the Center for Chemistry and Chemical Engineering and has about 300 employees, of whom about 150 are post graduate students. The number of full-time students enrolled in undergraduate studies is almost 500.

The Department of Chemistry aims to create and maintain a supportive research environment which increases chances of success in current and future research, as well as creating a safe and inclusive work environment where we all respect each other.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. https://www.lth.se/english/study-at-lth/phd-studies/

Subject and project description

The advertised position is part of the EU-financed MSCA doctoral network LLIMIT, a European doctoral training network dedicated to advancing immunomodulatory glycoscience. The consortium unites seven academic institutions in Slovenia, France, Italy, Germany and Sweden with accredited PhD programs in organic and medicinal chemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, immunology and pharmacology, each with strong expertise in glycoscience. They are joined by seven non-academic partners and a graduate and research academy, ensuring comprehensive, cross-sector training that spans fundamental science, translational research, and entrepreneurship.

The LLIMIT network will train 14 doctoral candidates in a joint, research-based program supported by expert supervision and specialized training events, advancing innovative research on immune lectins and carbohydrate ligands, covering the full early drug discovery pipeline from target identification and validation, through advanced glycochemistry and drug design, to hit and lead discovery. The specific project is entitled “Design and synthesis galectin-9 inhibitors”. The doctoral candidate (DC4) will undertake PhD studies at Lund University under the supervision by Profs. Ulf Nilsson, Derek Logan. External suervisors will be Prof. Marko Anderluh (University of Ljubljana, Slovenia) and Dr Björn Borgström (RG Discovery AB, Lund, Sweden).

The research project is to design, synthesize, and evaluate in biochemical and biological assays new lectin inhibitors possessing high-affinity, selectivity, oral availability, and optimized PK-ADMET properties. Knowledge-based design based on published structures, as well as de novo design, will be the basis for selecting synthetic target molecules.

The selected candidate will participate in the network’s training activities and work placements in the laboratories of the participating academic and industrial teams. Regular meetings and workshops within the EU-funded Llimit Network will complement the training and support provided by the host institutions.

The doctoral student be performing her/his PhD thesis work at the Department of Chemistry of Lund University, Sweden under the supervision of Professor Ulf Nilsson and Derek Logan.

Work duties

You will devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Chemistry if the applicant has:

  • The specific entry requirement of 120 credits (courses, or a combination of courses and degree project) is defined by the research orientation of the project. This typically means courses in chemistry, but may also include courses with substantial content in, for example, molecular sciences, mathematics, life sciences, materials science, or physics. The specific qualification may also have been obtained through other equivalent education, which is assessed on a case-by-case basis.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • completed their M.Sc. or equivalent and have not acquired, since, more than 4 years (full-time equivalent) research experience.
  • passed a course in advanced theoretical organic chemistry (or equivalent)
  • passed a course in advanced practical organic chemistry (or equivalent)
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems
  • good written and oral communication skills
  • good ability to cooperate
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written

At the time of recruitment, the successful candidate must not have been awarded the doctorate degree and must not have resided, nor carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the first day of employment.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications:

  • practical experience of carbohydrate chemistry
  • practical experience of medicinal chemistry
  • practical experience of studying carbohydrate-protein interactions
  • practical experience of analytical methods (LCMS, NMR, HPLC, IR)
  • letters of recommendation from relevant persons/institutions
  • international experience (studying, internship or research work abroad for a period of at least 1 month)

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. https://www.lunduniversity.lu.se/about-university/work-lund-university

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting as agreed. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

How to apply

Recruited researchers: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/wp-call/2026-2027/wp-2-marie-sklodowska-curie-actions_horizon-2026-2027_en.pdf). The applicant must submit the application through the Lund University portal https://lu.varbi.com before 15th January 2027, clearly indicating in the subject “Application for DC4 position”.

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project.
  • References (at least three)

  • Answers to the question appended below
  • A critical summary of a research article (10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5c03703); verification of candidate skills in terms of understanding and analyzing science, understanding and writing in English language. The summary should be of maximum 2500 characters length, one figure, and fully referenced.

We welcome your application.

About the subject

English Language and Linguistics is concerned with research on the English language and its many varieties, primarily with regard to semantics, syntax, text and discourse analysis, language policy, language acquisition, language teaching and testing methods. Some types of research are comparative and therefore involve other languages. 

About the education

Information about doctoral studies in English Language and Linguistics can be found at https://www.sol.lu.se/en/engelska/ interested-in-phd-studies/. Information about doctoral studies at the Joint Faculties of Humanities and Theology can be found at https://www.ht.lu.se/en/education/doctoral-studies/.

The education is carried out in Lund.

Work assignments

Doctoral studies. Departmental work, such as teaching and administrative tasks, can be assigned. The maximum amount of such work is 20 %.

Entry requirements

Eligibility for admission to doctoral studies in English Language and Linguistics is set out in the general syllabus for the subject, available at https://www.ht.lu.se/en/education/doctoral-studies/general-syllabi/. 

Assessment criteria

The selection process will primarily take into account the applicants’ ability to benefit from doctoral studies. This is assessed against the criteria quality, quantity, progression and relevance.

We welcome applications from candidates whose research interests align with the subject’s current areas of expertise (see https://www.sol.lu.se/en/engelska/research/) and who have the relevant theoretical and methodological background to undertake doctoral research in one or more of these fields. In the current round of applications, we particularly welcome candidates whose background and proposed doctoral project fall within one or more of the following areas and address questions relating to the English language:

Applied Linguistics: We welcome proposals on English as a foreign/second language, its acquisition and use; lexical processing and the multilingual mental lexicon; language testing and assessment, and the psychology of language learning and teaching. We also welcome research on language teacher education, as well as research on language planning and policy, English-medium instruction (EMI), and content and language integrated learning (CLIL). We encourage innovative projects that combine or draw on a range of methodological approaches, whether quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods.

Cognitive Linguistics and Multilingual Cognition, including research on language-cognition interactions in a variety of domains, including motion, time, aspect, gender, number, and colour, as well as research on conceptual transfer/restructuring, decision-making, and broader cognitive functions in multilingual individuals, societies, and real-life settings. Projects that engage in comparisons between speakers of English and other languages, different varieties of English, and multilingual settings where English is one of the languages spoken are welcome.

Corpus Linguistics, including corpus-based approaches to English language variation and use, for example in sociolinguistics, stance and evaluation, and discourse-pragmatic phenomena. We also welcome research on language in digital and social contexts, as well as studies integrating corpus data with experimental or other empirical methods. Projects with a comparative or cross-linguistic dimension, in which English constitutes a central component, are also of interest.

Neurolinguistics, particularly sentence processing from syntactic, semantic or pragmatic perspectives, using EEG.

jobs.department: Lund University, Department of Philosophy, HT
jobs.description_html:
About the subject

Cognitive Science is an interdisciplinary subject dealing with different aspects of cognition in biological and artificial systems. Among the phenomena studied are perception, memory, learning, language, thought and problem-solving. Central disciplines involved are psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, philosophy and computer science. 

About the education

The project Irony Re-examined in Interactive Settings (IRIS) seeks to bring about a paradigm shift in the experimental study of pragmatics by studying diﬀerences in comprehension between addressees and overhearers, focusing on irony as a test case. The main hypothesis of the project is that addressees and overhearers use diﬀerent comprehension strategies when understanding irony, with repercussions for irony processing, the development of irony comprehension, and how comprehenders hold ironic speakers accountable for the meanings that they convey. IRIS will develop a novel experimental paradigm that studies both addressees and overhearers, combining accuracy and rating-scales measures with recent technical advances in cognitive pupillometry.

Within the project, the doctoral student will write a dissertation on how differences in conversational roles (i.e., addressees and overhearers) impact how speakers are held accountable for the ironic and literal meanings that they communicate. The dissertation will be based on the results of experimental studies that the student will be expected to conduct.

IRIS is a project funded by an ERC starting grant awarded to Camilo Rodríguez Ronderos.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Computer Science – human-centred monitoring of autonomous AI-enabled systems
jobs.department: Lund University, LTH, Department of Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
About the workplace

The position is placed in the Software Engineering (SE) division at the Department of Computer Science. The division conducts empirical research on how software-intensive systems are developed, verified and evolved in practice, in close collaboration with industry. The division has a long tradition of research on quality assurance, testing, requirements engineering and continuous software engineering.

As a doctoral student in the project, you will become part of an active doctoral environment where several ongoing thesis projects address related questions, including AI-driven DevOps, AI alignment through continuous operational testing, and software engineering for software-defined vehicles. The project is carried out in collaboration with Blekinge Institute of Technology (BTH) and with industrial partners.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you are trained in a scientific approach. In brief, this means that you practise thinking critically and analytically, solving problems independently using appropriate methods, and developing an awareness of research ethics. You will also have the opportunity to work on projects and to develop your leadership and teaching skills. Throughout your studies, you are guided by supervisors. The doctoral studies conclude with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH at lth.se.

Subject and project description

The research subject is Computer Science. The position focuses on software engineering and is part of a research project funded within the strategic research environment ELLIIT and carried out by Lund University together with Blekinge Institute of Technology.

Modern autonomous and AI-enabled systems, such as driver-assistance systems in vehicles, industrial robots or AI agents in software services, are continuously updated through DevOps practices and feedback from use in the field. Each update may be correct and comply with requirements and standards, yet over time the system’s behaviour may gradually drift away from what users and other stakeholders intend and expect. This is called alignment drift. The project investigates how alignment drift can be characterised, how it can be detected through indicators in operational data (e.g. telemetry, test outcomes and customer feedback), and how humans can interpret and act on these signals within existing CI/CD workflows.

The project is empirical and design-oriented. It develops and evaluates support for how alignment drift can be characterised, detected and managed in industrial practice. You will work with retrospective case studies, analysis of data from issue trackers and logs, interviews and observations with engineers, and longitudinal action research in industry. The focus is on software engineering and on the interplay between people, processes and data – not on developing new machine-learning models or autonomous functions.

Work duties

Your main duty will be your doctoral studies, which include participation in research projects as well as doctoral courses, seminars and conferences.

You will drive the project’s research, from characterising alignment drift to evaluating new practices in industrial settings. The work is carried out in close collaboration with supervisors at Lund University and BTH and with industrial partners. The position involves some travel, e.g. to BTH in Karlskrona, industrial partners and conferences.

The duties include:

  • planning and conducting empirical studies, e.g. retrospective case studies, interview studies, and analysis of data from issue trackers, logs and test results
  • developing and evaluating support for how alignment drift can be characterised, detected and managed, in collaboration with engineers in industry
  • writing scientific papers and presenting results at international conferences and to industrial partners
  • participating in doctoral courses and seminars.
  • The duties may also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20 % of working hours).

Qualifications

To be admitted and employed as a doctoral student, you need to meet the requirements below.

Admission requirements

You meet the general admission requirements for third-cycle studies if you have:

  • been awarded a second-cycle qualification or
  • satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

You meet the specific admission requirements for doctoral studies in Computer Science if you have:

  • at least 60 credits at second-cycle level relevant to the subject area, or
  • a Master of Science in Engineering in computer engineering, electrical engineering, information and communication technology, engineering physics, or engineering mathematics.

Finally, the student must be judged to have the ability required to complete the programme.

Additional requirements

To benefit from the doctoral programme in question, the following is also required:

  • in-depth knowledge of software engineering corresponding to at least 30 credits of courses in the field, e.g. requirements engineering, testing and verification, software processes, DevOps or software architecture
  • good knowledge of programming and data analysis, corresponding to the ability to analyse large amounts of data from software development and operation and to build simple prototypes
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle scientific problems
  • the ability to plan and drive the work forward on your own, across several parallel studies, and to adapt plans when conditions change, e.g. access to data and industrial cases
  • good written and oral communication skills, including with professionals outside academia
  • good collaboration skills
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written

Other qualifications

The following is considered meritorious for this doctoral programme:

  • knowledge in one or more of the following areas: continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD), DevOps or MLOps, requirements engineering and traceability, testing of AI-based systems, machine learning, and autonomous systems, e.g. in vehicles, robotics or AI agents
  • a second-cycle course in research methodology or empirical methods, e.g. case studies, interview studies, qualitative data analysis, surveys or mining software repositories
  • a degree project with an empirical focus, preferably in collaboration with industry, where the quality of the degree project is assessed based on the attached work
  • professional experience of software development, especially in environments with continuous integration and delivery
  • good academic results in courses in software engineering and computer science.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority, which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous pension scheme. You will work in a research environment with close industrial collaboration, with supervision from both Lund University and Blekinge Institute of Technology and the opportunity to build a network within ELLIIT.

Read more about working at Lund University at lu.se. 

Terms of employment

The employment is a fixed-term, full-time position, starting by agreement. Doctoral studies comprise four years of full-time study. If the position includes teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Regulations on employment as a doctoral student are found in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1–7.

Read more about employment conditions for doctoral students on Lund University’s staff pages. 

Other information

Selection takes place in several stages and includes interviews, a work sample and reference checks. Interviews are planned for December 2026 and January 2027.

How to apply

Applications must be written in English and must include:

  • CV (maximum two pages) starting with your education. State your degrees, relevant courses, the title of your degree project, any professional experience, and any publications and links to examples of your own code or reports.
  • Cover letter (maximum one page) structured under the following four headings:
    • Motivation: why you are applying for this particular position and how the project matches your interests.
    • Educational background: which courses and which degree project are most relevant to the project, and why.
    • Methodological experience: concrete examples of empirical studies or data analyses you have conducted and what your role was.
    • Reflection (maximum 150 words): How could one detect that a continuously updated software system is gradually starting to behave in ways that deviate from what its users and other stakeholders expect?
  • Transcript of records with a list of courses, and degree certificate or a statement of expected graduation. The transcript must show the grade for each course and the grading scale used. These must demonstrate that you meet the general and specific admission requirements and have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral project.
  • Degree project at second-cycle level (or equivalent independent work). If it is not yet completed, attach a summary and a description of its current status.
  • Anything else you wish to refer to, e.g. letters of recommendation or contact details of referees.

Please also answer the selection questions in the recruitment system. It is important that all documents are attached, as they form the basis for the assessment of eligibility and qualifications.

Welcome to apply!

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Physics with focus on attosecond Physics
jobs.department: Lund University,Technical Faculty, Physics Department
jobs.description_html:
The research at the Division of Atomic Physics is centered on different applications of optics and lasers, including atomic and molecular physics with ultrashort light pulses, high-intensity laser-plasma physics, quantum information, and biophotonics. The Division operates the High-Power Laser Facility, including several advanced femtosecond laser systems and collaborate with several free electron laser facilities. It is a central part of a major interdisciplinary research environment within the Lund University, the Lund Laser Centre, LLC. The division is also heavily involved in undergraduate education, especially within the Photonics programme.

Work duties

At the division, research is performed on the generation and application of extremely short light pulses, in the attosecond and extreme ultraviolet range. The activities span from ultrafast laser technology and extreme nonlinear optics to studies of the electron dynamics in atoms and molecules as well as more complex systems using attosecond light pulses. The division of Atomic Physics is now looking for one PhD student for the project described below.

The project is funded through a Marie Sklodowska-Curie doctoral network:

Quantum information science and ultrafast nonlinear control at the attosecond timescale – QU-ATTO

This means that the positions come with some additional constraints and possibilities. The candidates recruited for these positions cannot have worked in Sweden for the last 5 years to be eligible. The positions come with a training network in Europe together with 15 PhD students in different countries.

The project focuses on using a technique for the tomographic reconstruction of entangled states in photoionization. The goal is to improve the technique that has been developed in Lund for the reconstruction of the density matrix of photoelectron originating from the absorption of ultrashort XUV pulses by atoms and molecules.

The main duties of doctoral students are to devote themselves to their research studies which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20%).

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if he or she:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle studies in Physics if he or she has:

  • at least 30 second-cycle credits of relevance to the subject, of which at least 15 credits shall comprise a second-cycle degree project, or
  • an MSc in engineering physics or an associated field, or a Master’s degree in physics or an associated field.

 Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually. In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Physics may be considered for admission.

Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme.

Additional requirements:

  • Very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • The student should have a background in optics/photonics and/or atomic physics/quantum mechanics.

Other assessment criteria

Experience in some of the following areas is a qualification for all the projects:

  • Femtosecond lasers and ultrafast optics
  • Quantum optics
  • High-order harmonic generation and attosecond physics
  • Photoelectron and photoion spectroscopy
  • Data analysis, vacuum technique, and mechanical design

Basis of assessment

Selection to postgraduate studies is based on the expected ability to perform well in the studies. The evaluation of the ability to perform well is based primarily on the results of studies at the basic and advanced levels, in particular:

  1. Knowledge and skills relevant to the thesis project and the subject of the study.
  2. An assessment of ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  3. Written and oral communication skills
  4. Other experience relevant to postgraduate studies, such as professional experience.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

Terms of employment

Only those admitted to third cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral studentship. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. A doctoral studentship is a fixed-term employment of a maximum of 5 years (including 20% departmental duties). jobs.title: Doctoral student in computer science with focus on program transformation
jobs.department: Lund University, LTH, Department of Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The position is within the Software Development and Environments division, part of the Department of Computer Science.  The division is exploring novel tools, languages, and methods for supporting software development, and conducts research in a variety of topics that include refactoring, program analysis, compiler construction, declarative specification languages, distributed development environments, and automatic program repair. Its research involves strong collaborations both locally within Lund University, internationally with other universities, and with industrial partners, such as ABB and Ericsson, including research driven by industrial PhD students. The division currently has twelve members, and regularly organises group activities to foster a positive working environment.

The division is actively developing the JastAdd metacompilation framework, which is the foundation for several compilers and software tools, including the division's ExtendJ extensible Java compiler and the static analysis tools IntraJ and MetaDL.

More about the Software Development and Environments group (sde.cs.lth.se/)
More about JastAdd (jastadd.cs.lth.se/web/)
More about ExtendJ (extendj.org)
More about MetaDL (github.com/lu-cs-sde/metadl)

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will learn to approach questions and challenges scientifically. In short, this means that you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

This research project aims to develop novel tools and techniques that enforce rigid guard-rails during software refactoring and other forms of software evolution. We assume an unreliable source of program transformations, such as a human developer or a large language model.  The guard-rail mechanism will then inspect, steer, and augment any sequence of program transformations to detect and recover from unintended behavioural change.
The position is funded by the Excellence Center at Linköping – Lund in Information Technology (ELLIIT), and it is a collaboration with the Natural Language Processing group at Linköping University, part of the division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems.

More about ELLIIT (elliit.se)
More about the Division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems at Linköping University (liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida/aiics)

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The work duties include:

  • Research on automatic program analysis and program transformation applied to preventing unintended behavioural change during refactoring and similar program evolution tasks. You will work towards exploring approaches that can aid real-world software evolution, and examine qualitative aspects of these approaches.
  • Applying appropriate research methods: depending on the trajectory of this research, different and possibly novel methodologies may be required to provide robust answers to the underlying research questions. You will learn, apply, and possibly support the development of suitable methods.
  • Artefact-oriented activity: You will develop software tools, algorithms, and other software components. These should be evaluated in realistic scenarios and integrated with, as well as shared within, the project team.
  • Presentation and collaboration: You will present your research findings at the annual ELLIIT workshop in southern Sweden and discuss your work at meetings with academic project partners, including personal meetings with our collaboration partners in Linköping.
  • Interaction with the industry: You will have opportunities to discuss your work and collaborate with industrial researchers, especially in Lund.
  • The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (limited to a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in computer science if the applicant has:

  • at least 60 second-cycle credits at an advanced level with relevance for the research topic, or
  • an MSc in Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Information and Communication Technology, Engineering Physics or Engineering Mathematics.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Knowledge or experience in at least one of the following areas (demonstrated e.g. in the form of a university course, or through professional experiences or contributions to relevant open source projects):
    • o compiler construction, or
    • o the foundations of static program analysis.
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  • good written and oral communication skills.
  • good ability to cooperate.
  • very good knowledge of English, in speech and writing.
  • very good programming experience (demonstrated e.g. in the form of professional experiences, contributions to open source projects, or outstanding results in university courses).
  • persistence and the ability to plan and structure your own work
  • curiosity and willingness to learn and adopt new techniques, especially within the cross-disciplinary scope of the project

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, it is advantageous if you can demonstrate experience or knowledge in one or more of the following subjects:

  • developing automatic program transformation tools, such as
    • o refactoring tools, or
    • o meta-programming tools.
  • software development in teams, especially in the context of:
    • o professional software engineering,
    • o open source projects, or
    • o legacy software engineering projects.
  • dynamic program analysis.
  • programming in Java.
  • functional or declarative programming (logic programming, reference attribute grammars etc.).
  • natural language processing, machine learning, and/or applying large language models, such as
    • o working with the underlying machine learning techniques, such as latent/embedding spaces, representation learning, or transformers,
    • o training or fine-tuning such models, or
    • o applying them to software development / software engineering tasks.
  • systematic evaluation of software systems and relevant statistical methods.
  • systems programming.
  • areas of discrete mathematics with relation to program analysis (lattice theory, type theory, Galois connections etc.).

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.  This project additionally offers collaboration opportunities with Linköping University via its joint supervision structure, and industrial outreach opportunities via ELLIIT, such as the annual ELLIIT workshop.

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, with intended start date in the spring of 2027 or according to agreement, but no later than 2027-12-31. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Numerical simulations of turbulent heat transfer over rough surfaces
jobs.department: Lund University, Faculty of Engineering, LTH, Department of Energy Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The doctoral student will be employed at the Department of Energy Sciences, Faculty of Engineering (LTH), Lund University, and will be part of the Division of Heat Transfer. The research environment conducts research in fluid mechanics, heat transfer and computational fluid dynamics, with particular emphasis on the numerical modelling and simulation of turbulent flows and engineering applications.

The doctoral student will work in a research environment combining fundamental research with applications of direct relevance to industry. The project will be carried out in close collaboration with Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB and RISE. This provides an opportunity to work at the interface between fundamental research, advanced numerical methods and industrially relevant problems.

The doctoral student will have access to expertise in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), turbulence, heat transfer, numerical methods and high-performance computing. The work will involve extensive use of high-performance computing resources, including both GPU- and CPU-based computing platforms.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

Surface roughness has a significant influence on turbulent flow, wall friction and heat transfer in many engineering systems. Understanding and predicting these effects is important in a wide range of applications, including energy systems, thermal management and transport applications. Despite its practical importance, accurately predicting turbulent heat transfer over realistic rough surfaces remains challenging, particularly when the properties of the working fluid and the relative thicknesses of the momentum and thermal boundary layers vary.

The aim of this doctoral project is to develop a deeper physical understanding of the interaction between surface roughness, turbulence and heat transfer, and to translate this understanding into improved engineering models.

The research will primarily use high-fidelity numerical simulations, including Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) and Large Eddy Simulation (LES). Different CFD codes will be employed depending on the problem and required level of fidelity, including OpenFOAM, CaNS and nekRS. The simulations will make extensive use of modern high-performance computing resources based on both GPUs and CPUs.

The project will investigate how surface roughness influences turbulent flow and heat transfer for different fluids and thermal conditions. Particular attention will be given to the interaction between roughness geometry, turbulent structures, and the momentum and thermal boundary layers, including conditions in which the relative thicknesses of the thermal and momentum boundary layers differ.

The high-fidelity simulation data will be used to identify relevant physical mechanisms and scaling relations and to support the development of reduced-order and engineering models for rough-surface heat transfer, including improved models and correlations suitable for Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) simulations.

The overall objective is to establish a connection between fundamental turbulence physics, high-fidelity numerical simulations and computational models that can be applied to engineering design.

The project will be conducted in close collaboration with Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB and RISE, providing opportunities for scientific exchange and interaction with researchers and engineers working on industrial applications of turbulent flow and heat transfer.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral studies, which include participation in research projects as well as third-cycle courses, seminars and scientific conferences.

A central part of your work will be to perform and analyse high-fidelity numerical simulations of turbulent flow and heat transfer over rough surfaces. You will use CFD and high-performance computing frameworks, which may include OpenFOAM, CaNS and nekRS, on CPU- and GPU-based systems. Applicants should already have experience with comparable simulation tools and High Performance Computing (HPC) systems; familiarity with the specific codes used in the project is an advantage.  

The work duties include:

  • Performing DNS and LES of turbulent flow and heat transfer over rough surfaces using OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS or comparable CFD and scientific-computing frameworks.
  • Setting up, running, validating and analysing simulations on GPU- and CPU-based high-performance computing systems.
  • Investigating the influence of surface roughness geometry and characteristics on turbulent momentum and heat transfer.
  • Investigating the effects of fluid properties and thermal conditions, including different relationships between momentum and thermal boundary-layer thicknesses.
  • Processing, analysing and visualising large datasets and identifying physical mechanisms and developing scaling relations from DNS and LES data.
  • Developing reduced-order models, correlations and improved RANS modelling approaches for turbulent heat transfer over rough surfaces.
  • Assessing and validating the developed models against high-fidelity numerical data and, where available, experimental data.
  • Collaborating with researchers at Lund University and with the project's industrial and research partners.
  • Presenting research results at project meetings, scientific conferences and international workshops.
  • Writing scientific articles for publication in international peer-reviewed journals and contributing to the doctoral thesis.

The work may involve travel within Sweden and internationally for project meetings, visits to research and industrial partners, conferences and research collaborations.

The duties may also include participation in teaching and other departmental work, however to a maximum of 20% of working hours.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • A Master’s degree, or equivalent qualification, in mechanical engineering, engineering physics, aerospace engineering, energy engineering, applied mathematics, computational science, or another subject relevant to the project.
  • Good knowledge of fluid mechanics, CFD, and turbulent flows, and relevant knowledge of heat transfer.
  • A substantial research project or thesis in CFD, turbulence, heat transfer, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently set up, run, troubleshoot, validate and analyse numerical simulations. This should be supported by research experience, rather than coursework alone.
  • Scientific programming experience in a relevant language, such as C/C++, Fortran and Python or Matlab.
  • Practical experience running computational simulations on HPC systems.
  • Ability to plan and carry out research tasks with limited day-to-day supervision, analyse results critically and communicate findings clearly.
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered meriting:

  • Experience with DNS or LES, wall-bounded turbulence, turbulent heat transfer, surface roughness or convective heat transfer.
  • Experience with a CFD or high-fidelity simulation framework, such as OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS or a comparable research code.
  • Experience with parallel computing or GPU-accelerated scientific computing.
  • Knowledge of RANS, wall modelling or thermal turbulence modelling.
  • Research experience beyond the Master’s thesis, such as work as a research assistant or research engineer.
  • Experience presenting or publishing research results or collaborating with industry.

Applicants are not expected to have experience with every code used in the project. However, they should have demonstrated the ability to carry out computational research independently using a comparable CFD or scientific-computing framework. They are expected to contribute from an early stage, building on existing experience in numerical simulation and HPC.

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. 

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting as soon as possible. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages.

Other

The doctoral student will be expected to interact regularly with the project's academic and industrial partners. The position may therefore include visits to partner organisations and participation in project meetings, workshops and conferences in Sweden and abroad.

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and cover letter stating why you are interested in the doctoral programme and this particular research project, and explaining how your educational background, research experience and interests relate to CFD, turbulence and heat transfer.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and demonstrate that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral research project.
  • Degree transcripts showing completed courses and grades.
  • A copy of the Master's thesis or, if the thesis has not yet been completed, a summary of the ongoing thesis work and its expected completion date.
  • Other documents you wish to be considered, such as scientific publications, technical reports, conference contributions, letters of recommendation or other material demonstrating relevant research experience.
  • Contact information for at least two references who may be contacted during the recruitment process.

We welcome your application.

Description of the workplace

The Planet Formation Group at the Department of Physics (Division of Astrophysics) at Lund University is seeking a PhD student to work on models of planet formation on a galactic scale. Research within the division encompasses galaxy formation, galactic dynamics and evolution, star formation and dynamics, stellar evolution, stellar spectroscopy and astrometry, planet formation and dynamics, as well as exoplanet atmospheres.

Work duties

We are seeking a PhD student in theoretical astrophysics. The PhD student will study how planets form at different times and in different regions of our galaxy. The PhD student will also calculate how certain planetesimals are ejected from planetary systems to become free-flying interstellar planetesimals. The PhD project will give astronomers new insight into where interstellar comets came from.

Your primary responsibility will be to pursue your doctoral studies, which will mainly consist of conducting research and writing a doctoral thesis. In addition, you will be expected to:

  • Conduct research within the subject area.
  • Publish results in high-quality scientific journals.
  • Present research results at national and international conferences.

The 120 credits must include at least 60 second-cycle credits. 

Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually. 

In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Astronomy and Astrophysics may be considered for admission.

  • Excellent numerical and analytical problem-solving skills, as well as experience with programming languages (e.g. Python and Fortran).

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on hydraulic design of structures within hydropower. Many dam facilities have been rebuilt or are to be upgraded to achieve a higher level of safety. A bottom outlet is a critical structure from both a dam safety and operational point of view. Emergency lowering of a reservoir's water level is entirely dependent on it and the outlet can also be used in the event of a spillway overflow. jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on reinforced concrete structures within hydropower. Dams in Sweden and many other countries are aging and have an average age of over 50 years. Spillways and associated concrete structures play a crucial role in reducing the risk of dam overflow and serious damage. However, over the years, these have been exposed to varying flows, including extreme high flows, which in many cases has caused damage. The most common repair method today is underwater concrete casting, which is costly and experience shows that many such repairs do not last as long as planned.

The project is part of a national research program within the hydropower area called SVC – Swedish Centre for Sustainable Hydropower. The research is carried out together with senior researchers at KTH and in interdisciplinary research collaboration with international researchers and industry partners. The aim is to create a better understanding of how damage occurs, what forces and hydraulic loads act, and how these affect both concrete and the rock subsurface. The project is expected to provide decision-making information for maintenance, repair and reconstruction of embankments and associated structures.

jobs.title: Doctoral student on structural health monitoring of concrete hydro dams
jobs.department: KTH, School of Architecture and Built Environment
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on reinforced concrete structures within hydropower. Dams in Sweden and many other countries are aging and have an average age of over 50 years. As they age, damage becomes more common. Typical visible damage includes cracks, leaching and scratching of the concrete surface and can be detected by visual inspections. However, there are also many other types of damage that may be more difficult to detect, such as reinforcement corrosion. In order to maintain older dams in full operation with a high level of safety, the response of the dams should be continuously monitored.

The project is part of a national research program within the hydropower area called SVC – Swedish Centre for Sustainable Hydropower. The research is carried out together with senior researchers at KTH and in interdisciplinary research collaboration with international researchers and industry partners. The aim is to create a good understanding of the structural response of concrete dams during normal operation, what should be measured and where sensors should be placed. The project will also identify which types of sensors are appropriate to use and identify reasonable alarm limits.

Third-cycle subject: Sustainability studies

We are seeking applicants with an interest in wetland restoration as a nature-based solution for sustainable water supply under changing climate conditions. The  will combine methods such as policy analysis, value mapping, socio-economic analysis, and qualitative research methods. The overall aim is to develop policy and valuation frameworks that link wetland indicators to societal benefits and costs, as well as to practical policy instruments and financing mechanisms. The successful applicant will primarily contribute to: (1) developing policy-relevant indicators for the water-related benefits of restored wetlands and exploring how these can be translated into information relevant for valuation, decision-making, and policy development; and (2) analyzing and mapping the values generated by wetland restoration for different stakeholders and society as a whole, including benefits, costs, and risks, as well as how these are distributed among different actors.

Hormones shape metabolism, fertility, mood and sleep, yet they are rarely measured, and then mostly by blood tests in a clinic. jobs.title: Doctoral student in Organizational Implications of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Industrial Engineering and Management
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Industrial Economics and Management

The deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly across public and private sectors. AI-driven technologies—particularly machine learning algorithms and large language models —are becoming integral to knowledge creation, task augmentation, and business analytics. This shift has catalyzed a rise of AI ecosystems, which brings together AI startups, intermediaries, and established enterprises, fundamentally reshaping how employees, businesses, and entire industries function. However, while certain use cases offer efficiency gains, organizations frequently grapple with critical challenges, such as low returns on investment, output unreliability, and pressing ethical dilemmas.

This PhD project aims to critically analyze the organizational implications of AI. The PhD student may explore questions such as, but not limited to: How do organizations mitigate the managerial challenges stemming from the probabilistic nature of AI technologies? How will AI transform the modern industry; and what are the opportunities and risks associated with such transformation? Along with the Big Tech companies and AI giants, what role do startups and intermediaries play in a more responsible transformation towards AI-based economy?

The PhD position is a part of the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program - Humanity and Society (WASP-HS), a national research program in Sweden. WASP-HS fosters novel interdisciplinary knowledge about AI and autonomous systems and their impact on humanity and society. WASP-HS enables cutting-edge research, expertise, and capacity building in the social sciences and humanities. For more information, see here.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in probabilistic machine learning for fluid mechanics
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

FLOW is a strong community of researchers engaged in fundamental and applied research in fluid mechanics within the department of Engineering Mechanics.

We are currently seeking a PhD student in probabilistic machine learning to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group within FLOW. AI is becoming a critical investment across science and engineering, but fluid mechanics poses particular challenges: flows are often high-dimensional and chaotic, and couple physical processes across many scales.

This position offers an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to develop trustworthy probabilistic methods for inference, optimization and data assimilation. These methods will integrate simulations and experimental data into reliable tools for the design, prediction and control of complex fluid systems.

The work focuses on turbulent flows that carry electric charge, as found for example in power transformers. These systems involve coupled processes that are only partly understood, and measurements are sparse and costly. This makes them an ideal testbed, where models must be calibrated, uncertainties quantified and experiments chosen with care, with direct impact on safer and more sustainable power infrastructure. The project is funded by Digital Futures och Hitachi Energy

Supervision: Shervin Bagheri and Ozan Öktem are proposed to supervise the student. Decisions are made on admission.

Admission requirements
