jobs.title: Doctoral student in fusion plasma physics and nuclear engineering
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering 

The provision of plasma-facing components (PFCs) with sufficient lifetime is one of the major technological obstacles to be overcome in developing fusion reactors. Recently, the damage of PFCs due to interaction with runaway electrons (RE) has become a highly critical issue in evaluations of disruption consequences. ITER, currently seeks for the validation of relevant numerical models and tools against existing experimental evidence in order to gain confidence in their applications to predictive reactor modelling.

PhD project will focus on the development of modelling tools for simulations of RE-induced PFC damage and their validation against data from EUROfusion Consortium, and DIII-D (USA). The validated models will be employed for predictive modelling of specific ITER scenarios following input from the ITER Organization. The modelling of MeV RE energy deposition in PFCs will be performed with Monte Carlo simulations. These results will serve as input for the thermomechanical models to be developed in FEM and CFD software to address severe deformation and potential explosion of the material.

We offer expertise in the theory and modelling of plasma-surface interactions and electron transport into matter, access to state-of-the-art experimental data from the largest tokamaks worldwide and close collaboration with the Experiments & Plasma Operation Section of the ITER Organization.

jobs.title: MSCA Doctoral Student in Automatic Control with a Focus on Secure Control Systems under Uncertainty
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Information Technology
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working on control theory applied to cybersecurity, supported by competent, friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University.

The position is part of the SecReSy4You Doctoral Network, funded by the EU Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA).  For a complete list of the 10 available positions, please visit the network’s website.

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, with 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

The doctoral student will join the Secure Learning and Control Laboratory, an interdisciplinary research group doing basic and applied research at the intersection of control theory, cybersecurity, and machine learning. Our vision is to develop methodologies for designing intelligent autonomous decision-making systems that are secure and resilient against malicious adversaries and natural failures. 

As a doctoral student with us, you get offered:

  • Work in an interdisciplinary network of national and international collaborators at an outstanding research institution.
  • Active supervision and promotion of your scientific development toward a PhD.
  • A close integration of fundamental research and applications.
  • Access to state-of-the-art research facilities and resources, including high-performance compute clusters.
  • A collaborative and supportive research environment with an international, friendly, and dedicated team.
  • A balanced and family-friendly work-life relationship.

About the MSCA Doctoral Network
Critical infrastructures and cyber-physical systems face increasing risks from cyberattacks that exploit vulnerabilities in digital communication networks, embedded hardware, and software. These attacks have far-reaching consequences, including the potential to collect sensitive information, cause physical damage, and endanger human lives.

In response to these challenges, the European MSCA Doctoral Network SecReSy4You aims to train a new generation of 10 researchers in control engineering, computer science, and machine learning, with a focus on cybersecurity and resilience for cyber-physical systems (CPS). The 10 doctoral candidates will collaborate on modeling threat actors, developing control-theoretic and AI-based solutions for monitoring and controlling dynamical systems under adversaries, and designing strategies to ensure long-term CPS protection.

The network brings together leading research institutions and companies from Austria, Cyprus, Estonia, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden, and the Netherlands. It comprises 10 closely connected research projects and a joint doctoral training program.

Project description
The project aims to develop new theories and methods for enhancing the security of control systems in the presence of strategic, realistically constrained adversaries and probabilistic uncertainty. We seek to develop control-theoretic analysis and design algorithms that incorporate cross-layer information and account for trade-offs among nominal performance, resilience to undetectable attacks, and uncertainty for both the operator and the adversary. 

We envision the project involving methodologies from control theory, game theory, and robust optimization, integrated with advanced adversary models and control frameworks such as model predictive control or reinforcement learning. The exact details of the project will be decided in a dialogue between the student and supervisors. 

The doctoral candidate in this project will work primarily with control engineering methodologies. Prior experience in cybersecurity or machine learning is not required, although an interest in these areas is welcome.

As part of an MSCA Doctoral Network, the project includes extended research visits abroad of up to 6 months in total. The planned supervisors are Assoc. Prof. André Teixeira and co-supervisor Prof. Christian Rohner.

Duties
The doctoral student will primarily devote their time to graduate education. Other departmental duties of at most 20%, including teaching and administration, may also be included in the employment. In addition, the duties include the following:

  • Interdisciplinary research on control theory and cyber-physical security, with a focus on secure control systems under uncertainty and realistic adversaries.
  • Publication of scientific results in top journals and at flagship conferences.
  • Contributions to network-wide events and participation in (transnational) academic and/or industrial secondments within Europe.

Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in electrical and computer engineering, engineering physics, computer science, applied mathematics, or a closely related field, or 
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

For special entry requirements, please see the subject’s general study plan.

Additionally, you must have: 

  • Solid knowledge of automatic control and systems theory.
  • Very good academic performance in previous studies.
  • Good proficiency in programming (e.g. in C, C++, Python, Julia, or Matlab).
  • High-quality MSc thesis (or equivalent) or other independent written work.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.
  • Personal characteristics such as a good level of creativity, thoroughness, and/or a structured approach to problem-solving.

To be eligible as a doctoral student within MSCA (Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions), you must not have a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment and not be enrolled in a doctoral program. The MSCA mobility rule requires applicants not to have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of their host organization (Sweden) for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the recruitment date.

Additional qualifications

  • Knowledge in one or more of the following areas: model predictive control, robust or stochastic control, optimization, or game theory.
  • Demonstrated high-quality analytical ability.
  • Personal qualities such as initiative, collaborative ability, and the capacity to communicate effectively with both international and national project partners, as well as to work independently and as part of a team.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

Application
The application must include the documents listed below. The submitted materials should provide clear evidence of the applicant’s qualifications in relation to the assessment criteria.

  1. Cover letter (maximum two pages) describing the applicant’s motivation for applying for the position and the earliest possible starting date. The letter should include a section titled “Suitability for this position”, in which the applicant briefly explains how their background, skills, and experience match the requirements and assessment criteria.
  2. Curriculum vitae (CV).
  3. Copies of degrees and transcripts of records, including grades (with translations into English or Swedish if the original documents are in another language).
  4. Master’s thesis (or a draft, if not yet completed) and/or one other self-produced technical or scientific writing that demonstrates the applicant’s research and analytical abilities. Applicants may also include publications or other relevant documents.
  5. Contact information for two references (names, email addresses, and telephone numbers). Applicants may also include up to two letters of recommendation.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date 15 January 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala.

Doctoral students employed through the Marie Sklodowska-Curie programme will receive a salary in accordance with the Marie Curie rules for doctoral students for the duration of the scholarship (36 months). This means that the gross salary (i.e., after deduction of employer contributions but including employee taxes) is approximately (depending on the exchange rate) 37,000 SEK/month (without family allowance). Employee’s national and local taxes will be deducted from this gross salary before payment of the net salary to the doctoral candidate. At the end of the project an additional payment of salary may be made, if the average exchange rate during the entire project is higher than the estimated exchange rate.

For the remaining period of your studies, you will be employed under a regular doctoral contract, with salary according to the agreed salary ladder for doctoral students plus a salary increment of 1800 SEK/month. Follow this link to read more about financing for PhD students, and a local collective agreement for salaries for PhD students.

For further information about the position, please contact: Associate Professor André Teixeira (email: andre.teixeira@it.uu.se, phone: +46  18-471 5414,).

Please submit your application by 16 December 2026, UFV-PA 2026/3678.

jobs.title: PhD student in nuclear safeguards for advanced reactors in maritime applications
jobs.department: Uppsala universitet, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
The Division of Applied Nuclear Physics at Uppsala University conducts research in several areas of nuclear science and technology, including reactor physics, nuclear fuel, nuclear data, radiation detection, and nuclear safeguards.

You will join the nuclear safeguards research group, where experimental measurements, computational modelling, and data analysis are combined to develop methods for verifying nuclear materials and supporting nuclear non-proliferation. The group's research includes non-destructive measurements of spent nuclear fuel, applications of machine learning, and the development of safeguards methods for emerging nuclear energy systems.

The PhD project focuses on nuclear safeguards for advanced reactors, with particular emphasis on maritime applications. The aim is to develop methods for characterising and verifying nuclear materials in these systems, particularly TRISO-fuelled reactors and other advanced reactor concepts. The research will be conducted in collaboration with academic and industrial partners within the international SAINT (Sustainable Applied and Industrialized Nuclear Technology) consortium, coordinated by the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics


Duties

The doctoral project focuses on nuclear non-proliferation and safeguards for advanced Generation IV nuclear energy systems. The project aims to support the future deployment of Generation IV reactor technologies by developing methods and tools for nuclear material accountancy, safeguards implementation and verification.

As a PhD student, you will combine reactor physics, fuel depletion modelling, radiation detection, and data analysis to investigate how nuclear materials can be characterised and verified in advanced reactor systems. Particular emphasis will be placed on TRISO-fuelled reactor systems and other advanced reactor technologies of relevance to the SAINT consortium, including concepts proposed by industrial partners. The duties include:

  • Developing reactor physics and fuel depletion models for advanced reactor concepts.
  • Simulating fuel irradiation and calculating isotopic inventories and neutron and gamma-ray emissions throughout the fuel cycle.
  • Investigating how radiation signatures can be used to verify nuclear materials and assay changes in fuel composition.
  • Developing and evaluating measurement techniques, instrumentation and data analysis techniques, potentially including machine learning, for nuclear safeguards.
  • Assessing the applicability of existing safeguards approaches and developing new methods to address challenges associated with advanced reactors in maritime applications.
  • publishing research results in scientific articles, and presenting results at national and international conferences,

Teaching and other departmental duties may be included, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time employment, with a corresponding extension of the employment period.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • Hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in engineering physics, physics, nuclear engineering, or another area relevant to the topic or
  • Have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • Have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way
  • Good ability to communicate in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively, demonstrating maturity, sound judgement, and reliability.

In addition, you must be eligible to a personal licence for export-restricted codes such as MCNP. This eligibility will be checked before admission to the doctoral studies.

Information about doctoral education, eligibility requirements and admission rules can be found on the web site of the Faculty of Science and Technology.

 

Additional qualifications

The following qualifications are considered meriting:

  • Knowledge of nuclear energy systems, including light water reactors and advanced reactor concepts.
  • Experience with reactor physics simulations, nuclear fuel modelling, or radiation transport codes such as Serpent, MCNP, or Geant4.
  • Experience with modelling radiation detection, particularly neutron and gamma-rays and of data analysis.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including experience in programming, data analysis, and the application or development of machine learning methods.
  • Knowledge of nuclear safeguards and experience with national or international research collaborations.
  • Experience with national and international collaborations

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, § 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.


About the application

Please attach your transcript of records, a copy of or link to your degree project, and any other supporting documents you wish to rely on in your application. In this recruitment we have replaced the cover letter with questions that you are asked to answer when making your application. The answers will be used as a part of the selection process.

The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100%. Starting March 1 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

jobs.title: PhD student in Tumour Immunology
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology at Uppsala University has a broad research profile with strong research groups focused on cancer, autoimmune and genetic diseases. A fundamental idea at the department is to stimulate translational research and thereby closer interactions between medical research and health care. Research is presently conducted in the following areas: medical and clinical genetics, clinical immunology, pathology, neuro biology, neuro-oncology, vascular biology, radiation science and molecular tools. Department activities are also integrated with the units for Oncology, Clinical Genetics, Clinical Immunology, Clinical Pathology, and Hospital Physics at Akademiska sjukhuset, Uppsala. The department has teaching assignments in several education programmes, including Master Programmes, at the Faculty of Medicine, and at the Disciplinary Domain of Science and Technology. The department has a yearly turnover of around SEK 500 million, out of which more than half is made up of external funding. The staff amounts to approximately 345 employees, out of which 100 are PhD-students, and there are in total more than 700 affiliated people. Feel free to read more about the department's activities here: https://www.uu.se/en/department/immunology-genetics-and-pathology

Read more about our benefits and what it is like to work at Uppsala University

Are you interested in working with tumour immunology and cancer immunotherapy, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD student position at Uppsala University.

Research in Yumeng Mao’s group aims to understand the interaction between the immune system and tumour cells. The group studies the negative mechanisms that cancer cells use to inhibit the function of immune cells, combining experimental tumour immunology with bioinformatic analyses. The group’s research generates knowledge that can accelerate the development of immunotherapy for patients. More information about the group’s research is available at https://maolab.nu.

Duties
In this project, the prospective PhD student will combine advanced single cell transcriptomics and spatial transcriptomics tools and advanced genetic modification cell and animal models, to elucidate how to sensitize triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells to immunotherapy. As a PhD student, you will plan and perform experiments, analyse data, including with bioinformatic methods, and compile and present your results in scientific articles and at conferences. The programme also includes doctoral-level courses and teaching duties at the department.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • - hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in a relevant subject, e.g. immunology, biomedicine or molecular medicine, or
  • - have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • - have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

In addition, the following are required:

  • - Documented skills in bioinformatic analyses using R or Python, e.g. scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, RNA-seq or proteomics. Applicants should have experience in two of these areas and an interest in learning the remaining ones.
  • - Documented practical experience of experimental research in tumour immunology and tumour biology.
  • - Experience of isolating and handling cancer cells and primary immune cells.
  • - Experience of CRISPR/Cas9 technology, genetic engineering, western blotting, ELISA, PCR, handling of blood products and cell culture.
  • - Willingness to conduct hands-on experiments using various mouse models. Certification of working with laboratory animals is not required at the point of application but is expected to be acquired within 6 months of employment.
  • - Solid theoretical understanding on relevant subjects, e.g. TNBC biology, immunology, tumour micro-environment, etc.
  • - Good command of written and spoken English.

As a person, you find it easy to collaborate with others, but you also have a good ability to work independently.

Additional qualifications
Research experience of data integration and machine learning methods, as well as of co-culture systems of human immune cells and cancer cells, is a strong advantage. A demonstrated ability to publish scientific studies, e.g. co-authorships on research articles is considered a significant advantage.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date February 1st or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

For further information about the position, please contact: Yumeng Mao (yumeng.mao@igp.uu.se).

Please submit your application by 15 December 2026, UFV-PA 2026/3695.

The Department of Civil and Industrial Engineering consists of three divisions: Quality Science, Industrial Engineering and Management, and Civil Engineering and Built Environment. The department has approximately 100 employees and has its research and education both at the Ångström Laboratory in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland. For more information, see Department of Civil and Industrial Engineering (uu.se). This position will be located at the Division of Civil Engineering and Built Environment in Uppsala.

The Division Civil Engineering and Built Environment conducts research and education in the field of construction with a focus on energy in buildings and the built environment. We provide courses in building physics, building design, energy efficiency in buildings, energy systems for buildings and infrastructure systems. Around 20 people work with us and we have several successful collaborations with businesses and organizations

Duties  
People spend a large portion of their time indoors, making the indoor environment an important factor for health and well-being. As climate change intensifies and heatwaves become increasingly frequent, the risk of overheating in the existing building stock is rising. This can result in increased exposure to heat and, consequently, a higher risk of heat-related health problems, particularly among vulnerable groups. In this research project, funded by Formas, you, as a doctoral student, will work to develop mathematical models for analysing the indoor climate in the Swedish building stock. Furthermore, you will identify which building types and urban areas in Sweden are particularly vulnerable to high indoor temperatures under both current and future climate conditions. The work also includes evaluating various climate adaptation measures aimed at reducing the risk of indoor overheating and thereby preventing related health risks. The research project is interdisciplinary which involves close collaboration with environmental epidemiologists and health scientists. Through this interdisciplinary collaboration, you as a doctoral student will have the opportunity to combine expertise in building physics, indoor climate, and climate change with a health-oriented perspective. This will contribute to a deeper understanding of the relationships between building characteristics, the indoor climate, and human health.

jobs.title: PhD student in Microbial Chemistry with a focus on nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria
jobs.department: Uppsala universitet, Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's five programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. Department of Chemistry Ångström Laboratory.

Duties
Plants require nitrogen to grow but cannot directly use atmospheric dinitrogen, which makes modern agriculture dependent on synthetic fertilizers. Fertilizer production is energy-intensive, environmentally costly and strongly dependent on fossil fuels, tightly linking food production to energy supply and climate impact. There is therefore an urgent need for sustainable biological alternatives. Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria uniquely couple oxygenic photosynthesis with nitrogen fixation, making them a powerful model for uncovering core metabolic and regulatory principles. Despite extensive genomic information, many of their genes remain functionally uncharacterized, which limits our understanding of how nitrogen fixation is integrated with growth and metabolism. In this project, you will help establish a comprehensive, system-level view of nitrogen fixation across multiple cyanobacterial lineages. Using genome-scale library screening, you will systematically map genotype–phenotype relationships to identify genetic, metabolic and regulatory determinants of growth and nitrogen fixation. These data will be integrated into interpretable models to reveal system-level constraints and predictive principles, generating fundamental knowledge with long-term relevance for sustainable nitrogen biology and future fertilizer-independent agriculture.

You work will include cultivating cyanobacteria under different nitrogen regimes, genetic engineering, construction and screening of genome-scale libraries, next generation sequencing based analyses, phenotypic characterization of growth and nitrogen fixation, and bioinformatic analysis and modelling of the resulting data. You will be part of a research group with several ongoing cyanobacteria projects, and you are expected to present your results in scientific publications and at national and international conferences. The doctoral education also includes PhD-level courses. Teaching and/or other departmental duties may be included, up to 20% of full time.

jobs.title: PhD student in plant evolution
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Ecology and Genetics
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about studying how flowers have convergently evolved in response to bee pollinators? We are now looking for a PhD student in plant evolution to join us at the Plant Ecology and Evolution program, Department of Ecology and Genetics.

The Department of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) is an international environment with staff and students from all over the world. We are part of the Evolutionary Biology Center (EBC) which is a prime environment for graduate students interested in addressing fundamental and applied biological questions through an evolutionary perspective.

Project description

Convergent evolution in buzz-pollinated flowers
Convergent evolution, where similar traits evolve repeatedly across independent biological groups is a recurrent and important phenomenon in the history of life. In most studies of convergent evolution, similarity in function is assumed from similarity on phenotype (form). However, in principle, it is possible that similar traits evolve independently without functioning in the same way.

To date, few studies have explicitly compared similarity in form and function across a taxonomically broad sample of convergent plant lineages, and this is the main knowledge gap that the PhD student will address here. As a model system, we will study flowers that are pollinated by vibration-producing bees (buzz pollinated flowers). These flowers are one of the most widespread examples of convergent evolution in plants, encompassing more than 20,000 species. Our project will study independent origins of buzz pollinated flowers to: (1) evaluate the extent of convergence in key floral traits across plants in several plant families, (2) test specific hypotheses for the function of buzz pollinated flowers across independent evolutionary origins, and (3) combine analyses of trait and functional convergence to understand the pathways of convergence and evolutionary novelty in plants.

Duties
The PhD student will work with both bumblebees and with recently developed bee-size robotic shakers (robo-buzzers) to explore form and function of buzz pollinated flowers. This is an experimentally focused project that requires skills for working with delicate electronic equipment, careful experimentation, and handling live bees. The student should be willing to learn the use and troubleshooting of electronic and mechanical hardware and corresponding software. Floral characterization will include the use of X-ray micro-computed tomography. Other tasks include growing and caring for plants in the glasshouse and maintaining bumblebee colonies.

The PhD student is also expected to actively participate in the academic activities of our research group (including attending weekly meetings), develop analytical frameworks, prepare manuscripts for publication, and present their work at national and international meetings.

Qualifications required
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • Hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in biology, evolutionary biology, plant biology, or electrical engineering or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.
  • Be able to work closely with plants and bees.
  • Be able to handle and effectively use delicate and complex electro-mechanical equipment and associated software.

Candidates must be able to express themselves fully in spoken as well as written English.

Qualifications desired

  • Knowledge of ecological and evolutionary theory
  • Demonstrated capacity to design and troubleshoot experiments
  • Experience of working with technically complex electro-mechanical equipment
  • Knowledge of basic biophysical and biomechanical principles
  • Experience with statistical analyses and associated software (e.g., R, MatLab)
  • Previous experience with plant and bee work
  • Academic writing skills appropriate for their career stage
  • Familiarity with pollination biology
  • Capacity to work as part of a team and contribute to the academic development of more junior members

The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. 

Duties
Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) designed for electric vehicles and grid storage have longstanding sustainability and security-of-supply concerns. Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) address both concerns, but do not currently hold enough energy to replace LIBs in all applications. The most promising strategy to improve the energy density of SIBs is to remove the conventional anode material from SIBs: an “anodeless” cell. However, serious challenges remain to increase lifespan and develop them to commercial viability. The project aims to address these challenges to commercializing next-gen SIBs by focusing on the stability of sodium metal anodes.

The PhD position will involve the development of electrolytes and electrochemical techniques for anodeless sodium-ion batteries. The overarching aim is to develop high energy density sodium-ion batteries that are made from sustainable materials and are free of critical raw materials. The PhD position will be based in Uppsala University, but the candidate will be expected to collaborate closely with industrial actors (Altris AB and Polestar), and the position will involve a 6 month placement in Humboldt University of Berlin to gain expertise in electrochemical dilatometry (to be completed within the 3rd year of the PhD).

The work will involve a combination of fundamental electrochemical evaluation of anodeless SIBs, development and characterization of novel liquid and gel electrolytes, advanced operando techniques (particularly operando microscopy and electrochemical dilatometry) and development of anodeles cells in near-commercial multi-layer pouch cells. Teaching and other departmental duties may be part of the position, to a maximum of 20% of the working hours.

The duties of the PhD candidate will include:

  • Development and characterisation of SIB liquid electrolyte, as well as explorations of gel electrolyte.

jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's five programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website.

The student will be part of the bioinorganic chemistry group within the molecular biomimetics program. The program is highly recognized internationally with strong visibility and the group is situated in a modern building at the Ångström Laboratory. Strong cross-disciplinary collaborations are characteristic for the program

Project description
The project involves biochemistry and biophysics, with a focus on so-called hydrogenase enzymes. Hydrogenases are redox-active metalloenzymes that catalyze the interconversion of protons and molecular hydrogen, enabling molecular hydrogen metabolism central to microbial energy systems. Recent findings have challenged the prevailing view of [FeFe] hydrogenases as fully reversible catalysts, instead revealing enzymes with strong intrinsic catalytic bias toward either hydrogen uptake or production. This project explores the hypothesis that such enzymes act as “metabolic rectifiers,” supporting unidirectional electron flow with minimal energy loss—an adaptation potentially critical for life near thermodynamic limits.

Duties
The doctoral student will participate in a research project with two main objectives: to establish the prevalence of unidirectional catalysis among hydrogenases by characterising enzymes from different ecological and phylogenetic contexts, and to identify the molecular determinants of catalytic directionality through the rational design and analysis of enzyme variants. Complementary studies will aim to develop kinetic models linking thermodynamic reversibility to catalytic directionality.

The doctoral student's role in the project will primarily involve the isolation and characterisation of novel [FeFe] hydrogenases, as well as the detailed characterisation of selected enzymes using a combination of electrochemistry and spectroscopy (EPR and FTIR spectroscopy) to elucidate their reaction mechanisms. Writing scientific publications will also be an important part of the position. The work will be carried out in collaboration with other specialists at Uppsala University and at other universities in Sweden and abroad.

The main duties of the doctoral student are to devote themselves to their doctoral studies, which include participation in the research project described above and completion of third-cycle courses. jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with research in Computational Science, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University.

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, with 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

Project description
The project focuses on the development of computational and data-driven methods for epidemiological modelling and analysis. A central component is the development of stochastic models and Bayesian methods for combining epidemiological models with different types of data, with the aim of enabling reliable estimates and situational awareness. The project offers several possible research directions, including statistical validation and diagnostics for simulation-based inference, the use of neural networks to construct informative prior distributions, and game-theoretic modelling of epidemics and the value of information in decisions concerning public health interventions. The common foundation is computational modelling and Bayesian inference, while the specific research direction can be adapted to the doctoral candidate's background and interests. The project thus offers opportunities to work at the intersection of applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning and computational science, with epidemiological applications providing a common focus.

A more detailed project description is available at: https://stefanengblom.github.io/files/docs/Comput_Modeling_Epidemics.pdf

Duties

Requirements

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in Computational Science, Enigineering Physics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, or a related subject, or

jobs.title: PhD student in plant demography
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Ecology and Genetics
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to conduct research on the population ecology of plants? Do you want to join an outstanding academic environment at Uppsala University’s Evolutionary Biology Centre? We are now looking to recruit a PhD student who wishes to begin their research career together with us.

The Department of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) Department of Ecology and Genetics – Uppsala University at the Evolutionary Biology Center (EBC) is an international environment with staff that conducts research to understand ecological and evolutionary processes across all levels of biological organization. IEG provides access to advanced national and local research infrastructures, including free super computing resources (NAISS) and the latest molecular technologies and sequencing platforms (SciLifeLab platforms). IEG hosts a Climate Lab with controlled environmental chambers, greenhouses and a state-of-the-art molecular lab. PhD-students at IEG can join the PhD school which provides ample opportunities for networking on and off campus with PhD-students from the other two biology departments at Uppsala University (The Department of Organismal Biology, and the Department of Cellular and Molecular Biology).

The position is offered by the research program in Plant Ecology and Evolution at IEG. Information about the program’s current research can be found here.

Duties
The PhD project will address central current questions about plant life history and population dynamics, with focus on how demographic parameters (survival and reproduction) are affected by plant ageing and how environmental factors influence the same “vital rates” and thus the dynamics and distribution patterns of populations. The goals of the research will be to address key basic ecological questions and to achieve knowledge on how environmental changes will affect populations and communities. For examples of our previous work on demographic ageing see key papers here and here, and on environmental drivers of population dynamics here and here.

The main supervisor of the PhD candidate will be Johan Dahlgren. Specific aims and focus of the project will be decided together with the supervisor but will involve a combination of independent field work and mathematical modelling, and utilize ongoing long-term studies of Actaea spicata, Pulsatilla vulgaris subsp. gotlandica, and orchids of the genera Dactylorhiza and Gymnadenia. The exact balance between tasks will depend on the candidate's interests and the project's development.

PhD students at the Institute of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) have the option to engage in teaching and to develop their pedagogic CV by taking courses. The type and level of teaching will depend on availability and the student's interests but cannot exceed 20% full-time employment. The position and funding are extended by the time the student has engaged in teaching.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in biology with focus on ecology or a related field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

We attach great importance to personal qualities such as motivation, independence, and problem-solving analytical skills. We value highly other personal qualities including initiative, creativity, and the ability to cooperate and collaborate with others. 

The candidate is also expected to:

  • have a valid international driver’s license,
  • have good understanding of central ecological concepts,
  • have experience with statistical analysis and population modelling, especially using the software R,
  • be highly motivated and curious and thrive in a collaborative environment,
  • be able to take responsibility for carrying out and finishing independent tasks and projects, and
  • express themselves at a high level in spoken as well as written English.

Additional qualifications
Experience with ecological field work, plant species identification and all forms of quantitative skills are meriting.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date 1 April 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

Instructions for the application
The application must include:

  1. A cover letter describing yourself, your research interests, why you want to pursue a PhD, and why you are suitable for this specific position (maximum 2 pages).
  2. CV.
  3. A brief description of your education.
  4. A copy of your master's degree and course transcripts, as well as a copy of your master's thesis.
  5. Names and contact details of at least two references (email and phone number).
  6. Any publications.

For further information about the position, please contact: Johan Dahlgren, johan.dahlgren@ebc.uu.se.

jobs.title: PhD student in Computer Science with a focus on Computer Architecture
jobs.department: Uppsala universitet, Department of Information Technology
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with next-generation interconnect technology for energy-efficient AI systems, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University.

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, with 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

Project description
The PhD position is part of the NEAT research project and focuses on computer architecture for future AI systems. The project aims to contribute to efficient and sustainable computing by investigating how architectural and system-level choices affect performance, energy use and scalability.

As a PhD student, you will investigate research questions in computer architecture, develop and evaluate new approaches, and analyse their potential benefits and limitations. The work involves modelling, simulation and experimental evaluation, combining theoretical understanding with practical research skills.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Yuan Yao and join an international research environment with established collaborations with both academia and industry.

Duties 
The doctoral student will primarily devote their time to graduate education. Other departmental duties of at most 20%, including teaching and administration, may also be included in the employment.

Requirements 
To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must: 

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, embedded systems, or another field relevant to the project, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The University may permit an exemption from the general entry requirements for an individual applicant, if there are special grounds (Chapter 7, § 39 of the Higher Education Ordinance). For special entry requirements, please see the subject’s general study plan.

The position also requires that you have:

  • very good knowledge of computer architecture and digital hardware design,
  • very good programming skills, for example in C/C++ and Python,
  • excellent oral and written proficiency in English.

Great emphasis will be placed on personal qualities such as analytical ability, independence, attention to detail, and good collaboration skills, as well as on motivation for doctoral studies.

Additional qualifications 
Experience with any of the following is considered an advantage:

  • FPGA development and hardware description languages (e.g. Verilog, VHDL, or Chisel),
  • architecture or network simulators (e.g. gem5, SCALE-Sim, ASTRA-sim),
  • interconnection networks/networks-on-chip (NoC) or AI accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, NPUs),
  • machine learning frameworks (e.g. PyTorch) and work with large AI models,
  • scientific publications in computer architecture or related areas.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

jobs.title: PhD student in experimental nuclear physics with a focus on nuclear fission and gamma-ray emission
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with experimental nuclear physics, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Division of Applied Nuclear Physics, at Uppsala University conducts research and education in applied nuclear physics. Its activities aim to deepen our understanding of the properties of atomic nuclei and apply this knowledge in areas such as energy and materials research.

The successful candidate will join an internationally active research group investigating nuclear-reaction dynamics and nuclear fission through experiments and modelling. Our research tests theoretical predictions and addresses fundamental questions relevant to nuclear physics and astrophysics. It also produces high-precision nuclear data for applications in nuclear-energy systems, cancer treatment, and radiation-tolerant microelectronics. The group collaborates with leading research facilities across Europe.

This doctoral project forms part of a Nordic collaboration between Uppsala University and the University of Oslo (UiO), within the Norwegian Nuclear Research Centre (NNRC). It brings together expertise in nuclear fission, nuclear structure, gamma-ray spectroscopy, detector development, and nuclear modelling. A substantial part of the experimental work will take place at the Oslo Cyclotron Laboratory (OCL).


Duties

The doctoral project will ultimately investigate how excitation energy and angular momentum are shared between fission fragments and subsequently carried away by gamma-ray emission. You will measure prompt fission gamma-ray spectra, multiplicities, and total energies as functions of excitation energy, and attempt to extract fission-product yields and isomeric yield ratios. These measurements will test our understanding of nuclear fission and provide data to improve predictions of gamma-ray heating and other fission observables relevant to Generation IV reactors operating with fast neutron spectra.

You will prepare and conduct experiments at OCL in close collaboration with researchers and technical specialists at UiO. The experiments will use the uranium-235(d,pf) reaction as a surrogate for neutron-induced fission of uranium-235. Detecting the outgoing proton together with fission fragments and gamma rays will allow the measured observables to be related to the excitation energy of the fissioning nucleus.

A central part of your work will be centered around the OSCAR gamma-ray detector array, charged-particle detectors, and a newly developed fission chamber. You will contribute to detector characterisation, calibration, commissioning, and optimisation of the experimental setup.

You will analyse the experimental data using coincidence techniques, detector-response corrections, background subtraction, and uncertainty analysis. Characteristic gamma-ray transitions will be used to identify selected fission products, while delayed emission will provide complementary information about fragment angular momentum through isomeric yield ratios.

The project also includes computational fission modelling in close collaboration with the nuclear data section at the International atomic energy agency. Using TALYS and fission models such as FREYA and GEF, you will assess how well current calculations describe energy sharing, angular momentum, and fragment de-excitation. Comparisons with the measurements will help identify model limitations and guide further development.

The position involves extended research visits to Oslo and may include detector tests and experiments at other international facilities. You will present your research in peer-reviewed publications, at scientific conferences, and in collaboration meetings.


Requirements

Applicants must meet the general eligibility requirements for doctoral studies through one of the following:

  • Hold a Master’s degree in physics, engineering physics, nuclear engineering, applied physics, or another subject relevant to the project;
  • or Have completed at least 240 higher education credits, including at least 60 credits at Master’s level and an independent project of at least 15 credits;
  • or Have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge through other studies or professional experience.

The position also requires:

  • An interest in physics, experimental work, data analysis, and physical modelling.
  • The ability to work independently and systematically, with attention to data quality.
  • Good collaboration skills.
  • Good oral and written communication skills in English.
  • Willingness and ability to undertake research visits abroad, particularly to Oslo, and participate in experimental campaigns and scientific conferences.


Additional qualifications

Desired qualifications that will be used in the ranking of the candidates:

  • Good knowledge of physics, including nuclear physics and radiation detection.
  • Programming experience, for example in Python or C++, and an interest in developing your scientific-computing skills.
  • Gamma-ray spectroscopy, coincidence measurements, or nuclear-fission experiments. Radiation detectors, detector electronics, or data-acquisition systems.
  • Experimental data analysis using ROOT or comparable tools.
  • Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport and detector response, for example using Geant4.
  • Nuclear-reaction or fission calculations using TALYS, FREYA, GEF, or related codes.
  • Statistical analysis, uncertainty propagation, or detector-response unfolding.
  • Scientific computing involving large experimental or simulated datasets.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

About the application

  • Please attach your transcript of records, a copy of or link to your degree project, and any other supporting documents you wish you rely on in your application.
  • We also welcome applications from candidates who have not yet completed their master’s thesis, however the eligibility requirements must be completed at the time of employment.

jobs.title: Doktorand i pedagogik
jobs.department: Mittuniversitetet, Institutionen för pedagogik, psykologi och socialt arbete
jobs.description_html:
Pedagogik är ett akademiskt ämne som undersöker olika former av systematiska påverkansprocesser som exempelvis fostran, ledarskap, lärande, undervisning och utbildning på individuell nivå, inom grupper och på en samhällelig nivå. Detta studeras inom olika organisationer och kontexter, exempelvis inom det formella utbildningssystemet eller inom arbetslivet och ur ett livslångt lärandeperspektiv. Vid Mittuniversitetet har pedagogikämnet utbildning och forskning kopplat till lärarutbildningen och till det beteendevetenskapliga programmet. Forskningen är organiserad i fyra forskargrupper: Didaktik, Inkludering och Mångfald (DIM), Higher Education and E-Learning (HEEL), Kritiska perspektiv i Utbildningsforskning (KUF) och Leadership in Education Administration and Development (LEAD). 

Vi söker en doktorand med fokus på högre utbildning och livslångt lärande i arbetslivet och de förutsättningar som råder vid pedagogiska processer som exempelvis organisationsutveckling, kompetensutveckling och lärande i arbetslivet. Av speciellt intresse är ett högskolepedagogiskt perspektiv på livslångt lärande och den roll som högre utbildning och aktuell samhällsutveckling spelar för att stödja arbetslivets pedagogik. I den utlysta tjänsten kommer du att i samarbete med dina handledare – erfarna forskare inom tjänstens tema – bidra till att utforska detta område.

 

Arbetsuppgifter
Forskarutbildning i ämnet pedagogik innefattande initialt 100 % forskning. I ett senare skede av utbildningen kan undervisning och administrativt arbete ingå upp till 20%.

 

Behörighet
Grundläggande behörighet har den som avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå eller på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskild behörighet har den som har grundläggande behörighet varav minst 90 högskolepoäng i pedagogik på grundnivå inkluderande ett självständigt arbete om 15 högskolepoäng samt minst 30 högskolepoäng i pedagogik på avancerad nivå inkluderande ett självständigt arbete om 15 högskolepoäng, eller på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet har förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

 

Övriga krav 
Vi söker en person som trivs med att hantera intellektuella utmaningar. Vidare har du en god förmåga att samarbeta och kommunicera. Du är intresserad av att skapa professionella relationer och nätverk med andra forskare och det omgivande samhället, både nationellt och internationellt. Du är även flexibel och bekväm i att hantera krav och motgångar i ditt arbete.

 

Bedömningsgrunder
Vi kommer att värdera följande bedömningsgrunder vid anställningen:

  • God förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildning på forskarnivå.
  • Dokumenterad god förmåga att självständigt planera och organisera arbetet.
  • Dokumenterad god samarbetsförmåga och förmåga att skapa relationer och nätverk.
  • God förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på såväl svenska som engelska.
  • God förmåga att hantera för anställningen särskilda krav.                  

Övriga meriter som är relevanta för den utlysta tjänsten är en allmänpedagogisk utbildning på grundläggande och avancerad nivå och ett dokumenterat intresse för högskolepedagogik, livslångt lärande, arbetslivets pedagogik och utveckling av pedagogiska processer i arbetslivet. 

 

Handläggning
Beredningen av anställningen följer de former som anges i högskoleförordningens 5 kap och fortgår i enlighet med Mittuniversitetets anställningsordning. 

 

Anställning och tillträde 
Doktorsexamen, 100 % egen forskarutbildning.

Doktorandanställningen avser en anställning som motsvarar fyra års heltidsstudier och beräknas leda fram till en doktorsexamen. Om studietakten i forskarutbildningen förändras ändras anställningstiden i motsvarande omfattning.

En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen får därefter förnyas med högst två år i taget. Bestämmelser gällande anställning som doktorand finns i Högskoleförordningen (1993:100), 5 kap 1-7 §§. 

Tillträde 2027-04-01 eller enligt överenskommelse.

 

Anställningsort: Sundsvall

Lön: Enligt Mittuniversitetets lönetrappa för doktorander.  

 

Information
Närmare upplysningar lämnas av ämnesföreträdare professor Jimmy Jaldemark jimmy.jaldemark@miun.se eller 010-142 82 88 samt av prefekt Ulrika Danielsson, ulrika.danielsson@ miun.se. 

 

Ansökan
Ansökningshandlingar ska vara på svenska eller engelska. 

Till din ansökan ska följande dokument bifogas:

  • Personligt brev
  • CV
  • Intyg/betyg och övriga styrkta merithandlingar du som sökande vill åberopa
  • Intressebeskrivning där du redogör för ditt forskningsintresse inom den angivna inriktningen för den utlysta tjänsten, samt dina förväntningar på forskarutbildningen.
  • Examensarbete på avancerad nivå eller magister-/masterarbete.

 

Välkommen med din ansökan via vårt rekryteringssystem senast 2026-12-15.

jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in model-based optimization of industrial heat pumps Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Position in model-based optimization of industrial heat pumps 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Energy and Process Systems Engineering (EPSE) Group at ETH Zürich is looking for a doctoral student to work on a new generation of model-based process optimization methods for high-temperature industrial heat pumps. The EPSE group, led by Prof. Dr. André Bardow, is dedicated to advancing sustainable energy and chemical process systems. Our research spans from the molecular level to the scale of systems. We develop simulation and experimental methods to advance sustainable energy and chemical processes from the molecular to the system scale. Project background Decarbonizing the industry is among the most pressing challenges of our time. Electrically driven heat pumps can reduce CO₂ emissions by more than 90% compared to conventional gas boilers when powered by green electricity, yet commercially available solutions reach only up to 160 °C, leaving the critical segment between 160 and 250 °C without viable options. For this temperature range, the transcritical cycle, with evaporation below and gas cooling above the critical point, is thermodynamically superior to all current heat pump approaches. Transcritical heat pumps are ideally suited for applications where the heat sink undergoes large temperature changes of more than 60 K, a condition found in drying, pasteurization, pressurized water heating, and many other widespread industrial processes. Despite this clear thermodynamic advantage, no commercial transcritical heat pump exists for high-temperature applications. The barriers to commercialization are the absence of systematic cycle design tools, missing refrigerant-lubricant property data around the critical point, and untested component behavior in these conditions. Job description This project directly addresses these barriers through an integrated approach combining system-level modelling, property characterization, and experimental demonstration. Your main task will be to advance superstructure-based process optimization models to identify the best cycle architectures and working fluids across industrial use cases defined with our industrial advisory board The work will be conducted in tight integration with a companion doctoral candidate in our group, who will focus on advancing the experimental counterpart methods The third (experimental) doctoral position envisaged by the project will be opened at the partner institution OST (Ost Schweizer Fachhochschule), the professors and senior researchers at both institutions will supervise the project. Your role will also involve mentoring and co-supervising student projects and theses Additionally, you will engage in various group and institute duties and activities As an integral part of your work, you will publish your results in peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences Profile You meet the requirements for a doctoral program at ETH Zurich and have an excellent Master's or diploma in process engineering, mechanical engineering, energy science & technology, chemical engineering, or a related field. Ideally, you already have experience in model-based process optimization methods The ability to work independently and excellent communication and writing skills in English complete your profile Workplace Workplace We offer We offer a full-time position for the duration of your doctoral studies, starting upon agreement with the earliest start date of April 1st, 2027. We offer a flexible and supportive working environment that fosters professional and personal growth . jobs.title: Doctoral Position in "Snow Avalanche Release Mechanics and Modeling"
jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in "Snow Avalanche Release Mechanics and Modeling" Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Position in "Snow Avalanche Release Mechanics and Modeling" 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Alpine Mass Movements at ETH Zürich and SLF Davos is looking for a motivated Doctoral student to advance our understanding and prediction of snow avalanche release. You will connect fracture mechanics, numerical simulation, and observations to address a central challenge in avalanche hazard assessment: predicting how large an avalanche will be. Project background Why does a fracture sometimes stop after a few meters, while in other cases it spreads across an entire mountainside? Snow slab avalanches release through crack propagation in a buried weak layer, followed by fracture of the overlying slab. Their final size depends on how these processes interact with snowpack variability and terrain. Despite its importance for avalanche forecasting and hazard assessment, release size remains difficult to predict. Existing methods for identifying potential release areas rely mainly on topography and account only indirectly for snow mechanical properties. Job description You will investigate how crack propagation, crack arrest, and slab fracture determine avalanche release dimensions across complex mountain terrain Using and further developing a depth-averaged Material Point Method established in our group, you will examine when release size is controlled by snowpack properties and when terrain becomes the dominant constraint You will evaluate simulations against observations from instrumented slopes and avalanche release areas mapped from drone and satellite imagery Building on this physical understanding, you will develop a probabilistic framework to assess how uncertain snow loading and mechanical properties affect the location and size of avalanche release zones This will connect the mechanics of individual releases with release-area mapping at the mountain scale As a subsequent application, you will couple release scenarios to our highly efficient depth-averaged flow solver to investigate how uncertainty in release conditions and friction parameters affects avalanche runout You will publish your results in scientific journals, present your work at international conferences, and contribute to teaching activities at ETH Zürich Profile You hold an MSc in civil engineering, geotechnics, mechanics, geophysics, physics, computational science, or a related field You have experience using or developing numerical models and strong programming skills Experience in computational mechanics, probabilistic methods, or geospatial analysis would be useful You are curious and enthusiastic about applying computational methods to snow avalanches and natural hazards You must be fluent in English; knowledge of German or French is beneficial Workplace Workplace We offer Your Doctorate is part of the project “A multi-scale modeling framework for understanding and predicting snow avalanche release size”, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). Under the supervision of Prof. Johan Gaume, you will collaborate with researchers in snow mechanics, avalanche forecasting, remote sensing and statistics. You will join a diverse, international and multidisciplinary team, bringing together Doctoral students, postdoctoral researchers, scientists, engineers and support staff working on alpine mass movements and natural hazards. jobs.title: Doctoral Position in Statistical Network Modeling
jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in Statistical Network Modeling Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Position in Statistical Network Modeling 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We are an interdisciplinary lab studying social and behavioral phenomena using network concepts. Members of the lab actively develop theories, methods and software in a variety of domains, for our own empirical studies and for our collaborative endeavors across multiple discplines. The group of Prof. Christoph Stadtfeld is looking for a motivated Doctoral student interested in the field of Statistical Network Modeling . Project background The Social Networks Lab develops, extends and applies cutting-edge statistical models for network data. Social networks are multi-layered, dynamic systems that play a crucial role for the lives of individuals they connect. In our empirical research we often asks questions about how social networks emerge and change, and how individuals’ positions in these networks matter for very personal outcomes, such as well-being, identities and behavior. But there are some statistical challenges. Connections between individuals and individual outcomes in social networks are not independent observations, like we often assume in standard statistical models. The presence of one tie can indeed alter the probability of another tie, and individuals are commonly influenced by those they are connected with. This observational dependence is not merely a nuisance but lies at the core of what networks researchers in the social sciences are interested in: how much do shared contexts, shared friends, prior interactions, or popularity increase the chance of two individuals to connect? How much do people change in response to their peers’ identities and behaviors? Job description During this project, you will be at the forefront of social network research, both independently and as a member of our research team. jobs.description: Doctoral Position in Social Networks in Education Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht Partnerinserat chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Position in Social Networks in Education 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We are an interdisciplinary lab studying social and behavioral phenomena using network concepts. Members of the lab actively develop theories, methods and software in a variety of domains, for our own empirical studies and for our collaborative endeavors across multiple discplines. The group of Prof. Christoph Stadtfeld is looking for a motivated Doctoral student interested in the field of Social Networks in Education .This position is fully funded and a joint degree with EPFL Lausanne. Project background The position is embedded in the Joint Doctoral Program in Learning Science (JDPLS) of ETH Zurich and EPFL Lausanne. The Social Networks Lab takes a sociological perspective on learning, understanding, and education within the JDPLS. One core focus of our lab is the study of social networks in education, aiming to understand how students at various levels of education form social relationships with their peers, how those aggregate into complex, dynamic social networks, and how individuals’ relationships and their network positions affect very personal outcomes, such as their well-being, motivation, learning processes, and academic success. With whom students form social ties can largely depend on institutional decisions, for example, about group and lecture assignments. The most visible example of this research line is the Swiss StudentLife Study which was conducted from 2016 to 2026. It investigated undergraduate students' social and academic intregration over the course of several years. Social networks research in educational contexts is highly interdisciplinary and simultaneously addresses theoretical, statistical, and research design challenges.  Members of the lab combine research approaches from the social sciences, statistics, and computer science. They address empirical research questions with modern ways of data collection (often combining data from digital behavioral traces with surveys) and advance the development of statistical methods, algorithms, and scientific software. The SN-LAB thereby offers a sociological perspective to research questions in education and learning science. Job description During this project, you will be at the forefront of social network research, both independently and as a member of our research team. Your responsibilities may encompass: Developing theoretical and empirical perspectives on the social embeddedness of learning, understanding, and education Conceptualizing and designing innovative observational research designs, data collection strategies and behavioral experiments in educational settings Analyzing network data with cutting-edge statistical and computational methods Engaging in interdisciplinary dialogues (e.g., learning science, sociology of education, statistics, computer science, computational social science, etc.) to enhance our knowledge how social networks emerge and change in educational settings, and how they affect the individuals they connect Presenting research progress at related conferences to an international, multidisciplinary audience Profile Successful candidates should have the following qualifications: An excellent Master's degree in learning science or quantitative behavioral sciences with a focus on learning and education (e.g., learning science, sociology of education, applied math, social data science, psychology) Prior work such as a Master thesis that demonstrates a strong interest in learning science and quantitative social network research Excellent quantitative analysis and data management skills, including experience in or willingness to learn R or Python Strong skills in scientific writing Ability and willingness to work productively in an interdisciplinary, international team Workplace Workplace We offer We offer an inspiring research environment at one of the world's top universities, close collaboration in a small research lab that is part of a leading international network of social networks researchers, advanced training in modern social networks research, generous research funding and a competitive salary. Doctoral Researcher in Energy Systems Modelling, Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Researcher in Energy Systems Modelling, Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Energy Systems Analysis (ESA) , within the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering at ETH Zurich, is recruiting a highly motivated Doctoral Researcher to work broadly in the area of energy systems analysis, artificial intelligence and digitalization. The ESA Chair is headed by Prof. Dr Russell McKenna and generally focuses on the energy system analysis of low-carbon energy systems and technologies, by working at the intersection of engineering and economics to develop and apply energy system models to diverse energy systems and research questions. The Chair holder’s joint appointment as the Head of the Laboratory of Energy Systems Analysis at PSI means a strong collaboration with this group and regular presence is also required. Project background This position is linked to the industry-financed project "SyDEF - Systemic Digitalization of Energy Futures” , led and managed by Dr. Fabian Heymann at ESA, Dr. Evangelos Panos (PSI) and Prof. Russell McKenna (ESA and PSI). In your research, you will develop novel methods to represent digitalization in large energy system models. This involves a) a digitalization module that can link to established energy system models (such as TIMES, MERGEE-ETL or similar), and b) to assess spatially- and temporally varying net-benefits of digital technologies (such as artificial intelligence – robotic and agentic AI), digital practices (e.g. teleworking, platormization, virtualization) and digital infrastructures (such as data centers). The project will provide urgently needed evidence for more accurate decisions in energy system planning and contribute to the advancing of co-optimizing digital and energy infrastructures. jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in Pore-Scale Modelling of Multiphase Flow and Reactive Transport Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Position in Pore-Scale Modelling of Multiphase Flow and Reactive Transport 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We are looking for a highly motivated doctoral student to develop advanced numerical models for investigating multiphase flow and reactive transport processes in porous materials. We are offering a doctoral position in the Durability of Engineering Materials research group at ETH Zurich. The group, led by Prof. Ueli Angst, addresses research challenges related to the durability of engineered materials, combining experimental and computational approaches in corrosion science, materials science, porous media, and reactive mass transport. One important research challenge in this field is understanding multiphase transport in porous materials and its role in natural and engineered systems. As liquids move through porous materials, gas can become trapped within the pore space, forming bubbles or irregular gas clusters. These trapped gases can subsequently dissolve, grow, or change in composition, with their evolution closely linked to fluid distribution, mass transport, and chemical reactions. Understanding these processes is important for a wide range of applications, including the durability of construction materials, geological waste containment, CO2 sequestration, and underground energy storage. Job description This doctoral project aims to advance the understanding of multiphase flow and reactive transport in porous media through the development and application of advanced numerical models The research will focus on the evolution of gas and liquid phases in complex pore geometries, considering processes such as gas compressibility, gas–liquid interfacial mass transfer, and (electro-)chemical reactions The successful candidate will develop and apply numerical methods for pore-scale simulations of multiphase flow, coupling fluid dynamics with gas dissolution, diffusion, and reactive transport The research will investigate how gas–liquid interface dynamics and pore geometry influence gas entrapment and evolution The project will build on ongoing research in pore-scale modelling and offer opportunities for collaboration with experimental researchers Profile MSc degree in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related field Strong background in fluid mechanics and numerical methods Good programming skills in Python, C++, or another scientific programming language Strong analytical
