jobs.title: PhD Researcher Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:
PhD Researcher in “A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Culture: Insights from Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Southeast Asia” (Minaret Project), 1.0 FTE.

The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) invites applications for one PhD Researcher (1.0 FTE, 4 years) from September/October 2027 – September/October 2031 to join the Minaret Project, a HORIZON Unit Grant-funded interdisciplinary and transnational research initiative, which examines the interconnection between law, religion and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies to promote democracy and good governance.

The project brings together 11 universities with 15 PhD researchers across 3 work packages and 15 subprojects, with the applicant contributing to the subproject Neo-Imperialism and Constitutional Reform: The Global Dimension. This subproject examines to what extent international organizations and global governance actors act as neo-imperial forces shaping constitutional reform in North Africa and the Middle East.

It will explore how donor-driven “rule of law” and “good governance” programs are developed, interpreted, and implemented in countries such as Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria. Particular attention will be paid to how the legal frameworks promoted by international actors relate to the government practices in these countries, and in particular to those embedded in local traditions and religious values.

Drawing on policy-document analysis and elite interviews with a diverse range of actors -including international advisers, domestic policymakers, civil-society representatives, legal practitioners, religious scholars, and community leaders-, the study will investigate how transnational constitutional models are negotiated, adapted, resisted, or hybridized in practice. It will contribute to debates on postcolonial constitutionalism by examining the processes through which legal and governance norms circulate across borders, as well as the forms of influence, dependency, and agency that shape their adoption.

Ultimately, the project seeks to develop a nuanced account of how external interventions affect perceptions of legitimacy, legal pluralism, and sovereignty in transitional Muslim-majority societies.

What you will do
The PhD researcher will join the Leiden-based Minaret team, working closely with two senior-researchers and two external mentors (one academic and one non-academic, associated with the project). The position provides the opportunity to conduct original empirical research on the underlying structures of constitutional reform in said countries, while also contributing to public engagement and the collaborative life of the project. All PhD researchers are required to undertake two secondments abroad with the project’s associated partners, one academic and one non-academic, of between two and six months' duration. This will not only enhance research capabilities but also equip the PhD researcher for academic and non-academic roles.

Academic Research
  • Conduct socio-legal and policy analysis with key stakeholders in selected countries.
  • Write a doctoral dissertation and co-author academic publications based on qualitative research.
  • Contribute to the project’s comparative framework within the subproject; within the work package (Imperial Genealogies and Constitutional Formation) and between the work packages.


Communications & Engagement
  • Present research findings at events organized by the research project, such as 3 summer schools and 4 training events.
  • Willingness and ability to spend extended periods abroad for fieldwork and 2 secondments.
  • Help organize international workshops, conferences, and events with academic and civil society partners.
  • Contribute to project website and social media accounts.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Law is based in both Leiden and The Hague and, with over 7,000 students and approximately 600 staff members, is one of the largest law faculties in the Netherlands. The faculty is committed to innovative, multidisciplinary research and a constantly evolving curriculum that addresses key societal challenges. Our faculty is large enough to make an impact on both a national and international scale, yet small enough to offer a personal and engaging learning experience. In this way, we contribute every day to a safer and more sustainable world. Impact with law! For more information, please visit https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/law.

The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) is part of the Leiden Law School. The VVI seeks to advance knowledge of the formation and functioning of legal systems in their social contexts, the impact of these systems on society and vice versa, their effectiveness in governance, and their contribution to development. The Institute adopts a socio-legal and global approach, doing research on law in the books and law in action in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. VVI staff teaches several socio-legal thematic and regional courses for both Dutch and foreign exchange students. In addition, VVI provides PhD supervision, advisory services and training courses to policy makers and practitioners. For more information, see www.vvi.leidenuniv.nl.

What you bring
In our team, we are looking for someone who can work independently while also contributing to a collaborative environment. Since every position is unique, we will devote careful attention to your onboarding. If some aspects of the work are new to you, we will identify what support you need and develop a tailored plan for your professional growth.

We do not expect candidates to already have all the qualifications listed below. Training will be provided in areas such as socio-legal studies, research methods, and the specificities of constitutional reform in the Middle East. That said, this position will be a good fit for you if you recognize yourself in many of the following:
  • A MSc or LLM in Anthropology, Political Science, Law, International Studies, International Relations, Development Studies, or a closely related field;
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting empirical research, ideally in the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria);
  • Experience working with (inter)national civil society actors;

  • Familiarity with socio-legal literature and qualitative research methods;
  • Ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary and international research team;
  • Familiarity with one of the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria) is an asset;

What we offer

Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research means inclusive education and research.

jobs.title: PhD Positions on Silicon-Carbide Quantum Networks
jobs.description_html:
Job description
We are recruiting several PhD candidates to join the Taminiau lab in research on quantum networks based on spin defects in silicon carbide (SiC). As a part of the team, you will work alongside scientists to investigate and develop SiC devices that enable fast optical entanglement links and high-fidelity spin-qubit control. The research combines the design and fabrication of nano-photonic SiC devices, with quantum optics experiments to demonstrate small, but scalable, quantum networks for distributed quantum computation, simulations, and communication.

The Taminiau Lab is an international and collaborative group where people from different backgrounds work closely together, share ideas openly, and support each other's development. We value diversity, teamwork, and creating an environment where everyone can contribute and grow.

Requirements
  • You have a MSc in science in (applied) physics, quantum technologies, material science, or a related field.
  • You are highly motivated to work on the nano fabrication and characterization of quantum devices for quantum networks.
  • Relevant experience in device fabrication, nanophotonics and/or experimental quantum physics (e.g. with spins or superconducting systems) are appreciated but not essential.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Nitrogen Valorization in High-Temp Electrochemical Cells (F/M/X)
jobs.description_html:
Sustainable ammonia production is an important challenge in the transition towards a climate-neutral chemical industry. Conventional ammonia synthesis is highly energy intensive and relies predominantly on fossil-derived hydrogen. Electrochemical routes offer the possibility to produce ammonia using renewable electricity while enabling new, decentralized production concepts.

This PhD project will focus on the development of advanced materials, electrodes, and membrane-electrode assemblies for high-temperature electrochemical ammonia synthesis using solid oxide and protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (SOC and PCC technologies). The research will address the electrochemical conversion of nitrogen- and NOx-containing streams towards NH3.

The project will combine catalyst and electrode development with ceramic-cell fabrication, electrochemical testing, product analysis, and advanced materials characterization. Different catalyst integration strategies, including infiltration and exsolution, will be investigated to improve activity, selectivity, and long-term stability. Particular attention will be given to electrode–electrolyte interfaces, reaction mechanisms, and degradation under realistic operating conditions.

This PhD position is part of HyNITROGEN (https://groenvermogennl.org/en/nieuws/e20-3-million-for-hynitrogen-consortium-research-into-sustainable-nitrogen-chemistry) a large national research program within GroenvermogenNL that brings together more than 40 academic and industrial partners to develop sustainable production routes for ammonia and other nitrogen-based chemicals using renewable hydrogen and green electricity.

jobs.title: PhD Position Systematic Derivation of Formal Languages and Their Correctness
jobs.description_html:
From Semantics to Syntax — Systematic Derivation of Formal Languages and Their Correctness   

Job description
Formal languages, such as type theories and program logics, let us state and prove precisely what software should do. Today, each new language is designed by hand: experts invent the syntax, then check that it really means what it should. This is slow, and it has to be redone for every new problem. This project explores a different approach: start from the mathematical meaning of a language and derive the language itself from it, together with a proof that the two match. Several recent type theories were built this way, but each one with its own ad hoc techniques. Together, we want to find out whether there is one general recipe behind them. You will develop this theory using tools from category theory and type theory, and check your results in the Agda proof assistant. You will be supervised by Dr. Benedikt Ahrens in the Department of Software Technology at TU Delft.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • conducting this research, both individually and as part of a team;
  • participating in scientific life at TU Delft and in the Netherlands, for example by attending and organizing seminars;
  • participating in scientific life more globally, including publishing papers and attending workshops and conferences;
  • contributing to teaching in computer science, providing the opportunity to gain teaching experience.

  • Masters degree in mathematics, computer science, or a related field
  • Experience in both category theory and theoretical computer science (e.g., type theory, logic or programming language semantics), or a strong motivation and ability to learn them.
  • Experience with a proof assistant (e.g., Agda, Rocq or Lean) is a plus, but not required.
  • Enjoyment of precise mathematical reasoning,
  • Ability to work independently and to collaborate across the maths/CS boundary;
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Willingness to contribute to, and possibly experience in, student supervision and teaching

jobs.title: PhD Candidate: Psychosocial, Environmental and Economical Impact in Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathies
jobs.description_html:
Welcome to Maastricht University!

How does cardiomyopathy (heart failure in young adults) affect patients beyond their physical health? And how can we better understand how psychosocial and environmental factors, such as stress, obesity and physical activity, influence the disease process and patients’ quality of life and mental well-being? As a PhD candidate, you will use Health Technology Assessment (HTA) methods to study the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy-related complications as well as the role of psychosocial and environmental factors in the disease process, and contribute to evidence on the value and cost-effectiveness of healthcare strategies.

PhD Candidate: Psychosocial, Environmental and Related Economical Impact in Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathies (Heart Failure in Young Adults)
  • Our goal: The goal of this research is to understand how psychosocial and environmental factors influence the cardiomyopathy disease process and related biological changes in the heart, as well as their impact on quality of life, mental well-being and societal burden in young patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. By combining clinical phenotyping, questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, healthcare use, employment and cost data, the project aims to link these factors and biological and clinical findings to better understand, detect, prevent or treat cardiomyopathy complications.
  • Your colleagues & research context: You will join the Heart Failure Research team of Prof. dr. Stephane Heymans at CARIM and Maastricht UMC+ and work within a large Dutch research consortium. You will collaborate with the team of Prof. dr. Jan Y. Verbakel at KU Leuven, Department of Public Health and Primary Care, and work closely with the HTA and health economics group at KU Leuven. The research uses a prospective cohort, biobank and omics of more than 1,300 cardiomyopathy patients. You will be based in Maastricht (CARIM / Maastricht UMC+) and make regular working visits to Leuven. Supervision will take place by both Dr. Stephane Heymans and dr. Verbakel.

The project focuses on Health Technology Assessment (HTA) and on understanding the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy-related complications. An important part of the research is to examine how psychosocial and environmental factors, including factors such as stress, obesity and physical activity, are related to the cardiomyopathy disease process and biological changes in the heart. Using a prospective cohort, biobank and omics, you will integrate clinical phenotyping, questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, biosamples and multi-omics to study cardiomyopathy and associated psychosocial, economical, environmental and behaviourial conditions.

You will link these data to healthcare use, cost, work, quality of life, mental well-being, patient preferences and societal burden to generate evidence for HTA and cost-effectiveness analyses.You will have the freedom to identify their original projects, e.g. where biological findings in the heart (e.g. RNA/protein data) can be linked to psychosocial and environmental factors, as part of the gene-environmental interactions paradigm.

What you do
  • Quantify the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy complications using questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, healthcare use, employment and cost data.
  • Investigate how psychosocial and environmental factors, such as stress, obesity and physical activity, may influence the cardiomyopathy disease process and related biological changes in the heart.
  • Evaluate the value and cost-effectiveness of strategies to detect, prevent or treat cardiomyopathy-related complications in patients with cardiomyopathy, incorporating patient preferences and societal impact.
  • Where relevant and if time allows, and in close collaboration with the molecular research team, translate selected cohort findings into patient-derived iPSC or experimental animal models.

Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you.

What you bring
We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this?

You bring strong analytical and communication skills and enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team. You are motivated to contribute to research at the intersection of clinical, psychosocial and economic perspectives.

Furthermore:
  • You have a Master’s degree in Medicine, AKO arts klinisch onderzoeker.
  • You have interest/experience in health sciences or related fields
  • You have an interest in and/or experience with Health Technology Assessment (HTA), with focus on psychosocial and related economic impact of cardiomyopathy on patients’ lives, including quality of life and patient-reported outcomes.
  • You are familiar with the Northern European and/or Dutch healthcare system.
  • You have experience with, or are willing to learn, statistical software such as R or Stata.
  • You have an excellent command of English and Dutch, both written and spoken, at minimum C1 level (CEFR).

What we offer
At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer:
  • A 12-month contract (1,0 FTE) with the prospect of a 3 year extension based on mutual satisfaction.
  • A gross monthly salary between € 3.204 and € 4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus.
  • 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours.
  • Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home.
  • Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas.
  • A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with.
  • A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities.
  • An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe.

We train healthcare professionals and researchers through innovative educational programmes and conduct groundbreaking research in health and well-being. jobs.title: PhD position: Bacterial packaging of biocatalytic nanofactories
jobs.description_html:
What you will do
With the recent rapid progress in synthetic cells, sometimes known as artificial cells, the toolbox for liposome-encapsulated biocatalyst has massively expanded, creating complex systems that can act as ‘chemical nanofactories’ for biocatalytic cascade reactions. In this PhD project, you will optimise, apply and exploit a new technology in which biocatalysts are ‘packaged’ and confined in lipid vesicles during bacterial expression, which not only massively enriches biocatalyst yields, but also creates a ready-to-go liposome-encapsulated systems.

About the project
This project is a good match if:
  • you are interested in the expression, characterisation and engineering of biocatalysts.
  • you like working in a multidisciplinary team.
  • you are interested in contributing to the field of Synthetic Cells and biotechnology.

What you bring
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who:
  • has a Master’s degree in Life Sciences and Technology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, or a related discipline
  • has experience in cloning, expression, purification and characterisation of biocatalysts, and preferably also in the preparation and analysis of lipid vesicles.
  • has a strong interest in structure-function relationship of enzymes, with proven excellent technical experimental and analytical skills and ability to work independently.
  • has a good proficiency in (scientific) English, and excellent communication skills.
  • feels comfortable working in a collaborative environment.

The Jeuken lab is member of the Macromolecular Biochemistry group in the Leiden Institute of Chemistry, with a shared biochemical lab headed by 8 group leaders. jobs.title: PhD Researcher: Environmental Impacts of Spatial Demographic Change
jobs.description_html:
The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for:
PhD Researcher: Environmental impacts of spatial demographic change

Excited to use geospatial and environmental analysis tools to explore the implications of spatial demographic change for urban planning, resource demand, and the environment?

Key responsibilities
The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance understanding of how spatial population distribution, demographic change (including aging population and smaller households), and urban form jointly shape future resource demand and GHG emissions. The project will evaluate core trade-offs in material and energy requirements and emissions, balancing the efficiency gains of urban density against the rise in vacant buildings and underutilized infrastructure caused by regional depopulation. Ultimately, the research will inform urban and regional development strategies to minimize net land take and GHG emissions, while catering to the needs of changing populations across the rural-urban continuum in Europe.

As a PhD researcher on this project, you will:
  • Develop high-resolution activity demand models for building and transport sectors under future spatially refined scenarios of European demographic change.
  • Integrate activity demand projections with material flow and life-cycle models to quantify future energy requirements, material intensity, and GHG emissions.
  • Evaluate adaptive reuse and circular strategies for vacant buildings and underutilized transport infrastructure in depopulating and/or aging regions.
  • Design integrated spatial planning scenarios combining built environment transformations with transport infrastructure investments to support high wellbeing and low resource/emissions pathways across population change and urban/rural contexts

Where you will work
Leiden University is situated between Amsterdam (36 km) and The Hague (15 km) and was founded in 1575, making it the oldest university in the Netherlands. It houses around 35,000 students originating from 112 nationalities, facilitated by approximately 8,000 staff.

The Institute of Environmental Science (CML) at Leiden University offers a vibrant and supportive community of scientists committed to the challenges of sustainability. CML distinguishes itself for its attention to professional development in coordination with the interests of its scientists. As such, there are plenty of opportunities to learn new skills, expand your knowledge, collaborate across disciplines, and experiment in a friendly environment fully embodying academic freedom across all career levels.

The core focus of CML is to perform research and education in the interdisciplinary field of Environmental Sciences. CML focuses on the sustainable use of natural resources and preservation of natural capital and biodiversity. CML has a culture of mutual support and collaboration between researchers. CML has two Departments: Industrial Ecology (CML-IE) and Environmental Biology (CML-EB). Presently, about 150 fte (including postdocs and PhDs) are employed at CML. CML further collaborates with TU Delft and Erasmus University in the Leiden-Delft-Erasmus Centre for Sustainability (LDE-CfS), and with the Naturalis Biodiversity Centre.

The Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) is positioned in the Faculty of Sciences. The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expanding fundamental knowledge by curiosity and looking beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelor’s and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2.800 staff and almost 6000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

For more information, see www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science. Information about CML can be found at www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/environmental-sciences.

Selection Criteria
  • Masters degree in Sustainability Sciences, Urban Planning, Engineering, Geospatial Science, or related discipline

jobs.title: PhD in Photonic Sensors for Light-Starved Applications
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about cutting-edge semiconductor technology for solving real societal problems? Then this PhD position could be a fit for you. In this project you will push the limit of spectroscopic analysis by developing novel photonic chips working at ultralow light levels (down to femtowatts). These chips will form the core of sensors which are crucial for advancing healthcare and the energy transition.

Information
Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) allows characterizing materials and tissues, and it is widely used in industry. Our group has recently developed integrated spectral sensors, based on an advanced nanophotonic platform. These low-cost spectral chips, already commercialized by our spin-off MantiSpectra, provide detailed spectral information in the spectral region 900-1700 nm and allow measuring materials properties. However, they are based on reflection and therefore require a powerful light source to illuminate the object. Their application could be widely extended if they were sensitive enough to measure light emitted by a sample through fluorescence or Raman scattering. This requires pushing the limit of spectral sensing technology to combine spectral discrimination and detection at the femtowatt/low picowatt level, in a single device. To this aim the project will explore advanced device designs and fabrication methods, and collaborate with other TU/e research groups for the integration with low-noise amplification. The sensors will be fabricated at the NanoLab@TU/e cleanroom facility, using advanced semiconductor equipment. Their application to low-light sensing applications will also be explored during the project, in collaboration with industrial partners.

jobs.title: PhD student: Effect van interventies op luchtkwaliteit in Nederland
jobs.description_html:
Luchtverontreiniging is verantwoordelijk voor ongeveer 80% van de ziektelast. Wereldwijd is blootstelling thuis en op het werk naar schatting verantwoordelijk voor 16% van alle sterfgevallen. In Nederland wordt naar schatting 8,5% toegeschreven aan milieuvervuiling en nog eens 2,7% aan vervuiling op het werk. Het Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS) van de Universiteit Utrecht onderzoekt hoe lokale interventies en bredere maatschappelijke transities de luchtverontreiniging beïnvloeden in praktijkgerichte Living Labs en aan de hand van beschikbare data.

Wat ga je doen?
Je gaat werken aan het NWA-ORC project ExpACT: een onderzoeksproject dat de gezondheidseffecten van luchtverontreiniging onderzoekt. Het project ontwikkelt verbeterde monitoringtechnologieën en methoden die kunnen inspelen op veranderende niveaus en bronnen van luchtverontreiniging. Je onderzoekt hoe interventies en transities in de praktijk de luchtverontreiniging in de ExpACT Living Labs veranderen. Interventies zijn lokale maatregelen, zoals een geluidsscherm langs een spoorlijn of de tijdelijke sluiting van een luchthaven. Ook onderzoek je hoe goed de gebruikte meet- en modelleermethoden deze effecten kunnen vaststellen. In elk Living Lab worden de onderzoeksvragen en methoden doorlopend bijgesteld door middel van co-creatie met relevante belanghebbenden, onder wie inwoners en professionals. Je werkt daarbij nauw samen met de Living Labs en met ExpACT-partners die nieuwe sensoren en apparatuur ontwikkelen. Je integreert hun technologieën en modelleertechnieken in de Living Labs.

In landelijke gebieden, waar veranderingen in de landbouw invloed hebben op de ammoniakuitstoot, gaat het onder meer om uitbreiding van een passief NH3-meetnetwerk, evaluatie van een mobiele NH3-sensor en onderzoek naar de vraag of filters kunnen worden gebruikt om bio-organische deeltjes en pollen te detecteren.

In stedelijke gebieden kan het onderzoek bestaan uit het meten van metalen en mogelijk andere emissies van spoorwegen, en het vaststellen van het effect van een gepland geluidsscherm op deze concentraties.

In Eindhoven onderzoek je het effect van de geplande tijdelijke sluiting van Eindhoven Airport op de concentraties ultrafijnstof. Je bespreekt gedurende het hele project met inwoners en professionals wat er gemeten moet worden, wat de resultaten betekenen en hoe bruikbaar de instrumenten in de praktijk zijn.

Je wordt begeleid binnen het Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS) van de Universiteit Utrecht. Je profiteert van nauwe samenwerking met onderzoekers, onderzoeksinstituten en partners van Living Labs in heel Nederland.

jobs.title: PhD in experimental physics: how do you make the first antimatter molecule?
jobs.description_html:
When a proton meets a hydrogen atom, the pair can emit a photon and stay together as H₂⁺. This is how the first molecules formed after the Big Bang, and it is one of the proposed routes to the first antimatter molecule, yet it has never been measured. In the NWO Vidi project SAMURAI, you will study these collisions one quantum state at a time: instead of colliding atoms, we use lasers to prepare a hydrogen molecule at the moment of a collision and watch it fall apart. You will be part of a small group in which experiment and theory go hand in hand.

Your duties
  • excite H₂ with two tunable extreme-ultraviolet lasers (60–205 nm), built in our lab and unique in the Netherlands, and image the fragments with velocity-map imaging
  • aim for the first spectroscopic observation of the excited electronic states of H₂⁺, calculated by Edward Teller in his PhD thesis in 1930 and never seen since
  • trap H₂⁺ ions and use millimetre waves and magnetic fields to control how they come apart
  • work towards the first measurement of radiative association: joining a cold proton and a cold hydrogen atom with light, next to a crystal of laser-cooled Be⁺ ions
  • compare your data with multichannel quantum-defect theory and scattering calculations, and contribute to the theory yourself if you like
  • develop your skills in lasers and nonlinear optics, ultrahigh vacuum, electronics, CAD design and scientific programming
  • present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed journals

jobs.title: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue
jobs.description_html:
Shape the future of nanoparticle safety and design. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue.

Job description
We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University.

Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles.

Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed.

The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target.

SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package.

As a PhD candidate, you will:
  • Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference.
  • Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up.
  • Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted.
  • Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue.

You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects.

You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster.

The intended start date is January 2027.     

Job requirements
  • MSc in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, systems biology, or a closely related quantitative field.
  • Demonstrated experience building and solving ODE or dynamical systems models.
  • Demonstrated experience with Bayesian inference in a probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro.
  • Strong scientific programming in Python. Please point us to a repository.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.

Preferred qualifications:
  • Continuous optimization or optimal control.
  • Causal inference or counterfactual reasoning.
  • Surrogate modelling, Gaussian processes, or emulation.
  • Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling or systems pharmacology.
  • Experience packaging and documenting scientific software.
  • No background in toxicology, nanomaterials, chemistry or biology is required.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. jobs.title: PhD Position in Neuroimaging, LLM, Genetics and Cross-species comparison
jobs.description_html:
Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison.

The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization.

A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience.

You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining.

You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence.

Your duties
  • analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets
  • develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis
  • investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity
  • integrate genetics with neuroimaging
  • perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution
  • integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities
  • develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks
  • contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows
  • collaborate with researchers within the Connectome Lab, CNCR and international research networks
  • present your findings at national and international scientific meetings
  • write scientific manuscripts
  • contribute to teaching activities where appropriate

jobs.title: PhD: Developing methodological standards for studying the effectiveness of new digital interventions
jobs.description_html:
Join our interdisciplinary team at the Methodology of Educational Science Research Group (CMPO) and the Center for Contextual Psychiatry (CCP) at KU Leuven, one of Europe’s most renowned research universities. The CMPO, part of the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, is internationally recognized for its expertise in advanced statistical modeling and research methodology, encompassing both quantitative and qualitative approaches. Prof. Ginette Lafit leads innovative work to advance quantitative methods in ESM study design and drives methodological innovation in intensive longitudinal research. The CCP, housed within the Department of Neurosciences in the School of Medicine, is an internationally leading research center specializing in Experience Sampling Methodology (ESM) in mental health research. Under the leadership of Prof. Inez Myin-Germeys, the CCP brings together a vibrant group of 25 researchers from diverse backgrounds and is widely recognized for its expertise in designing, implementing, and analyzing experimental studies and clinical trials. You will join the eMotion project, an ambitious long-term research initiative dedicated to developing new interventions for the negative symptoms of psychosis. As a PhD student, you will play a central role in developing a statistical framework for optimizing the design of Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) using Micro-Randomized Trials (MRTs).

Project
This research program uses Virtual Reality (VR) and the Experience Sampling Method (ESM) to examine the approach-avoidance mechanisms underlying amotivation, a core negative symptom of psychosis. A major advancement of the project is developing tailored interventions that combine EMIs with VR technology. As a PhD student, you will play a pivotal role in advancing statistical methodologies to optimize EMI design through MRTs, enhance EMI effectiveness by incorporating data from VR-based tasks, and develop rigorous measures to evaluate the clinical impact of the EMI-VR intervention framework.

Your Responsibilities

  • Apply quantitative methods to analyze ESM data, including time series analysis and multilevel modeling techniques.
  • Develop novel quantitative methods to construct EMIs and advance the EMI-VR integration using MRTs.
  • Write papers for publication in international peer-reviewed journals.
  • Collaborate closely with researchers across three research lines: (i) ESM methodology, statistics, and meta-science, (ii) Person-environment interactions in psychosis, and (iii) Development, efficacy testing, and implementation of Digital Mobile Mental Health.


This position is part of eMotion, a recently funded, large-scale research program aimed at creating new treatments for negative symptoms—among the most challenging aspects of psychiatric care. You will join a dynamic, interdisciplinary team of clinical psychologists, experimental psychologists, psychiatrists, and statisticians in an environment that fosters collaboration and scientific excellence.

Profile
The candidate holds a master’s degree in psychology or a related discipline (e.g., Mental Health, Psychiatry, Social or Health Sciences) and has demonstrated a strong interest in research. Solid experience with quantitative research methods and strong statistical skills are essential. Prior experience with, or knowledge of, the Experience Sampling Method is highly desirable. The candidate should be committed to open‑science practices and possess excellent written and spoken English skills (C1 proficiency level).

Offer
A contract for one year will be offered, which is renewable for another three years after a positive evaluation. Salaries for PhD students are competitive by international standards. The starting date is flexible, but no later than the first of March 2027.

  • Cover Letter (describing your motivation, research career goals, skills, and experience)

  • Diploma and transcripts of records (BSc and MSc)

jobs.title: PhD in Process-Aware Information Systems for Circular Care Pathways
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited about designing digital innovations for sustainable healthcare and eager to support Dutch care organizations in reducing medication waste while ensuring safe and compliant care? Join us as a PhD candidate on the NWO project REMARK.

Information
Healthcare organizations are under increasing pressure to become more sustainable while continuing to deliver safe, high-quality, and compliant care. Circular care pathways offer opportunities to reduce waste and improve resource utilization, but they also introduce new challenges. Healthcare organizations need to track resources across organizational boundaries, ensure compliance with regulations and quality standards, and monitor increasingly complex processes involving multiple stakeholders.

Existing healthcare information systems provide only limited support for monitoring circular processes and demonstrating compliance throughout the care pathway. As healthcare systems transition from linear to circular models, new methods are needed to continuously monitor processes, detect deviations, assess compliance risks, and provide actionable insights to healthcare professionals and managers.

In this PhD project, you will investigate how process-aware information systems can support the monitoring and governance of circular care pathways. You will develop novel methods that use event data and healthcare process information to provide visibility into the execution of care pathways and identify opportunities for improving compliance, transparency, and sustainability. A central goal is to understand how organizations can continuously monitor circular healthcare processes and ensure that circular interventions remain safe and compliant with regulatory requirements.

You will become member of the Information Systems group within the Department of Industrial Engineering & Innovation Sciences at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your work is embedded in the NWO KIC funded REMARK project, in which a multidisciplinary consortium investigates how circular healthcare pathways can be designed and implemented in practice. For this project, you will collaborate with researchers from multiple universities, Dutch healthcare organizations and industry partners, giving you a unique opportunity to achieve both scientific and societal impact.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Verbeterde diagnostiek en kennisdeling voor Multipele Systeem Atrofie'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Multiple systeematrofie (MSA) is een zeldzame en ernstige hersenziekte die zich vaak uit met Parkinsonverschijnselen, maar meestal veel sneller verloopt dan de ziekte van Parkinson. Dit onderzoeksproject probeert in een tweetal samenhangende deelprojecten oplossingen te bieden voor twee problemen rondom de ziekte MSA. Ten eerste: de slechte verspreiding van (nieuwe) kennis omtrent MSA onder professionals; ten tweede: de lange tijd tot aan een diagnose die mensen met MSA ervaren.

Deelproject 1 ‘MSA-Kennisradar’
De meeste neurologen krijgen MSA maar weinig te zien. Daardoor bereiken nieuwe inzichten over het herkennen en vaststellen van MSA hen vaak niet of pas laat. Ook voor neurologen en wetenschappers die gespecialiseerd zijn in bewegingsstoornissen is het moeilijk om alle nieuwe wetenschappelijke informatie bij te houden. De hoeveelheid onderzoek naar MSA groeit snel en de kennis is verspreid over veel verschillende wetenschappelijke publicaties. Met kunstmatige intelligentie (AI) systemen gaan we in dit project op een verantwoorde en veilige manier kennisoverdracht en scholing ontwikkelen omtrent MSA. De kern van dit MSA-kennisradar project is het ontwikkelen van een doorlopend en grotendeels geautomatiseerd proces dat nieuwe wetenschappelijke kennis over MSA omzet in betrouwbare en praktisch bruikbare informatie voor neurologen en wetenschappers op het gebied van MSA.

Deelproject 2: ‘MAESTRO’
In het begin van de ziekte kunnen de klachten van MSA en Parkinson sterk op elkaar lijken. Daardoor is het vaak moeilijk om in een vroeg stadium met zekerheid vast te stellen om welke ziekte het gaat. Het onderscheid is heel belangrijk, omdat mensen met MSA meestal minder goed reageren op de medicijnen die bij Parkinson worden gebruikt. Deze medicijnen kunnen bij mensen met MSA bovendien bijwerkingen veroorzaken. Daarnaast is het zo dat met mensen met MSA hun diagnose vaak pas na vele jaren krijgen. Zij ervaren dit als een van de meest frustrerende aspecten van hun ziekte.

Het doel van de MAESTRO-studie is om biomarkers te vinden waarmee MSA al in een vroeg stadium zo betrouwbaar mogelijk kan worden vastgesteld. We onderzoeken of een combinatie van verschillende meetbare biomarkers hierbij kan helpen, zoals bijvoorbeeld biomarkers in hersenvocht of bloed, zichtbare afwijkingen op een MRI of oogbewegingsstoornissen. We onderzoeken mensen bij wie neurologen denken aan MSA, maar bij wie tijdens het eerste bezoek nog niet met zekerheid kan worden vastgesteld welke aandoening zij hebben. Juist bij deze mensen is in de dagelijkse praktijk behoefte aan aanvullende onderzoeken die de arts kunnen helpen om sneller tot een betrouwbare diagnose te komen. Tijdens het eerste onderzoek bezoek worden verschillende mogelijke biomarkers onderzocht. Daarna volgen we de deelnemers gedurende drie jaar, waarna de klinische diagnose wordt vastgesteld. In de MAESTRO studie onderzoeken we welke biomarkers deze klinische diagnose het beste voorspellen.

Het strekt tot aanbeveling als je naast jouw onderzoek als promovendus bereid bent om gemiddeld één dag in de week als trialarts te werken voor meerdere studies binnen het onderzoekteam. Je beoordeelt of patiënten veilig kunnen deelnemen aan onderzoek en verricht studie-specifieke medische handelingen. Het biedt dus een mooie gelegenheid om je klinische vaardigheden op peil te houden.

jobs.title: PhD position: Optical metasurfaces controlling quantum electron wavepackets
jobs.description_html:
Work Activities
In this project, you will study the fundamental interactions between high-energy electrons and extreme light fields in a scanning electron microscope (SEM). Gaining control over these interactions may lead to new forms of electron microscopy that exploit the quantum-mechanical nature of electron wavepackets. The project uses an emerging technique, photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), in which electrons in a 1-ps-pulsed electron beam exchange energy with a strongly confined optical near field generated by intense laser pulses. This interaction changes the electrons' energy, which in turn modifies the electron wavepacket in space and time, creating, for example, attosecond electron pulse trains. You will develop specially designed non-local optical metasurfaces to control the interaction of the electrons with the strong light fields. Structured 2D dielectrics integrated with nanometer-thin transition-metal dichalcogenide layers, exhibiting strong optical resonances, will be designed to enhance and control the coupling in an ultrafast 1-30 keV SEM.

Your research will include:
  • PINEM and metasurface design (years 1): learn to operate the ultrafast SEM at AMOLF, study PINEM theory and modeling, and design and fabricate metasurfaces in the Amsterdam NanoCenter cleanroom.
  • PINEM-metasurface integration (year 2): measure the electron-light interaction of optimized metasurfaces and tailor electron wavepackets by design, including through two subsequent coherent PINEM interactions.
  • Coherence and entanglement (year 3-4): investigate correlations between electron energy loss and cathodoluminescence, and test a quantum-eraser geometry in which the which-path information is erased.

The project combines the ultrafast electron-light-matter interaction and cathodoluminescence expertise of Prof. Albert Polman (AMOLF) with metasurface design, fabrication and optical characterization expertise of Dr. Jorik van de Groep (University of Amsterdam). You will be based in the Photonic Materials group of Prof. Polman at AMOLF, with close interaction with the 2D Nanophotonics group of Dr. van de Groep at the University of Amsterdam.

Qualifications
We invite applications from highly motivated candidates with a strong background in physics and a keen interest in nanophotonics, quantum physics, nanofabrication and electron microscopy. We especially encourage individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. Prospective PhD candidates must hold an MSc degree in physics or equivalent qualification.

Work environment
Work environment The Photonic Materials group (www.erbium.nl), led by Prof. Albert Polman, studies light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. The group is composed of an international team of PhD students, postdocs and master students that work in a collaborative atmosphere with many social group activities. Every week we hold a group meeting and departmental colloquium and poster sessions. We also regularly organize an international group labtour.

AMOLF provides state-of-the-art ultrafast electron microscopy systems for time-, angle- and polarization-resolved cathodoluminescence spectroscopy and PINEM, and a shared cleanroom for nanofabrication and characterization (Amsterdam NanoCenter). We offer a highly collaborative and supportive environment, fostering strong connections both within the group and with our national and international partners. PhD students benefit from a variety of courses designed to enhance their research skills.

AMOLF is a part of NWO-I and initiates and performs leading fundamental research on the physics of complex forms of matter, and creates new functional materials, in partnership with academia and industry. The institute is located at Amsterdam Science Park and currently employs about 140 researchers and 80 support employees. www.amolf.nl The 2D Nanophotonics lab (https://vandegroeplab.com), led by Dr. Jorik van de Groep, studies nanophotonic metasurfaces that enable active control over light by harnessing the highly tunable optical properties of two-dimensional quantum materials. By combining resonant metallic and semiconductor nanostructures with exciton resonances in 2D semiconductors, we create dynamic metasurfaces that actively tune light emission, scattering, and absorption at the nanoscale. Our group is part of the Institute of Physics at the University of Amsterdam (https://iop.uva.nl) and works in a collaborative atmosphere with other researchers within the department and (inter)national collaborators.

Working conditions
  • The working atmosphere at the institute is largely determined by young, enthusiastic, mostly non-Dutch employees. Communication is informal and runs through short lines of communication.
  • The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment for the duration of four years. The planned start date is December 1, 2026. · The starting salary is 3.115 Euros gross per month and a range of employment benefits.
  • After successful completion of the PhD research a PhD degree will be granted at the University of Amsterdam.
  • Several courses are offered, specially developed for PhD-students.
  • AMOLF assists any new foreign PhD-student with housing and visa applications and compensates their transport costs and furnishing expenses.

More information?
For further information about the position, please contact Albert Polman: a.polman@amolf.nl and Jorik van de Groep: j.vandegroep@uva.nl

Application

Online screening may be part of the selection.

Diversity code
AMOLF is highly committed to an inclusive and diverse work environment: we want to develop talent and creativity by bringing together people from different backgrounds and cultures. We recruit and select on the basis of competencies and talents. We strongly encourage anyone with the right qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, gender, origin, sexual orientation or physical ability.

AMOLF has won the NNV Diversity Award 2022, which is awarded every two years by the Netherlands Physical Society for demonstrating the most successful implementation of equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI).

jobs.title: PhD in Early Modern Religious Debates. The use of AI in analysing sources
jobs.description_html:
In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, in the Low Countries many public religious debates were organized between, for example, Calvinists and Mennonites, or Catholics and Lutherans. Their written reports constitute an underexplored treasure of information about the religious dynamics following the Reformation and the development of a public sphere.

A PhD position is available within the NWO-funded project “In Search of the Truth, in Search of Adherents”. This interdisciplinary project investigates early modern religious debates in the Dutch language.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate early modern religious debates using digital humanities methods and tools. You will analyse how participants drew on classical and ecclesiastical traditions, examining how different religious groups appropriated and used these traditions to support their arguments and distinguish themselves from their opponents. In addition to conducting your own research, you will contribute to the preparation of a critical edition of early modern Dutch-language debates. You will also help develop and refine methods and tools for producing digital critical editions, making them more effective and widely applicable.

You will work closely with a second PhD candidate in the project, whose research focuses on the rhetorical and argumentative strategies employed by participants in religious debates and the role of these debates in the emergence of a public sphere. Together, the two PhD projects will offer complementary perspectives on the practices, intellectual traditions, and wider cultural significance of early modern religious debate. This position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of digital humanities and religious history, combining historical research with the development and application of digital methods. A full description of the project is available upon request.

Duties and Responsibilities
  • Conduct independent research and write a PhD dissertation, as well as academic articles.
  • Contribute to knowledge exchange and public engagement activities.
  • Contribute to the preparation of a critical edition of early modern Dutch-language religious debates.
  • Help develop, refine, and improve methods and tools for producing digital critical editions.
  • Contribute to the activities of the research group, research section, and department.
  • Participate in relevant courses and training offered by the Graduate School and NOSTER.

jobs.title: PhD Position in AI for Software Reuse and Agentic Development
jobs.description_html:
How can AI agents build on existing software instead of reinventing it? Join this collaboration between TU Delft and ING to research more reliable agentic software development.

Job description
Software intensive organizations rely on increasingly large and complex software ecosystems consisting of services, libraries, APIs, frameworks, documentation, and other shared engineering knowledge. Recent advances in generative AI and software engineering agents are changing how software is developed and how developers interact with these ecosystems. TU Delft is collaborating with ING to investigate how we can make enterprise software development more sustainable and reliable in this changing landscape.

We will develop new techniques and tools that help developers and AI agents make better use of existing software and developer knowledge. Our research will combine AI with software repository mining, program and architecture analysis, empirical software engineering, and studies with practitioners. The research will focus on real-world software engineering challenges at ING, while contributing scientific insights and open research results that can benefit the broader software engineering community.

Within this collaboration, we explore two main research directions:

Direction 1: Software Reuse in Enterprise Software Ecosystems

Large organizations invest substantially in reusable software assets. However, as a consequence similar functionality can be implemented independently across teams, increasing fragmentation and long-term maintenance costs. AI-assisted software development makes this challenge even more important: software engineering agents can rapidly generate new code, but may reproduce functionality that already exists elsewhere in an organization.

This direction investigates how software assets are discovered, consumed, adapted, and evolved across large software ecosystems. We will study where opportunities for reuse exist, how software can successfully be adapted across teams, how reusable assets evolve over time, and how developers and AI agents can be guided towards suitable existing software. Ultimately, we aim to develop intelligent techniques that help organizations maximize reuse while reducing unnecessary duplication and maintenance effort.

Direction 2: Reliable Agentic Software Development

AI software engineering agents can increasingly perform tasks such as implementing features, fixing bugs, testing, and refactoring software. Their success, however, depends not only on the underlying AI models, but also on the engineering context available to them. In enterprise environments, relevant knowledge is distributed across source code, documentation, architecture descriptions, requirements, APIs, development history, and organizational practices.

This direction investigates the engineering foundations required for reliable agentic software development. We will study what context agents need for different software engineering tasks, what makes specifications sufficiently complete and precise, how stale or incomplete context and software complexity affect agent performance, and how organizations can determine when tasks can be reliably delegated to AI agents. The goal is to develop techniques and safeguards that enable organizations to integrate increasingly autonomous software engineering agents while maintaining software quality and human oversight.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive research environment and encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their background or experience. We believe that diversity contributes to a more innovative and creative research community. If you do not meet some of the optional requirements listed, we encourage you to still apply and explain how your unique experience and skills can contribute to our research.

Job requirements
Required
  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field
  • Proficiency in the English language

Additional requirements:
  • Research focus, characterized by curiosity, data fluency, and critical thinking
  • Engineering mindset, including ability to create experimental prototypes and demonstrators
  • Team player, good listener, and ready to help

To thrive as a PhD candidate, it’s crucial to have a strong research mindset driven by curiosity and passion for your topic. Reflecting on your motivation for pursuing a PhD trajectory is essential, as this path involves unique challenges and uncertainties inherent to scientific exploration. Success requires dedication, adaptability, the ability to analyze complex problems, manage your time effectively, innovate and stay resilient under pressure. Combined with the ability and willingness to work independently and collaborate well, these qualities are indispensable for a fulfilling PhD journey. These experiences will build you as an independent researcher, expand your professional network, and pave the way for diverse career pave the way for diverse career paths, inside or outside academia.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context.

At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration.

Challenge. Change. Impact!

Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment.

Conditions of employment

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Klinisch en preklinisch onderzoek naar medicamenteuze behandelingen voor gokverslaving'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Sinds de legalisering van online gokken in Nederland in 2021 is er veel aandacht voor de gevolgen van gokproblematiek en de behoefte aan vernieuwende, effectieve behandelingen. In deze studie onderzoeken we veelbelovende medicamenteuze behandelingen voor gokstoornis, waarbij we klinisch onderzoek bij mensen combineren met preklinisch onderzoek in een diermodel.

Voor dit project zoeken wij een ambitieuze en gedreven promovendus die dit onderzoek coördineert en uitvoert. Je werkt samen met een multidisciplinair team van (dier)onderzoekers, klinische experts en ervaringsdeskundigen, binnen een breed onderzoeksconsortium dat zich richt op het verbeteren van de behandeling van gokstoornis.

Als promovendus ben je verantwoordelijk voor de voorbereiding, coördinatie en uitvoering van de studie. Voor de klinische studie onderhoud je contact met de deelnemende verslavingszorginstellingen en coördineer je de werving, dataverzameling en follow-up. Daarnaast draag je bij aan het preklinische onderzoek naar potentiële medicamenteuze behandelingen in een diermodel voor gokstoornis. Je analyseert de verzamelde data met geavanceerde statistische methoden om de effectiviteit van de medicamenteuze behandelingen te onderzoeken en inzicht te krijgen in factoren die de behandeluitkomsten beïnvloeden.

Je vertaalt de onderzoeksresultaten naar wetenschappelijke publicaties en presentaties voor nationale en internationale doelgroepen. Het onderzoek vormt de basis voor je proefschrift en draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van effectievere behandelingen voor mensen met een gokstoornis.

Wij bieden je:
  • Een uitdagend promotietraject waarin je klinisch onderzoek bij mensen combineert met preklinisch dieronderzoek naar nieuwe medicamenteuze behandelingen voor gokstoornis, met daarbij de mogelijkheid om de behandeling van mensen met een gokstoornis direct te verbeteren.
  • Een promotietraject van vijf jaar (60 maanden) voor 0,92 fte.
  • Samenwerking binnen een landelijk, multidisciplinair consortium met toonaangevende onderzoeksinstituten, verslavingszorginstellingen en ervaringsdeskundigen.
  • Ruimte voor wetenschappelijke ontwikkeling, met mogelijkheden om onderzoeksresultaten te publiceren in internationale wetenschappelijke tijdschriften, deze te presenteren op (inter)nationale congressen en bij te dragen aan (postacademische) onderwijsprogramma's.

jobs.title: PhD in Bioreactor-based preservation of human heart valves
jobs.description_html:
• Are you fascinated by the potential of maintaining heart valves outside of the human body?
  • Are you eager to contribute to better and sustainable healthcare at the interface of engineering and biology?
  • Are you passionate about inspiring and mentoring students and working in a high-end collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment?
  • Are you our next PhD candidate in bioreactor-based preservation of human heart valves?

Information
The Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) is seeking a highly talented, ambitious and passionate PhD candidate to investigate and further develop our model of heart valve preservation. We aim to develop a way to keep heart valves alive outside of the human body using dynamic bioreactors where the valves open and close as they do in the human body. As the successful candidate, your research with us will contribute to broader efforts to culture living cardiac tissues and to study their function and their response to immune cells and immune protective technology, closely aligned with our BIOSHIELD consortium funded by the Dutch Heart Foundation. Our group’s research concentrates on developing and improving heart valve replacements in young children born with congenital heart disease. The current valve replacement options available in clinical practice cannot adapt to the growing heart of a child and can elicit immune responses that destroy and calcify implanted valves. Therefore, these young patients require multiple invasive operations throughout their lives. We investigate how to develop a living valve that can grow with the heart and is safe from immune rejection. Alongside our advances in in-situ tissue engineering of heart valves, we investigate strategies for immune shielding and culture of living human donor heart valves as an alternative approach. An essential step in moving this approach forward is to maintain and preserve heart valves outside the human body. In this project, we will focus on extended culture and preservation of donor valves, unravelling valve homeostatic maintenance, and translating this knowledge into smart culture conditions and bioreactor designs with feedback options. This presents an exciting engineering challenge: designing systems that can reproduce the complex flow conditions, pressures, and mechanical stimuli experienced by heart valves in the human body. By combining mechanical design, fluid dynamics, and biomedical engineering, we aim to develop innovative bioreactor technologies.

You will generate unprecedented experimental data as a pioneer in the field to unravel the conditions for optimal ex vivo cardiovascular tissue preservation. Your investigations will build upon our track record on bioreactor design for tissue-engineered heart valves and in-house expertise with heart perfusion models to build a system that can maintain heart valves viable outside of the human body.

To that end, your research will include a selection of techniques including: i) flow-based bioreactor development, ii) sterile vessel and tissue culture, and iii) sophisticated tissue analysis including advanced microscopy. You are expected to write a doctoral thesis and publish your research results in scientific journals. A small part of your doctoral position will involve teaching in courses as well as the supervision of students at the bachelor’s and master’s levels offered by the group. Also, an educational and professional development program will be offered to you.

You will be embedded in a highly inspiring research environment, both socially and professionally, which facilitates access to high-end research facilities, as well as fosters interdisciplinary collaborations. You will be an integral member of the Soft Tissue Engineering and Mechanobiology (STEM) group of the Department Biomedical Engineering, and specifically operate at the interface of the teams led by Assistant Professor dr Marijn Peters (Translational Engineering for Pediatric Cardiovascular Regeneration) and Professor Carlijn Bouten (Cell-Matrix Interactions for Cardiovascular Regeneration) at the Department of Biomedical Engineering at TU/e. You will also work together with the team of Julie Legrand (Mechanical Engineering) and Assistant Professor Marcel Rutten (Cardiovascular Biomechanics) to build upon their work on Soft Robotics Systems, Biomechanical models, and Vascular Bioreactors.

Your project is aligned with our BIOSHIELD consortium of the Hartstichting: BIOengineering immune Shielded Heart valve Implants: Engineering Living Donor tissue by translating prenatal protection mechanisms from the womb to the heart. In this consortium, we work together with cardiothoracic surgery and transplantation immunology at the University Medical Center Utrecht and the Wilhelmina Children’s Hospital and the ETB-Bislife Multi Tissue Center. We stimulate and foster cross-institutional collaborations as part of the project.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Movement Ecology
jobs.description_html:
Climate change is affecting ecosystems, species, populations and individuals worldwide. This project will link unique long-term individual tracking data with remote sensing products and explore the dependence of waterfowl on small to intermediate water bodies throughout the year, focussing on the availability of freshwater as a key requirement for survival and reproduction.

Freshwater availability is a key determinant of life on earth, yet climate change is rapidly altering hydrological systems worldwide. Migratory waterbirds are particularly sensitive to these changes because they depend on water bodies at multiple sites along their flyway. While the role of waterbodies in shaping spring migration of waterbirds is relatively well understood, its importance during breeding, autumn migration and winter periods remains largely unexplored.

The aim of this project is to fill this gap and quantify how changes in freshwater availability influence movements throughout the annual cycle, identifying feedbacks between hydrological conditions and waterbird behaviour. The greater white-fronted goose (Anser albifrons), one of the most abundant goose species wintering in the Netherlands, will serve as a model species. The project builds on a unique long-term dataset comprising GPS tracks of more than 200 individuals collected since 2013 and which is continuously expanding.

The following research questions are central to this project:
  1. How do greater white-fronted geese adjust their movement decisions in relation to snow cover and freshwater availability in their Arctic summer ranges?
  2. Which water bodies do greater white-fronted geese use for resting during autumn migration and how is this influenced by water availability and breeding success?
  3. What is the effect of yearly temperature changes on freshwater roost availability and the movement of greater white-fronted geese during winter?

You will curate and analyse GPS tracking data, integrate them with remotely sensed environmental datasets, and develop statistical models to understand the ecological processes underlying the year-round movements of geese. You will also participate in BSc and MSc teaching activities. Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.

jobs.title: PhD Position Sensing Viscosity with Ultrasound
jobs.description_html:
Develop innovative ultrasound technology to measure the viscosity of flowing fluids in real time. Work closely with the University of Twente and leading industry partners to advance more efficient industrial processes, reduce waste and enable more precise medical applications.

Job description
Many industrial and medical processes rely on accurate, continuous measurements of fluid properties, such as flow rate and viscosity. These measurements are essential in the production of food, medicines and semiconductor products, as well as in environmental monitoring and medical infusion systems for neonatal care. Reliable, real-time measurements provide immediate insight into processes, helping manufacturers maintain product quality, detect deviations and prevent waste caused by production errors. In this way, better fluid measurement contributes to more efficient manufacturing, improved healthcare and sustainable food production.

In this PhD project, you will develop innovative, modular and scalable flowmeters that measure both flow rate and viscosity using ultrasonic surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensing. Although SAW-based sensing principles are already known, the mechanisms behind viscosity measurements are not yet fully understood or commercially applied in ultrasonic flowmeters. Your research will help establish the principles needed for accurate, quantitative measurements.

You will work at TU Delft in close collaboration with the University of Twente and leading companies in flow sensing. Combining theoretical modelling with experimental research, you will investigate how ultrasonic waves interact with flowing fluids and translate your findings into new measurement strategies and sensor designs.

Your responsibilities
As a PhD-researcher you will:
  • Investigating ultrasonic sensing principles and the relationship between fluid flow, viscosity and surface acoustic waves.
  • Developing novel measurement strategies for quantitatively determining the viscosity of flowing fluids.
  • Building a model of the sensing principles and validating it through experiments.
  • Designing and developing an experimental platform for ultrasound-based sensing.
  • Characterising propagation losses, quality factors, wave travel speeds and resonance behaviour.
  • Identifying optimal excitation frequencies to improve measurement accuracy and signal-to-noise ratio.
  • Publishing your findings in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at international conferences and writing your PhD thesis.
  • Contributing to education, for example by supervising MSc students.

Your work environment
You’ll be part of the Dynamics of Micro and Nanosystems (DMN) section within department of Precision and Microsystems Engineering (PME) of the faculty of Mechanical Engineering. The section studies and develops small-scale systems that move, aiming to better understand their physical properties and use this knowledge to drive future innovations. Its research combines fundamental scientific investigation with close collaboration with industry. You’ll have access to several research facilities that will support your research.

At DMN, you'll find an open and friendly environment, with opportunities for professional development and training to successfully develop your academic skills. We do not distinguish between hierarchical levels, and we have a strong collaborative culture. We interact daily and share a drive to strengthen the position of the group as a whole thanks to the growth of each member.
