jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Paediatric Mucosal Immunology
jobs.description_html:
Job description
Understanding mucosal immune protection against respiratory infections in children
Are you interested in understanding how the immune system protects children against respiratory infections?

Respiratory tract infections are among the most common causes of illness in children worldwide. While most children recover without complications, some experience frequent or severe infections. Why are certain children more susceptible than others, and how can we improve protection against respiratory pathogens?

Most immunological research and diagnostic approaches focus on immune responses measured in blood. Yet respiratory pathogens first encounter the immune system at the mucosal surfaces of the airways. Understanding immune protection at these surfaces may offer new opportunities for preventing and treating respiratory infections.

The Paediatric Respiratory Infection & Immunity Group at Radboudumc is looking for an enthusiastic and curious PhD candidate. Our ambition is to unravel the mechanisms underlying mucosal immune protection and translate these insights into new strategies to prevent respiratory infections in children.

Your research
We investigate how mucosal antibodies protect against respiratory pathogens and how local immune cells, including innate lymphoid cells, contribute to the generation and maintenance of these antibodies.

As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to understanding why mucosal antibody responses differ between children and how these differences relate to susceptibility to respiratory infections.

Your work will include:
  • Characterising mucosal antibody responses in children with recurrent respiratory tract infections and healthy controls.
  • Investigating the diversity and polyreactivity of mucosal IgA and IgG.
  • Studying associations between mucosal immune characteristics and clinical susceptibility to respiratory infections.
  • Exploring the cellular and tissue environments that support mucosal antibody production.
  • Integrating immunological, clinical and, where applicable, multi-omics data to identify the mechanisms underlying mucosal immune protection.

You will work with well-characterised paediatric cohorts and biological samples collected through established research collaborations in the Netherlands, South Africa and the Dutch Caribbean.

The project combines clinically relevant research questions with advanced immunological approaches and offers opportunities to develop expertise in mucosal immunology, translational research and quantitative data analysis.

What we offer
  • A PhD position within a funded research programme at Radboudumc.
  • A stimulating and supportive multidisciplinary research environment.
  • Close supervision and opportunities for scientific and professional development.
  • Access to established clinical cohorts and advanced immunological research infrastructure.
  • Opportunities for international collaboration and, where relevant, research visits to partner institutions.
  • The opportunity to contribute to research connecting fundamental immunology with clinical challenges in paediatric respiratory infections.

jobs.title: PhD in Dynamic CO₂ Capture and Conversion with Intermittent Renewable Power
jobs.description_html:
Can you help turn CO₂ from the air into a renewable carbon resource? Join us to develop electrically heated reactors that combine direct air capture with CO₂ conversion—and work effectively with a fluctuating renewable electricity supply.

Information
Europe’s ambition for a fossil-fuel-free chemical industry calls for new ways to produce chemicals and fuels from circular carbon and green hydrogen. Renewable electricity creates exciting opportunities for electrification, but its intermittency challenges conventional process design. Within CO2URAGE, universities and industrial partners will develop intensified, electrified processes to produce syngas, methane, or methanol from CO₂ captured from air, biomass, or other circular sources.

This PhD position focuses on designing and operating electrified, structured packed-bed reactors for direct air capture and integrated CO₂ conversion under changing renewable power availability. Your central challenge is to maintain efficient capture, sorbent regeneration, and heat recovery as the available electrical power varies. Capturing CO₂ from air requires processing large air volumes, while regenerating the sorbent requires efficient heat supply. How can we design compact reactors that combine low pressure drop, rapid heating and cooling, and effective heat recovery?

You will investigate how 3D-printed reactor structures and resistive or inductive heating can improve heat management and reduce the electricity required to release captured CO₂. You will then explore the integration of sorbent regeneration with CO₂ hydrogenation to methane or syngas. Combining capture and conversion offers opportunities to use reaction heat, simplify processing, and improve overall energy efficiency.

You will combine reactor modeling and laboratory experiments to:
  • Design and test 3D-printed, electrically heated reactors for direct air capture.
  • Optimize capture cycles and heat recovery under fluctuating electricity supply and ambient conditions.
  • Explore integrated CO₂ capture and hydrogenation through modelling and proof-of-concept experiments.

The central scientific challenge is to understand how reactor structure, local heat supply and dynamic operation interact—and use that understanding to design energy-efficient capture and conversion processes.

You will pursue your PhD at Eindhoven University of Technology under the supervision of Prof. Martin van Sint Annaland. Within CO2URAGE’s work package Electrification of Direct Air Capture and Conversion, you will collaborate with researchers at the University of Twente and Delft University of Technology, as well as industrial partners. Your reactor research will connect directly with program activities in process control, system integration, and techno-economic and environmental assessment.

jobs.title: PhD Researcher in Legal and ethical perspectives in data-driven technologies in healthcare
jobs.description_html:
We are inviting prospective researchers to apply for a PhD position led by Dr. Mahsa Shabani. This position offers a unique opportunity to work on an interdisciplinary project at the intersection of law, ethics, and technology. The candidate will have the opportunity to shape their own research plan within the broader VIDI project.

Join our team!
Artificial intelligence and genomics technologies are transforming healthcare, offering powerful tools for diagnosis and treatment. Yet, these innovations often fail to serve diverse populations fairly, which can reinforce existing inequalities. Current regulatory frameworks lack a comprehensive approach to fairness, often focusing narrowly on anti-discrimination measures while overlooking broader socio-ethical considerations. This PhD project would focus on building a multidimensional conception of fairness in medical AI and genetics, integrating technical, clinical, ethical, and legal perspectives. The project will employ a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical studies (including focus group studies and Delphi studies) to assess the real-world implications of fairness in data-driven healthcare. The PhD project is within the NWO-VIDI project Fairness in Data-Driven Medical Technologies: Solidifying Regulatory Oversight Based on a Multidimensional Conception of Fairness.

What are you going to do
  • Design the scope of the individual PhD research project, and fine-tune the research questions and methodology together with the whole project team;
  • Engage autonomously in - as well as collaborate on - the collection, coding and analysis of data, through doctrinal/literature research, conceptual analysis, focus groups and Delphi study;
  • Present intermediate research results in internal discussions and at workshops and conferences;
  • Contribute to project activities, such as organizing stakeholder meetings, academic events and outreach; and communication of research results to relevant communities of academics, practitioners and policy makers; and
  • Optionally, and in mutual agreement with the project leader and in line with the teaching needs of the Health Law group, have teaching responsibilities.

What do you have to offer
You have:
  • (or are about to obtain) a master’s degree in law (with a focus on health law or technology law) or bioethics /philosophy. A background in both philosophy / bioethics and law is an advantage.
  • interest (and ideally experience) in conducting multi-method empirical and legal research;
  • interdisciplinary interest in issues on the intersection of law, ethics, and technology (bridging technical, ethical, and legal domains);
  • experience with conducting academic research and academic writing in English;
  • demonstrable team working skills;
  • excellent command of English, both orally and written;
  • interest in broader dissemination of your research findings in the public debate.
  • familiarity with EU regulations (AI Act, MDR, GDPR & EHDS) is an asset;

Your salary ranges from €3,204 (in year 1) to €4,051 (in year 4) based on a 38-hour working week. This amount excludes 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% end-of-year bonus. The CAO Nederlandse Universiteiten (CAO NU) applies.

jobs.title: PhD position in organisational science and cybersecurity
jobs.description_html:
For our NWO-funded project “From ‘what went wrong’ to ‘what works well?’ Using Safety 2 principles to develop new cybersecurity solutions”, we are looking for a PhD candidate interested in building positive cybersecurity solutions for organisations. In this five-year project, we aim to develop cybersecurity solutions that organisations can implement in their ways of working based on what we learn from organisations where cybersecurity is managed successfully. The main research question the team will answer is: “What do successful organisations do differently on the individual, team, and organisational level to prevent the occurrence of cyber incidents or reduce their impact?” This position focuses on the organisational level of the main research question.

What you will do
The successful applicant will work with researchers from the cybersecurity governance and the governance of crisis research group to help answering this question. Knowledge of (organisational) cybersecurity at the start of the project is not a requirement. However, we do expect the successful applicants to quickly familiarise themselves with the field through self-study or by taking in-house courses. The successful applicant will conduct empirical research on what successful organisations do differently on the organisational level. Is it the structure, power dynamics or perhaps the communication between departments that warrants success? Or can other factors be found that explain what organisations could do differently to improve their cybersecurity?

Where you will work
ISGA is a scientific institute specializing in security, safety, and global challenges. These include challenges in the fields of cybersecurity, crises, intelligence, terrorism, war, violence, and diplomacy. ISGA is characterized by high-quality, interdisciplinary education and the development of scientific knowledge with a high potential for societal impact. ISGA is part of the Faculty of Governance and Global Affairs (FGGA) and is based in the city of The Hague, the international city of peace and justice. FGGA is one of the seven faculties of Leiden University. This young, entrepreneurial, innovative organization has three scientific institutes, two centers, over 3,700 students, and 425 staff members. For more information about the faculty, click here.

The interdisciplinary Cybersecurity Governance research group works on the non-technical side of cybersecurity at all levels of society. This includes the cybersecurity of end-users in organisations, regulation on the national and international level, but also international relations and diplomacy. The group consists of scientists with a range of different background including psychology, criminology, public administration, philosophy, political science, sociology and law. These different backgrounds are used to create collaborations to understand how we can improve cybersecurity on both the national and international level.

What you bring
In this team, we are looking for someone who can work independently. Every job is different, so in the beginning we will devote attention to your onboarding. If some of the work activities are new to you, we will look together at what you need, and draw up a development plan. This position is a good fit for you if you recognise yourself in the following:

jobs.title: PhD position in Atmospheric Sciences (Trace Gas Observations)
jobs.description_html:
Trace gases are important constituents of Earth’s atmosphere impacting on climate, the ozone layer and human health. In this project you will perform analysis of trace gas mixing ratio observations from the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. You will mainly rely on data from the long-term passenger aircraft project IAGOS-CARIBIC, which deployed scientific instrumentation during regular passenger flights over more than a decade. The dataset has been used to derive climatologies of trace gases in the upper troposphere and lowermost stratosphere, and it was found to be largely representative for that purpose. In this project, you are going to focus on special events that are characterized by unusual trace gas mixing ratios, in particular long-lived greenhouse gases but also other tracers. The aim is to identify and characterize such events, understand their origin and the meteorological processes causing them, as well as their likelihood and impacts.

What are you going to do?

The focus of this project is on data analysis, during the course of the project there may also be options for experimental work (airborne trace gas measurements, laboratory analysis of flask samples), depending on a candidate’s interests and background.

PhD candidates are expected to spend 10% of their working hours on teaching.

jobs.title: PhD position in micro- and nanoplastic research
jobs.description_html:
Bio-based and biodegradable materials are promising alternatives to fossil-based plastics, but how safe and sustainable are they? In this interdisciplinary PhD project, you will connect analytical chemistry and toxicology to investigate how these future plastics break down, characterize the resulting micro- and nanoplastics and leachates, and assess their potential human health effects. Your findings will contribute directly to the Safe and Sustainable by Design of next-generation plastics.

Your job
In this PhD project, you will investigate whether new bio-based and degradable plastics are truly safe and sustainable alternatives to conventional fossil-based plastics. You will follow these materials throughout their entire degradation process: from changes in the original plastic to the formation and identification of micro- and nanoplastics and chemical leachates, and ultimately to their potential effects on human health. Your research will combine analytical chemistry, materials characterization and in vitro toxicology.

You will:
  • Investigate plastic degradation by exposing pristine polymers and plastic products to controlled food-contact and environmental conditions, studying changes in their chemical composition, physical properties and material integrity;
  • Characterize polymer degradation products, including micro- and nanoplastics, dissolved compounds and leachates, using complementary analytical techniques such as infrared microspectroscopy, atomic force microscopy (AFM), AFM-IR, electron microscopy and mass spectrometry;
  • Assess potential human health hazards of plastic materials and their degradation products using a tiered in vitro testing strategy, starting with screening for cytotoxicity, oxidative stress and endocrine activity;
  • Investigate higher tier biological effects and mechanisms of toxicity using human-relevant cell models, including intestinal, liver, immune and neuronal systems, to study particle uptake, biological barrier integrity, inflammation, metabolism and neurotoxicity;
  • Integrate chemical and toxicological findings to establish relationships between polymer composition, degradation behavior and biological effects, translating these insights into actionable recommendations for Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD).

A unique aspect of this position is that you will work across two research environments at Utrecht University. You will spend roughly half of your time at the Institute for Sustainable and Circular Chemistry (ISCC) and half at the Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS). Rather than conducting chemistry and toxicology as separate components, you will actively connect them: toxicological observations can trigger further chemical analysis, while insights into degradation and composition will guide toxicological experiments. In this way, you will serve as a scientific bridge between the two institutes. You will also collaborate closely with researchers from chemistry, materials science and toxicology, as well as the broader interdisciplinary BIOSTAR-SSbD consortium and its academic, societal and industrial partners. Through this environment, you will develop a unique interdisciplinary scientific profile at the interface of analytical chemistry, micro- and nanoplastics research, toxicology and sustainable materials design.

jobs.title: PhD position RSO TraFFIC - AI and Space Domain Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
The University of Groningen (UG) partners in the national project Resident Space Object Tracking For Fusion, Inference, and Characterisation (RSO TraFFIC). It aims to improve the tracking and characterisation of objects in Earth orbit. The Groningen contribution is led by Dr Gijs Verdoes Kleijn of the Kapteyn Astronomical Institute and Dr Eduardo Balbinot (Center for Information Technology and Kapteyn Astronomical Institute).

The 2.6 Meur 6 year project brings together the universities of Delft, Groningen, Leiden and Radboud, the Royal Netherlands Aerospace Centre (NLR) and the space companies Dunedain and Ecosmic.

Modern society depends on space-based infrastructure, but Earth’s orbit is becoming increasingly crowded: about 40,000 objects are catalogued, two-thirds of all spacecraft ever launched have gone up in the past seven years, and more than a million untrackable fragments between one and ten centimetres—each large enough to destroy a satellite—are in orbit. This makes it more difficult to monitor what is happening in space and to prevent collisions.

The RSO TraFFIC project will address these challenges by combining data from different sensors and developing new sensing techniques and algorithms to track objects and examine the legal and governance frameworks needed to manage Earth orbit as a shared resource in a safe, sustainable and responsible way.

What are you going to do?

The Groningen team leads the project’s work on data management and AI-based analysis. You will do PhD research into adapting astronomical AI foundation models to recognise asteroids, comets and satellite trails in telescope images and extract signals from rapid brightness measurements. These capabilities will be built into General Open Orbital Dynamics platform, an open-science platform developed jointly by Delft University of Technology and the University of Groningen (Dirkx et al 2026). This platform will serve as the project’s central data and analysis hub and is hosted at the university’s OmegaCEN Astronomical Science Data Center using the UG's Center for Information Technology research data-handling facilities. The PhD project is planned to start around January 2028.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Computational Design and Fabrication of Adaptive 3D-Printed Structures
jobs.description_html:
Help shape the future of products that sense and adapt to the human body, using multi-material 3D printing and computational design.

Job description
Many products that support or interact with people need structures that do more than carry loads: they must respond reliably to changing forces and patterns of use. Multi-material additive manufacturing makes it possible to integrate different mechanical and functional behaviours within a single structure. Yet designing structures that combine load-bearing performance with embedded sensing and controlled adaptation remains a major challenge. Addressing it calls for new ways to connect geometry, material behaviour and manufacturing with the needs of people who use the resulting products.

In this PhD, you will develop and investigate computational design approaches for multi-material 3D-printed structures. You will explore how geometry, material distribution, electronics functions and manufacturing parameters can be designed together to achieve desired structural and functional behaviour. You will also design and fabricate prototypes that incorporate sensing and geometry-driven mechanisms for adaptation. Combining computational modelling with hands-on experiments, you will evaluate structural behaviour, sensing performance and durability under static and cyclic loading. You will interpret the results, refine design methods, integrate promising concepts into demonstrators, and communicate your findings through scientific publications and presentations.

Your research will include:
  • Developing fabrication-aware computational workflows for lattice geometries and multi-material layouts.
  • Designing and making 3D-printed prototypes to investigate load-bearing, sensing and adaptive behaviour.
  • Using computational modelling and experiments to evaluate stiffness, deformation, sensing and actuation performance, and durability.
  • Integrating and validating concepts in demonstrators, including a wheelchair cushion to evaluate sitting pressure redistribution and user comfort.

You will be part of the Materializing Futures group in the Department of Sustainable Design Engineering, Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering, supervised by Dr. Mehmet Özdemir and Dr. Wolf Song. You will have access to the faculty’s digital fabrication facilities and the Comfort Lab, and collaborate with experts in ergonomics, and smart materials, as well as industry partners.

Job requirements
We look for candidates who have:
  • A Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Industrial Design Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field
  • Hands-on experience with 3D printing and with building and testing physical prototypes
  • Experience with computational or parametric design (e.g. Rhino/Grasshopper, Python)
  • Strong interest in combining mechanics, materials, electronics, and human factors, and in research with sound experimental design
  • Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team, communicate effectively and take initiative
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English

Desirable experience:

Experience with sensors and basic electronics for sensor readout and control (e.g. Arduino), finite element analysis, soft robotics or user studies, and prior publications are assets but not requirements.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)

Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Matching the evolution of people with the speed of the revolution of technology. This is the focus of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering (IDE). IDE is a leader in design research across the application areas of mobility, sustainability and health, as well as its development of design tools and methods. A 350-strong research team and over 2,000 students work together in our inspiring hall, labs and studios.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Additional information

jobs.title: PhD position Placing the Local Group in a cosmological context
jobs.description_html:
Understanding how our Milky Way and its nearest neighbors formed is a central theme of modern Astrophysics, and one for which our group at the University of Groningen has worldwide recognition. The field of Galactic Archaeology uses the detailed fossil record of stars in our Galaxy, M31 and their satellites to reconstruct this history. It is currently undergoing a revolution thanks to the Gaia satellite and to massive spectroscopic surveys. However, we are currently missing sufficiently realistic cosmological simulations to fully interpret and exploit these datasets. Thanks to a recent development by our international team, producing such very realistic analogues of the Milky Way and M31 is within reach. Such high-resolution cosmological simulations of the evolution of gas, stars and dark matter with state-of-the-art codes, will allow us to quantitatively link the observed spatial, dynamical, and chemical structure of the Milky Way and M31 to their assembly history and environment and provide new tests of the standard cosmological model. 

What are you going to do?

Co-develop the most sophisticated suite of cosmological models of the Local Group galaxies to-date. Using the initial conditions provided by our new technology, you will carry out and analyze hydrodynamical simulations of the formation of the Local Group. By comparing these with observational datasets, you will identify mechanisms at play and establish where the models need improvement, make predictions to be tested observationally and envision new tests of the cosmological model. The project will be jointly supervised by prof. Amina Helmi at the University of Groningen and Dr Ruediger Pakmor from the Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics in Garching (Germany). Furthermore, you will be part of an international collaboration that also includes colleagues in Paris and Stockholm.

jobs.title: Promovendus Voeding, metabolisme en immuunrespons bij periampullaire tumoren
jobs.description_html:
Welkom bij de Universiteit Maastricht!
Hoe beïnvloeden voeding, metabolisme en het immuunsysteem de respons op de behandeling van periampullaire tumoren? En hoe kunnen we deze kennis inzetten om de behandeling beter af te stemmen op de individuele patiënt?

Binnen dit promotietraject onderzoek je de wisselwerking tussen de tumor en de patiënt (tumor-host interactie). Je combineert patiëntgebonden onderzoek met translationeel laboratoriumonderzoek en werkt mee aan innovatieve studies op het gebied van voeding, inflammatie en het functioneren van het immuunsysteem. Zo draag je bij aan nieuwe inzichten die de behandeling en zorg voor patiënten met periampullaire tumoren verder kunnen verbeteren.

Promovendus Voeding, metabolisme en immuunrespons bij periampullaire tumoren

Ons doel: Periampullaire tumoren, waaronder alvleesklierkanker, behoren tot complexe aandoeningen waarbij de behandeling en prognose niet alleen worden bepaald door de eigenschappen van de tumor. Ook de conditie, voedingstoestand, stofwisseling en immuunrespons van de patiënt spelen een belangrijke rol.

Vanuit de vakgroep Chirurgie van het Maastricht UMC+ en het Chirurgielaboratorium van het Maastricht University doen we onderzoek naar deze wisselwerking. Ons doel is beter te begrijpen welke factoren de respons op behandeling beïnvloeden en hoe we deze kennis kunnen vertalen naar meer gepersonaliseerde zorg. Binnen dit promotietraject onderzoek je deze vraagstukken vanuit zowel een klinisch als fundamenteel perspectief.

Jouw collega’s: Je maakt deel uit van een multidisciplinair team van klinische en fundamentele onderzoekers binnen de vakgroep Chirurgie en het onderzoeksinstituut NUTRIM (Institute of Nutrition and Translational Research in Metabolism). Je werkt nauw samen met chirurgen, medisch oncologen, MDL-artsen, pathologen en andere onderzoekers binnen het MUMC+. Daarnaast bouw je contacten op met onderzoekers en zorgprofessionals van andere Nederlandse en mogelijk ook internationale ziekenhuizen. De combinatie van klinisch en fundamenteel onderzoek bied je de mogelijkheid om vanuit verschillende disciplines naar complexe medische vraagstukken te kijken. Je wordt begeleid door ervaren klinische en fundamentele onderzoekers.

Wat jij doet
Als promovendus lever je een belangrijke bijdrage aan het onderzoek naar de rol van voeding, metabolisme en het immuunsysteem bij periampullaire tumoren. Je werkzaamheden vinden zowel in de kliniek als in het laboratorium plaats.

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:
  • Uitvoeren van klinische en patiëntgebonden metingen en verzamelen van relevante onderzoeksgegevens.
  • Opzetten en uitvoeren van experimenten in het Chirurgielaboratorium. Heb je nog geen ervaring met bepaalde laboratoriumtechnieken? Dan word je hierin begeleid en opgeleid.
  • Opzetten en beheren van een biobank met bloedmonsters en bijbehorende klinische gegevens van patiënten.
  • Samenwerken met andere Nederlandse ziekenhuizen waar pancreasoperaties worden uitgevoerd en bijdragen aan de uitbreiding van de biobank, waar mogelijk ook internationaal.
  • Analyseren en interpreteren van onderzoeksresultaten en bijdragen aan wetenschappelijke publicaties.
  • Presenteren van onderzoeksresultaten tijdens nationale en internationale bijeenkomsten.
  • Bijdragen aan het onderwijs en de begeleiding van studenten.

Je krijgt de ruimte om je gedurende vier jaar te ontwikkelen tot zelfstandig onderzoeker en je wetenschappelijke vaardigheden verder te versterken.

Ben jij nieuwsgierig naar de wisselwerking tussen tumorbiologie, voeding en het menselijk immuunsysteem? En wil je met jouw onderzoek bijdragen aan betere en meer gepersonaliseerde zorg? Dan ontmoeten we je graag!

Wat jij meebrengt
Je bent nieuwsgierig, onderzoekend en gemotiveerd om bij te dragen aan vernieuwend medisch-wetenschappelijk onderzoek. Je werkt nauwkeurig, neemt initiatief en voelt je thuis in een multidisciplinaire omgeving waarin klinisch en fundamenteel onderzoek samenkomen.

Het maakt ons niet uit of je vanuit een medische of biomedische achtergrond komt. Belangrijk is dat je gemotiveerd bent om de verbinding te leggen tussen wetenschappelijk onderzoek en patiëntenzorg. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in een van de volgende opleidingsprofielen:

Heb je Geneeskunde gestudeerd?
  • Je hebt een afgeronde master Geneeskunde.
  • Je hebt affiniteit met wetenschappelijk onderzoek.
  • Ervaring met laboratoriumtechnieken is een pré. Heb je deze ervaring nog niet, dan word je hierin begeleid en opgeleid.

Heb je Biomedische Wetenschappen, Gezondheidswetenschappen of een vergelijkbare opleiding gestudeerd?
  • Je hebt een afgeronde master Biomedische Wetenschappen, Gezondheidswetenschappen of een vergelijkbare opleiding.
  • Je hebt affiniteit met klinisch onderzoek en het werken met patiënten.
  • Je vindt het interessant om wetenschappelijke vraagstukken te onderzoeken in een directe relatie met de patiëntenzorg.

Daarnaast breng je mee:
  • Je beschikt over uitstekende schriftelijke en mondelinge communicatievaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels.
  • Je kunt zelfstandig, gestructureerd en nauwkeurig werken en neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor je onderzoeksactiviteiten.
  • Je beschikt over goede organisatorische en communicatieve vaardigheden.
  • Je kunt goed samenwerken met professionals uit verschillende disciplines en hebt een proactieve en betrokken houding.
  • Je bent een echte teamspeler en staat open voor nieuwe kennis en inzichten.

Wat je van ons mag verwachten
Bij de Universiteit Maastricht werk je in een internationale, open en betrokken omgeving. We bieden:
  • Een jaarcontract (1,0 fte), bij wederzijdse tevredenheid wordt het contract verlengd met 3 jaar.
  • Een bruto salaris tussen €3204,00 en €4051,00 bruto per maand (bij een fulltime dienstverband van 38 uur per week), exclusief 8% vakantiegeld en een 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering.
  • 29 vakantiedagen, vier extra vrije feestdagen en de mogelijkheid om 12 extra dagen op te bouwen via compensatie-uren.
  • Flexibele werktijden, een thuiswerkvergoeding en hybride werken.
  • Vrijheid en ruimte om je werk zelfstandig in te richten en je eigen ideeën te ontwikkelen.
  • Een hechte community van collega’s waarmee je nauw samenwerkt.
  • Een goede pensioenregeling via het ABP, bedrijfsfitness en toegang tot een uitgebreid sportaanbod.
  • Een inspirerende werkomgeving in het hart van Europa.


Over de Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML)
FHML werkt aan gezondheid in de breedste zin van het woord: van molecuul tot mens, en van gezondheidszorg tot preventie. We leiden zorgprofessionals en onderzoekers op binnen innovatieve onderwijsprogramma’s, en doen baanbrekend onderzoek op het gebied van gezondheid en welzijn. Als onderdeel van het Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+) vormt onze internationale en interdisciplinaire gemeenschap een unieke samenwerking tussen universiteit en academisch ziekenhuis, waar onderwijs, onderzoek en zorg samenkomen.


Nieuwsgierig geworden?
Wil je meer weten over deze functie of over werken bij onze universiteit? Neem contact op met Stefan Bouwense via stefan.bouwense@mumc.nl of Lars Vanderbroeck via lars.vanderbroeck@mumc.nl. De einddatum van de publicatie is 6 december 2026. Een meeloop dag behoort tot de mogelijkheden.


Solliciteer via onderstaande knop. We hopen je snel te leren kennen!


Over de Universiteit Maastricht
Aan de Universiteit Maastricht zoeken we samen naar antwoorden waarmee we de wereld vooruithelpen. Dat doen we samen met 23.300 studenten en 5.400 medewerkers, verspreid over 5 steden in de regio, 6 faculteiten en ruim 70 onderzoeksinstituten in de Euregio. Hier krijg je de ruimte om grenzen te verleggen en nieuwe kansen te ontdekken; voor jezelf en voor de wereld om je heen. Want echte antwoorden vinden we samen.

De vacature staat open voor interne- en externe kandidaten. Bij gelijke geschiktheid hebben interne kandidaten voorrang.



Bij Maastricht University nemen we graag zelf contact op met potentiële kandidaten. We vragen daarom vriendelijk om geen acquisitie of aanbiedingen van bureaus of tussenpersonen.

Universiteit Maastricht zet zich in voor het bevorderen en behouden van een diverse en inclusieve gemeenschap. Wij geloven dat diversiteit in onze medewerkers- en studentenpopulatie bijdraagt aan de kwaliteit van onderzoek en onderwijs aan de UM. Dit willen we mogelijk maken door middel van inclusief beleid en innovatieve projecten in samenwerking met studenten en medewerkers. We moedigen je aan om voor deze functie te solliciteren.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Ecology of Waterway Management
jobs.description_html:
We have five positions available on the new BALANS project in the Netherlands: three PhD positions (at Radboud University (RU), the University of Groningen (RUG) and FLORON/RAVON respectively), one 4-year postdoctoral position (RU) and one two-year position for a research assistant that will become available later in 2027 (RUG).

These positions are part of a larger project funded by LVVN (Dutch Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature) dedicated to the management of waterways. Waterways, such as ditches, are maintained to ensure sufficient water flow capacity, but also harbour important biodiversity. BALANS will generate knowledge on best practices for future management of waterways, searching for a balance between their practical functionality and their biodiversity. The results will be used for the revision of the new code of conduct for waterway management in the Netherlands (2029) and will be obtained by a consortium including RU, RUG, FLORON, RAVON, and Wageningen Environmental Research (WEnR), with project management by STOWA (Foundation for Applied Water Research), and guided by a committee including representatives from the Dutch water boards and species conservation NGOs.

Key topics that will be investigated are the timing, frequency and spatial scales of mowing activities, and the type of machinery applied. Methodological approaches will include the analysis of available data from water boards, field monitoring, field experiments that manipulate mowing and lab-based experiments for a mechanistic understanding. Research will be carried out across different types of landscapes and waterway dimensions, and will include impacts on different species groups (fish, plants, birds, macrofauna, amphibians, mammals) for which we will apply different monitoring techniques (e.g. camera trapping, tracking, surveys).

As a PhD candidate, you will combine data analyses with setting up and running ecological experiments to examine the effects of various types of waterway management on aquatic and terrestrial plant and animal species. The focus will be on field monitoring, field experiments and targeted lab experiments to unravel general mechanisms in the response of species to mowing activity and other stressors. Work will include comparing the effectiveness of sampling techniques on a diverse range of species groups. You will work at the Department of Ecology at Radboud University, collaborating with the other two PhD candidates in this project.

PhD candidates will receive varied, cutting-edge research training, with ample opportunities to attend advanced courses, workshops and conferences, complemented by training in transferable skills and teaching - as standard at Radboud University. As a PhD candidate at Radboud University, you will be expected to be committed to conducting independent and original scientific research, reporting it in international publications and presentations, and presenting the results in a PhD thesis to be completed within four years. PhD candidates will be expected to contribute 10% of their overall workload to teaching.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

The other positions in the BALANS project can be found here:

PhD position at the University of Groningen

jobs.title: PhD Position Improving Symbolic AI through Learning and Reasoning
jobs.description_html:
Join TU Delft in developing AI that thinks like a scientist

Job description
While all the headlines are full of AI learning from massivve datasets, in this position you will investigate how can we teach machines to learn from tiny amounts of data. You will investigate how how can we achieve this goal by making AI think like a scientist -- reason about which models and plausible and should be explored. We will build this new approach upon the combination of program synthesis and automated reasoning, and apply it to actual problems from scientific discovery and robotics.

You will join the Algorithmics Group in the Department of Software Technology, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS). You will collaborate with PhD students and postdocs working on program synthesis and automated reasoning, and will have opportunities to co-supervise students. You will be supervised by Prof. Sebastijan Dumancic.

Job requirements
The ideal candidate will be an ambitious, proactive, reflective, and results-driven researcher. We are looking for the following:
  • MSc degree in Computer Science and/or Artificial Intelligence (essential)
  • prior experience in automated reasoning (essential)
  • prior experinece with symbolic machine learning approaches (essential)
  • prior experience in applying automated reasoning or machine learning in biology, chemistry, or other naturla sciences (desirable)
  • good communication, organisation, and writing skills
  • good programming skills and desire to produce usable open-source software

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.


Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. jobs.title: PhD position Ecology of waterway management
jobs.description_html:
We have five positions available with the new BALANS project in The Netherlands: three PhD positions (at Radboud University (RU), at University of Groningen (UG) and at FLORON/RAVON), one 4-year postdoctoral position (RU) and one two-year position for a research assistant that will open later in 2027 (UG).

These positions are part of a larger project funded by LVVN (Dutch Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature) dedicated to the management of waterways. Waterways such as ditches are maintained to ensure sufficient water flow capacity, but also harbour important biodiversity. BALANS will generate knowledge on best practices for future management of waterways, searching for a balance between waterway’s practical functionality and their biodiversity. The results will be used for the revision of the new code of conduct for waterway management in the Netherlands (2029) and are obtained in in a consortium that includes RU, RUG, FLORON, RAVON, and Wageningen Environmental Research (WEnR), with project management by STOWA (Foundation for Applied Water Research), and guided by a committee that includes representatives from the Dutch waterboards and species conservation NGOs.

What are you going to do?

Key topics that will be investigated are the timing, frequency and spatial scales of mowing activities, and the type of machinery applied. Methodological approaches will include the analysis of available data from waterboards, field monitoring, field experiments that manipulate mowing, and lab-based experiments for a mechanistic understanding. Research will be carried out across different types of landscapes and waterway dimensions, and will include impacts on different species groups (fish, plants, birds, macrofauna, amphibians, mammals) for which we will apply different monitoring techniques (e.g. camera trapping, tracking, surveys). Affinity with applied science and the ability to (learn or) speak Dutch are considered a plus for all positions.

The three PhD positions differ slightly in focus, but are highly comparable. In case you are interested in more than one position, please apply to every position separately for administrative reasons, but feel free to use the same letter while mentioning that you also applied for other positions. We will take this into account during the selection procedure in which we aim to match the best candidates to the best position.


The UG PhD candidate will combine analyses of data with setting up and running ecological experiments to examine the effects of various types of waterway management on aquatic and terrestrial plant and animal species. The focus will be on field monitoring, field experiments and targeted lab experiments to unravel general mechanisms in the response of species to mowing activity and other stressors. Work will include comparing the effectiveness of sampling techniques on a diverse range of species groups, for which basic taxonomic knowledge on aquatic or terrestrial species is considered beneficial.

jobs.title: PhD Positions in Tactile Flight - Autonomous Drone Navigation Through Touch
jobs.description_html:
What if drones could navigate by touch when vision fails? Pioneer a new approach to autonomous flight, using tactile sensing and embodied intelligence to navigate challenging environments.

Job description
How can a drone navigate when it cannot see? In darkness, dust, smoke or other visually degraded environments, conventional vision-based navigation can become unreliable or fail entirely. But what if drones could use touch to understand and navigate their surroundings? For the department of Control & Operations, we are looking for three PhD candidates to join Tactile Flight – Autonomous Tactile Flight via Cutaneous Touch and Kinesthesia, an ERC Starting Grant project exploring a fundamentally new approach to autonomous drone navigation: flying through the sense of touch.

Your challenge is to help establish touch as a core sensing modality for aerial robots. By combining novel lightweight, low-latency tactile sensing technologies with new approaches to cognition and control, you will investigate how computationally constrained drones can understand and navigate their surroundings through physical interaction with the environment. You will contribute to interdisciplinary research at the intersection of aerial robotics, tactile sensing, embodied intelligence and autonomous navigation. Together with researchers from different disciplines, you will explore new ways for drones to perceive and interact with the physical world.

The project combines technological innovation with hands-on robotic research. You will contribute to experimental research and field campaigns, applying your knowledge and creativity to explore new approaches to autonomous flight. You will also contribute to teaching, particularly our MSc course on Aerial Physical Interaction. As one of the three PhD candidates, you will help shape an emerging research direction in aerial robotics. Together, we aim to open new possibilities for autonomous drone navigation in hazardous, confined and inaccessible environments.

Learn more about the ERC Tactile Flight project at TU Delft.

jobs.title: PhD in Intelligent Gate Drivers for Silicon Carbide Power Semiconductors
jobs.description_html:
Can power converters become intelligent systems that monitor their own condition and adapt their operation? Join our ERC-funded project to bring real-time models and local intelligence close to power semiconductors -the heart of power electronics- and advance the energy transition.

Information
Renewable energy integration and the electrification of transport depend on efficient and reliable power electronic converters. Silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductors offer opportunities to improve their performance, but how can we also enable these converters to interpret their own behaviour and act on this information?

This PhD position is part of the ERC-funded project Power Electronics As Edge Computing Grid Components (PELCom), which aims to transform SiC-based power electronic converters into intelligent, data-processing systems. You will join the Electromechanics and Power Electronics (EPE) group within the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology, under the supervision of Professor Dimosthenis Peftitsis.

Your research will focus on intelligent active gate drivers for SiC semiconductors: circuits that control power semiconductor switching while combining sensing, embedded processing and real-time models. You will investigate how electrical, thermal and reliability models can operate locally within these drivers to enable rapid, finely tuned switching adjustments and condition monitoring at semiconductor device level.

Your main research activities will include:
  • Developing electrical, thermal and reliability models and identifying the computational resources and processing platforms (e.g., FPGAs and DSPs) needed for real-time execution.
  • Designing an optimised network of onboard sensors and identifying the minimum set of measured quantities needed to fit the models.
  • Developing a wireless communication framework between the intelligent gate drivers and the converter’s central processor.
  • Designing, building and experimentally validating an intelligent active gate driver with embedded real-time models.

You will combine modelling, embedded implementation and experimental research, working with the PELCom team to connect device-level intelligence with converter-level functions. You will be part of a research group with several PhD students working on power electronics, offering opportunities to exchange ideas, share expertise and collaborate on related research challenges. Your work will contribute to more efficient and reliable power conversion technologies for a sustainable, increasingly electrified society.

jobs.title: Promovendus Politieke socialisatie en democratisch moreel vakmanschap
jobs.description_html:
Ben je geïnteresseerd in welke democratische en morele normen en waarden politieke ambtsdragers meekrijgen via training en opleiding? Ben je benieuwd hoe formele en informele processen van socialisatie binnen politieke partijen het democratisch moreel vakmanschap beïnvloeden? En wil je weten hoe de professionalisering van politieke ambtsdragers verder kan worden versterkt? Dan is het promotietraject ‘Politieke socialisatie en democratisch vakmanschap’ iets voor jou.

Jouw functie
Deze promotieplaats maakt deel uit van het project Democraft: een door de NWA-ORC gefinancierd samenwerkingsverband van maar liefst 4 universiteiten, 2 hogescholen en 27 maatschappelijke partners. Dit consortium onderzoekt hoe het democratisch moreel vakmanschap van politici kan worden versterkt: de kennis, vaardigheden, houding en praktijken die nodig zijn om het politieke ambt integer en volgens democratische en rechtsstatelijke normen uit te oefenen. Zulk democratisch moreel vakmanschap is cruciaal in tijden van crises en maatschappelijke transities. Ontwikkelingen zoals klimaatverandering, migratie, polarisatie en digitalisering zetten democratische instituties onder druk om snel én verantwoord te handelen. Politici staan daarbij voor complexe morele dilemma’s, waarin botsende waarden en belangen vragen om zorgvuldige afwegingen. Binnen Democraft onderzoeken we hoe politieke ambtsdragers met deze normatieve uitdagingen omgaan, hoe hun democratisch moreel vakmanschap beter kan worden ondersteund en hoe dat de institutionele veerkracht versterkt. Om die vragen te beantwoorden combineert het Democraft-consortium een interdisciplinaire mix van benaderingen (o.a. vanuit de politicologie, de bestuurskunde, de geschiedenis, communicatiewetenschap en het staats- en bestuursrecht).

In dit specifieke PhD-project onderzoek je hoe socialisatieprocessen bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling en internalisering van democratische en morele normen bij (aankomende) politieke ambtsdragers: hoe ontwikkelen politieke ambtsdragers de kennis, vaardigheden, houding en praktijken die nodig zijn om hun ambt integer en in overeenstemming met democratische normen uit te oefenen? Je richt je daarbij in het bijzonder op de rol van politieke partijen, beroepsverenigingen en opleidingen en trainingen voor politieke ambtsdragers. Wat wordt er in die context verstaan onder democratisch moreel vakmanschap? Welke waarden en normen worden er expliciet of impliciet overgedragen? Hoe wordt dat aangeleerd en getraind? Welke formele en informele processen spelen daarbij een rol?

Je onderzoekt onder meer trainings- en professionaliseringsprogramma’s voor politieke ambtsdragers. Je combineert daarbij literatuur- en documentstudie met interviews, focusgroepen en participerende observatie. Je werkt nauw samen met de beroeps- en belangenverenigingen en onderzoekt de randvoorwaarden voor effectieve training en opleiding van (aankomende) politieke ambtsdragers en andere vormen van politieke socialisatie. Het project resulteert in wetenschappelijke inzichten en concrete aanbevelingen voor de praktijk. Zo draagt je onderzoek bij aan beter begrip en versterking van het democratisch moreel vakmanschap van politieke ambtsdragers.

Je wordt begeleid door Niels Karsten (TiU), Leonie Heres (VU), Charlotte Wagenaar (VU) en Take Sipma (TiU) en werkt samen verschillende maatschappelijke partners, zoals de Nederlandse Vereniging voor Raadsleden, het Nederlands Genootschap van Burgemeesters, de Wethoudersvereniging en verschillende gemeenten.

Je proefschrift schrijf je bij de vakgroep Public Law & Governance (PLG), die onderdeel is van Tilburg Law School. Tegelijk maak je onderdeel uit van het Democraft-consortium. Democraft besteedt veel aandacht aan de ontwikkeling van promovendi en postdocs. Zo word je actief begeleid op het inter- en transdisciplinair samenwerken en netwerken buiten je eigen discipline en onderzoeksdomein. Ook organiseren we halfjaarlijkse workshops waar je met elkaar en met topwetenschappers uit het veld kunt sparren over je onderzoek, inspiratie kunt opdoen, en getraind wordt in vaardigheden die belangrijk zijn voor impactgericht onderzoek. En er is een mogelijkheid om naast je academische begeleidingsteam ook bij één van onze maatschappelijke partners een mentor te krijgen die je wegwijs maakt in de ambtelijke en/of politiek-bestuurlijke praktijk.

Als promovendus in dit project draag je uiteraard bij aan activiteiten van Democraft en van de vakgroep PLG, zoals bijvoorbeeld het participeren in, of organiseren van lezingen, workshops en/of seminarlunches. Daarnaast draag je bij aan het onderwijs van de vakgroep PLG in de Bachelor Bestuurskunde en/of de Master Public Governance & Strategy.  Concreet houdt dit alles in, het:

  • Uitvoeren van verschillende (empirische) deelstudies naar politieke socialisatie en democratisch moreel vakmanschap;
  • Schrijven van een Engelstalig interdisciplinair proefschrift, bij voorkeur op basis van artikelen;
  • Deelnemen aan programma’s van de Tilburg University Graduate Law School en de promovendi-opleiding van het Netherlands Institute of Governance (NIG);
  • Bijdragen aan het onderwijs in de Bachelor Bestuurskunde en/of de Master Public Governance & Strategy (0.1 FTE);
  • Samenwerken met collega-onderzoekers en maatschappelijke partners om het Democraft-consortium verder te versterken.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Prospective Environmental Assessment of Technological Innovations
jobs.description_html:
Would you like to help advance environmental sustainability in healthcare from the very first design step? As a PhD candidate at Radboud University, you will join the European Doctoral Network Implant-to-Market, an interdisciplinary collaboration between environmental scientists, clinicians, health economists and policy experts working towards sustainable innovation of medical devices across Europe.

Environmental impacts are still rarely considered in the design phase of medical devices, such as implants, although decisions at that stage largely determine their life cycle impact on human health and ecosystems. Robust methods are needed to assess the future impacts of medical devices under development.

Your research will focus on developing methods in Life Cycle Assessment to support Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) medical devices. A particular focus will be on developing methods to estimate material, energy, chemical and water use of lab scale technologies, and to assess impacts that are relevant for this sector, such as toxicity and water use.

As a PhD candidate, you will develop, evaluate and apply innovative methods in prospective Life Cycle Assessment for medical devices. A particular focus will be on improving the scientific basis to assess prospective inventory data collection and quantifying the corresponding impacts on ecosystems and human health. You will investigate how robust estimates can be made to guide developers towards SSbD medical devices with advice from innovation to market introduction. In addition, together with developers, you will apply and evaluate these methods in real-world implant case studies. This will allow you to connect methodological innovation with real-world design and development, and contribute to more sustainable innovations.

Within the Implant-to-Market project, 15 doctoral candidates will be hired at institutes throughout Europe. A secondment of at least 3 months to a partner institute in another country is mandatory. You will also have the opportunity to further develop and improve your skill set by attending training courses organised within the project, and courses of the Graduate School of the Radboud Institute for Biological and Environmental Sciences and elsewhere. You will communicate your findings through publications in peer-reviewed journals; and part of your workload (10%) will consist of teaching activities at our institute, assisting staff members in their courses at the MSc level (in English) and supervising thesis research.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

jobs.title: PhD: AI for early detection of cardiometabolic diseases using oral health data
jobs.description_html:
You develop and clinically validate innovative AI-based screening models integrating retrospective and prospective data from multiple sources. These models are applied in the context of oral and systemic health, with a particular focus on the early detection of cardiometabolic diseases (CMD). You also assess the usability of the models in clinical practice. Working within a multidisciplinary research team, you help translate advanced AI methods into clinically relevant applications. In addition to your research activities, you may contribute to ongoing educational activities within the department, including the supervision of bachelor's and master's theses.

About the project
Cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, oral cancer and osteoporosis remain among the most important public health challenges in Europe. Increasing evidence suggests that oral health and general health are closely connected, yet these links are not routinely used to support disease prevention and early detection.

The MYDIAG.AI project, funded by EU-Horizon, aims to address this gap by developing a generative AI-powered virtual assistant capable of analyzing multiple sources of health information, including electronic health records, clinical notes, intraoral photographs, and panoramic dental X-rays. The AI assistant will help healthcare professionals identify potential health risks, support clinical decision-making, and generate draft medical notes and referral letters. By bringing together expertise in dentistry, medicine, data science and AI, MYDIAG.AI seeks to strengthen collaboration between oral healthcare and general healthcare.

The Academic Center for Dentistry Amsterdam (ACTA) will focus on the development and validation of a multimodal AI-model, which will serve as a core component of the virtual assistant. ACTA will also contribute to the clinical validation and implementation of the virtual assistant in dental settings. Both retrospective and prospective observational data will be collected and used in the study.

jobs.title: Promovendus Agressie te Lijf+ voor volwassenen met een LVB
jobs.description_html:
Agressief gedrag komt vaak voor bij volwassenen met een licht verstandelijke beperking (LVB) en heeft impact op henzelf en omgeving. Begeleiding en psychomotorische therapie (PMT) wordt ingezet om agressie te verminderen. Agressie te Lijf+ (ATL+) is een vorm van PMT die helpt om lichamelijke signalen van angst en boosheid te herkennen en er beter mee om te gaan (coping), zodat agressie wordt voorkomen. Dit project heeft als doel om ATL+ te toetsen, om daarmee inzicht te krijgen in de mate waarin het volwassenen met een LVB helpt om minder vaak agressief te zijn en meer lichaamsbewustzijn, mogelijkheden voor coping en kwaliteit van leven te ervaren. Het onderzoek vindt plaats met deelnemers met agressief gedrag en een Wlz indicatie uit vijf instellingen, willekeurig verdeeld over twee groepen: ATL+ en begeleiding of alleen begeleiding. Hiertoe werkt je vanuit de Academische Werkplaats Viveon samen met de academische werkplaats Leven met een Verstandelijke Beperking in Tilburg, Hogeschool Windesheim in Zwolle, ’s Heeren Loo, Reinaerde, Prinsenstichting en de Nederlandse Vereniging voor Psychomotorische Therapie.

Wat ga je zoal doen
  • je voert een Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) uit naar de effectiviteit van Agressie te Lijf+ (ATL+)
  • je bent betrokken bij de voorbereiding, opzet en uitvoering van het onderzoek, waaronder het werven en includeren van deelnemers en coördineren van de dataverzameling
  • je verzamelt, verwerkt en analyseert onderzoeksgegevens en interpreteert de resultaten
  • je werkt nauw samen met de zorgorganisaties, psychomotorisch therapeuten, onderzoekers en andere betrokken professionals
  • je presenteert de onderzoeksresultaten op wetenschappelijke bijeenkomsten en congressen en schrijft wetenschappelijke artikelen die samen leiden tot je proefschrift
  • je draagt bij aan de vertaling van onderzoeksresultaten naar de praktijk, zodat de kennis over PMT en agressieregulatie verder wordt ontwikkeld en toegepast

jobs.title: PhD position Data-Driven Distribution Systems Planning with District Heating
jobs.description_html:
Job Description
The Delft University of Technology is hiring a doctoral candidate on the subject "Data-Driven Distribution Systems Planning with District Heating".

The decarbonization of the heating sector in the Netherlands is resulting in an increased adoption of district heating at the city scale. Depending on the type of district heating system and its interface with the electricity infrastructure, uncoordinated operation and poor planning may increase congestion at the medium-voltage level. In this PhD project, we will investigate how the electricity infrastructure can accommodate district heating networks by properly coordinating their future operation. To do this, we first investigate which data are needed (from distribution system operators, municipalities, users, etc.) to properly model future district heating demand and operations. We will also aim to understand what the barriers are to obtaining and using such data. As more data becomes available, we will investigate the role of artificial intelligence and machine learning models in facilitating coordinated planning, as well as how to incorporate risk and uncertainty. This PhD Position is part of the NWO Share the “Warmth Project: Data Sharing for Urban Heat Transition Planning”. The Sharing the Warmth Project aims to help Dutch cities move toward affordable, sustainable, and gas-free heating. The project brings citizens, municipalities, and grid operators together to share data in a safe and trustworthy way. By developing privacy-preserving tools and fair data-sharing arrangements, this project strengthens cooperation and informed decision-making. This enables municipalities to plan heating upgrades more efficiently and creates a fairer, more future-proof energy system for everyone.

This is a four-year doctoral appointment. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Pedro P. Vergara (Associate Professor), Prof. Peter Palensky (Chair IEPG) and Dr. Ivo Potof (CEG Faculty). You will be a member of the section Intelligent Electrical Power Grids in the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, and Computer Science. The project will offer opportunities to collaborate with industrial partners but also with academics from other disciplines, as required (mathematics, operations research). Within the team, we strive to develop methods that are mathematically rigorous and have near-term application potential. We are strong supporters of open science (publishing, source code, data). You will also be expected to assist in teaching activities (student supervision, labs) related to your subject area.

About the ESE Department

The research in the Department of Electrical Sustainable Energy is inspired by the technical, scientific, and societal challenges originating from the transition towards a more sustainable society and focuses on four areas:
  • DC Systems, Energy Conversion and Storage (DCE&S).
  • Photovoltaic Materials and Devices (PVMD).
  • High Voltage Technologies (HVT).
  • Intelligent Electrical Power Grids (IEPG).

jobs.title: PhD Candidates in Gravitational-Wave Astroparticle Physics (GRAPPA, University of Amsterdam)
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working at the interface of general relativity, gravitational wave astrophysics, and dark matter phenomenology?

Do you enjoy working in an interdisciplinary research setting and do you want to be active in a variety of educational programmes? The GRAPPA team is looking for one or more ambitious PhD positions.

Join Us!
You will join the GRAPPA centre of excellence for Gravitation and Astroparticle Physics at the University of Amsterdam, embedded in the Institute of Physics at Amsterdam Science Park. You will be part of an international team working on dark matter in strong‑gravity environments, in close contact with collaborators in the LISA community and beyond. Your mission is to advance the theory and computation needed to identify dark matter signatures in gravitational wave data.

This is what you will do
  • Carry out research on gravitational wave sources in dark matter or related astrophysical environments;
  • Present your work in group meetings and conferences; write and co‑author publications;
  • Contribute to education (exercise classes and BSc/MSc supervision) as customary at the Faculty of Science.

You will be based at GRAPPA — an internationally recognized hub in gravitation, astroparticle physics, and cosmology. GRAPPA hosts experts in gravitational waves, numerical relativity, multimessenger astrophysics and dark matter, and collaborates with LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, LISA, and the Einstein Telescope communities.

What we ask of you
  • We are looking for highly motivated candidates who will have completed an MSc in Physics, Astronomy, or a closely related field by the start date;
  • have a solid grounding in General Relativity and/or gravitational wave astrophysics;
  • have experience in scientific programming (for example in Python or C++);
  • can communicate clearly in English;
  • enjoy working in a collaborative research environment.

It is a plus, not a requirement, if you are already familiar with cosmological or N‑body simulations, basic concepts in gravitational wave data analysis, or dark matter phenomenology.

This is what we offer you
We offer a temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (Scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD candidate is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants.

The preferred starting date is to be discussed. This employment should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

The Institute of Physics (IoP) of the University of Amsterdam is located in the centre of the Amsterdam Science Park. The IoP – as part of the Faculty of Science –is housed in a modern building with excellent labs and technical facilities. Surrounded by several national research institutes and with our partners at the Vrije Universiteit (VU) Amsterdam, the institute is part of a strong physics centre of international standing.

You will be based at GRAPPA — an internationally recognized hub in gravitation, astroparticle physics, and cosmology. GRAPPA hosts experts in gravitational waves, numerical relativity, multimessenger astrophysics and dark matter, and collaborates with LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, LISA, and the Einstein Telescope communities.

GRAPPA was established as a research priority area of the university in 2010 and is part of the Anton Pannekoek Institute for Astronomy and the Institute of Physics and connects to Nikhef and Institute for Informatics. GRAPPA members have won high-profile awards including the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics, the Shakti Duggal Prize and the Humboldt Research Award.
