jobs.title: PhD position: ‘Action research into learning about knowledge in policy practice’
jobs.description_html:
The Athena Institute at VU University Amsterdam is seeking a PhD candidate for the research project Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP), funded under the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA). The PhD candidate will conduct research within the subproject ‘Learning from and evaluating new knowledge-for-policy arrangements’.

The overarching project:

Research-based knowledge is an essential building block for effective policymaking. In practice, however, the systematic use of research evidence in policymaking cannot be taken for granted. The research project Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP) aims to strengthen forms of collaboration between research and policy to foster more usable knowledge and more effective knowledge use. The CRISP consortium brings together several knowledge institutions and government ministries and will include eight PhD candidates and three postdoctoral researchers. The research will be conducted in co-creation with government ministries and other stakeholders and focuses on a set of current policy issues. For a description of the CRISP consortium and its subprojects, please see: www.scienceforpolicy.nl

Your research:
As a PhD candidate in this subproject, you will develop an approach to designing and monitoring (inter)departmental learning processes on knowledge in policy. You will support the work of policymakers who, together with academics and other stakeholders, experiment in so-called Policy Labs with new ways of constructing and utilising knowledge in their day-to-day policy work. Among the project aims is to assist in the development of cross-sectoral policy by integrating objectives and instruments for the general well-being of society (‘Brede Welvaart’) into domain specific policy. Key questions in this subproject are: How can we map learning in policy? How does monitoring experimental ‘knowledge work’ help improve the policies at issue? How can we embed lessons on integrated knowledge utilization from the Policy Labs into existing policy processes?

To answer these questions, you will conduct action research in various Policy Labs, facilitate a systematic comparison of their results, and empirically test how the insights from the CRISP project on policy-oriented learning and knowledge utilisation can be effectively shared in policy practice. The research will be carried out under the supervision of Dr Anne Loeber, Dr Kristiaan Kok and Dr Eva Kunseler.

Concretely, your tasks are:
  • developing the research proposal into a coherent and feasible PhD plan that aligns with the overarching CRISP project
  • collecting and analysing empirical data in support of the subproject ‘Learning from and evaluating new knowledge-for-policy arrangements’
  • co-creating research with partner from policy and science, by actively involving them in the research process and translating results into practice-oriented recommendations
  • completing an English-language doctoral dissertation within four years
  • publishing in international peer-reviewed journals and contributing to Open Access and professional publications
  • presenting research findings at national and international academic and practitioner-oriented conferences
  • actively participating in meetings and research activities organised by the Athena Institute, the subproject and the CRISP consortium
  • contributing to BSc and/or MSc teaching provided by the Athena Institute (up to 20 per cent of the appointment)

jobs.title: PhD position Societal entrepreneurship in equitable global health innovation
jobs.description_html:
The Athena Institute of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is looking for a motivated PhD candidate for the project ‘Navigating multiple accountabilities: societal entrepreneurship in equitable global health innovation’. In this position, you will study how organisations in global health innovation navigate competing accountabilities, and how these accountability relations can be reshaped to foster equity.

Creating an equitable and socially responsible global health innovation system is a widely shared ambition. It includes access to medicines, vaccines, diagnostics and medical devices, but also where R&D and manufacturing take place, who owns IP and data, and who captures value. Pharmaceutical and biotech companies, product development partnerships (PDPs), funders, universities and LMIC-based manufacturers present themselves as societal entrepreneurs committed to this ambition. Yet translating these ambitions into practice is far from straightforward. Everyday organisational decisions involve trade-offs between different expectations, responsibilities and values. Questions about research priorities, licensing arrangements, intellectual property, manufacturing strategies, partnerships and pricing become moments where broader societal ambitions are interpreted, negotiated and enacted. Organisations involved in global health innovation are accountable to multiple actors at the same time, including investors, funders, regulators, patients, civil society organisations and communities. These actors often have different expectations about what constitutes equitable and socially responsible innovation, what outcomes matter, and who should benefit from innovation processes and outcomes. As a result, organisations must continuously navigate competing demands and values in everyday decision-making. Navigating this web of accountabilities is a lived challenge for companies, PDPs, NGOs under funding pressure, and manufacturers and regulators in the Global South, and some of them are already experimenting with new arrangements.

Questions that you can focus on are: How do organisations navigate multiple and sometimes competing accountabilities? Which values, responsibilities and understandings of social responsibility and equity are prioritised, negotiated or marginalised in organisational decision-making? How are societal responsibilities reflected in licensing, IP and data-sharing terms, manufacturing location and portfolio decisions? Under which conditions do accountability mechanisms contribute to organisational learning and change, rather than compliance alone? And how can organisations and those to whom they are accountable jointly reshape accountability relations in practice, in ways that support more equitable and socially responsible global health innovation?

This is a transdisciplinary PhD project: knowledge is produced together with partner organisations directly experiencing these challenges in their daily work, from pharmaceutical companies and PDPs to NGOs, manufacturers and regulators, operating across high-, middle- and low-income countries. You will examine concrete decisions and practices, identify tensions between accountability demands, and explore and test changes in practices and arrangements, supported by reflexive monitoring in action. At least one case is anchored in the Global South. The project focuses on how organisations make and justify strategic decisions, not on evaluating health interventions or clinical outcomes.

The project draws on governance and accountability studies, organisational behaviour, responsible and societal entrepreneurship, and the literature on sustainability transformations. You will be supervised by a team consisting of dr. Lieselot Vandenbussche and dr. Kenneth Fernald (daily supervisors), prof. dr. Linda van de Burgwal, dr. Nora Engel and prof. dr. Barbara Regeer.

Your duties
The PhD project is organised in three work packages. In year 1 you map, together with the partners, which accountabilities organisations face and how these are reflected in index scores, agreements, portfolios and manufacturing and IP arrangements, and you jointly select concrete cases and shared learning questions. In years 2 and 3 you run living labs with two to three partner constellations, working through concrete decisions with reflexive monitoring. In year 4 you draw cross-case lessons on the conditions under which accountability mechanisms move organisations beyond compliance, and translate these with the partners into actionable approaches for their organisations and networks. Together with the supervision team, in the first year you will develop a research proposal in which you outline your own ideas and interests for the PhD research.

Concretely, your tasks are:
  • conducting research and collaboratively writing scientific articles that will form the basis of your PhD thesis
  • setting up and facilitating living labs and workshops with partner organisations and stakeholders, in the Netherlands and in the Global South
  • contributing to recommendations for policy and practice based on the research outcomes
  • presenting your work at conferences
  • following courses to develop your research skills (formal PhD training)
  • teaching working groups in the education programmes of the Athena Institute (max 0.2 fte)

jobs.title: PhD positie ‘Actieonderzoek naar leren over kennis in de beleidspraktijk’
jobs.description_html:
Het Athena Instituut van de Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam zoekt een promovendus (m/v) binnen het Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP) project, gefinancierd in het kader van de Nationale Wetenschapsagenda (NWA). De promovendus zal onderzoek doen in het deelproject ‘Leren in en evalueren van nieuwe kennis-voor-beleid arrangementen.’

Het overkoepelende project
Kennis uit onderzoek vormt een belangrijke bouwsteen voor effectief beleid. De praktijk leert echter dat de systematische benutting van kennis uit onderzoek voor beleid niet vanzelfsprekend is. Het consortium ‘Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy’ (CRISP) wil door onderzoek bijdragen aan een verbeterde aansluiting tussen kennis en beleid. De verwachting is dat dit leidt tot beter bruikbare kennis en betere kennisbenutting. Daarmee kunnen complexe maatschappelijke opgaven beter worden begrepen, en effectiever en efficiënter aangepakt.

In het CRISP-consortium nemen verschillende kennisinstellingen en ministeries deel en zullen 8 promovendi en 3 postdocs onderzoek doen. Het onderzoek vindt plaats in co-creatie met ministeries en andere stakeholders en richt zich op actuele publieke vraagstukken. Voor een beschrijving van het CRISP-consortium en de deelprojecten: zie www.scienceforpolicy.nl

Het promotieonderzoek
Als promovendus in dit deelproject ontwikkel je een benadering om (inter)departementale leerprocessen vorm te geven rond kennis in beleid. Je ondersteunt en monitort het werk van beleidsmakers die samen met wetenschappers en andere actoren experimenteren in zogenaamde Policy Labs met nieuwe manieren van kennisproductie en kennisgebruik in hun dagelijks werk. Doel is onder meer om hen te assisteren bij het ontwikkelen van domeinoverstijgend beleid door doelen en instrumenten vanuit het perspectief van het algemeen welzijn in de samenleving (‘Brede Welvaart’) te integreren in specifieke beleidsdomeinen. Centrale vragen in dit deelproject zijn: Hoe kunnen we leren in beleid in kaart brengen? Hoe helpt monitoren van experimenteel ‘kenniswerk’ het beleid dat centraal staat te verbeteren? Hoe kunnen we lessen over integraal beleid en kennisgebruik uit de Policy Labs verankeren in bestaande beleidsprocessen?

Voor een antwoord op deze vragen voer je actieonderzoek uit in verschillende Policy Labs, maak je een systematische vergelijking van de resultaten mogelijk en toets je empirisch hoe de inzichten uit het CRISP-project over beleidsgericht leren en kennisbenutting effectief kunnen worden gedeeld in de beleidspraktijk. Het onderzoek wordt uitgevoerd onder begeleiding van dr. Anne Loeber, dr. Kristiaan Kok en dr. Eva Kunseler.

Concreet zijn jouw taken:
  • het uitwerken van het onderzoeksvoorstel tot een samenhangend en uitvoerbaar promotieplan, dat aansluit bij het overkoepelende CRISP-project
  • dataverzameling -en analyse in functie van het deelproject ‘Leren in en evalueren van nieuwe kennis-voor-beleid arrangementen’
  • het co-creëren van onderzoek met praktijkpartners, door hen actief te betrekken bij het onderzoeksproces en het vertalen van resultaten naar praktijkgerichte aanbevelingen
  • het binnen vier jaar afronden van een Engelstalig proefschrift
  • het publiceren in internationale peer-reviewed tijdschriften, bijdragen aan Open Access-publicaties en professionele publicaties
  • het presenteren van resultaten op nationale en internationale wetenschappelijke en praktijkgerichte conferenties
  • actieve deelname aan bijeenkomsten en onderzoeksactiviteiten van het Athena Instituut, het deelproject en het CRISP-consortium
  • het leveren van bijdragen aan BSc en/of MSc onderwijs dat verzorgd wordt door het Athena Instituut (max. 20% van de aanstelling)

jobs.title: PhD Position Understanding Incentives for Software Reuse
jobs.description_html:
Why do teams build new software rather than reuse existing solutions? Investigate how technology, incentives and organisational behaviour shape these choices in this PhD project.

Job description
Software reuse promises to reduce duplicated effort and help organisations develop technology at scale. Teams build data assets, software components, APIs and AI agents that other teams can adopt. Yet making these resources available does not necessarily mean they will be reused. What appears efficient for the organisation as a whole may create additional costs, dependencies or risks for individual teams.

This raises a research question that extends across organisations: under what conditions do teams choose to reuse existing solutions, and when do they build their own? Technical explanations, such as integration difficulties or poor documentation, may tell only part of the story. Performance targets, budget allocation, professional norms and regulatory requirements may also shape these decisions. Understanding how these factors interact is essential to explaining when reuse succeeds—and when developing a separate solution makes sense.

This PhD project investigates these questions through empirical research within a large international bank. A particular focus is how people become attached to their own solutions and their ideas of what “good” looks like—and how this shapes their willingness to adopt alternatives. You will use evidence from this setting to develop and test explanations relevant to the wider challenge of organising software reuse.

As a PhD researcher, you will conduct interdisciplinary research at the intersection of software engineering, economics and organisational behaviour. Your work will include:
  • Interviewing engineers, data scientists, product owners, architects and managers to understand how teams decide whether to build or reuse.
  • Analysing internal usage data to measure reuse and identify differences across teams, business units and types of software assets.
  • Examining how performance targets, ownership arrangements, budgets and regulatory requirements influence these decisions.
  • Comparing teams’ stated reasons with their observed behaviour to understand which explanations are supported by the evidence.
  • Developing proposals to improve reuse and evaluating selected interventions in practice.

The project draws on theories of incentives, transaction costs and the governance of shared resources. You will test existing assumptions and develop new explanations, including findings that challenge prevailing ideas about what enables effective reuse.

The research will be conducted in close collaboration with the partner bank. You will regularly spend time within the organisation and work with its experts. This collaboration provides an empirical setting for studying how technical and organisational factors interact across teams, business units and jurisdictions.

Your four-year PhD is part of a joint research programme between TU Delft and the partner bank. The programme brings together four PhD projects investigating incentives for reuse, resource orchestration, the evolution of software assets and reliable AI-assisted software development. Your findings will inform related work on improving support for reuse.

You will be supervised by Professor Michel van Eeten and Dr Yury Zhauniarovich at TU Delft’s Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Your project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary team of more than 20 researchers, bringing together computer science, social science and other disciplines.   • The ability to work independently, critically assess evidence and collaborate with researchers and practitioners from different disciplines.

For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

Please note:

Applications and additional information sent by email or through other channels, including unsolicited applications, will not be considered or responded to. This also applies to open applications.

When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security.
  • Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

jobs.title: Promovendus op het gebied van communicatie over onzekerheden bij forensische risico-inschattingen
jobs.description_html:
Ben je (bijna) afgestudeerd in de rechtsgeleerdheid, met een specialisatie in het strafrecht, de criminologie of forensische psychologie en wil je onderzoek doen op het snijvlak van het strafrecht en de forensische gedragskunde? Wij zoeken een promovendus die onderzoek wil doen naar de communicatie van onzekerheden rondom recidiverisico-inschattingen en de betekenis daarvan voor juridische besluitvorming. Het departement Criminal Law van Tilburg Law School biedt je, in samenwerking met het Nederlands Instituut voor Forensische Psychiatrie en Psychologie (NIFP), de mogelijkheid om vier jaar als onderzoeker (PhD) aan de slag te gaan met dit interdisciplinaire vraagstuk.

Jouw functie
Inschattingen van het recidiverisico spelen een belangrijke rol bij de onderbouwing van ingrijpende strafrechtelijke beslissingen, bijvoorbeeld over behandeling, toezicht en vrijheidsbeperking. Maar inschattingen van toekomstig delinquent gedrag zijn inherent onzeker. Juist vanwege de betekenis van deze inschattingen voor individuele beslissingen is het van belang dat ook relevante onzekerheden zorgvuldig worden gecommuniceerd, zoals de betrouwbaarheid van beschikbare informatie, de beperkingen van gebruikte instrumenten en toekomstige omstandigheden die het risico kunnen beïnvloeden. Het promotieonderzoek richt zich op de vraag hoe binnen de forensisch-psychiatrische en juridische praktijk kan worden omgegaan met de communicatie over onzekerheden in risico-inschattingen. Het project heeft een interdisciplinair karakter waarbij empirische en juridisch-normatieve onderzoeksmethoden worden gecombineerd. Met het onderzoek wordt beoogd aanknopingspunten te bieden voor een zorgvuldige communicatie en weging van risico en onzekerheid in strafrechtelijke beslissingen, mede vanuit een juridisch-normatief kader voor de vraag welke onzekerheidsinformatie daarbij relevant is.

Je wordt onderdeel van zowel het departement Criminal Law van Tilburg Law School (50%) als de afdeling Wetenschap en Opleidingen van het NIFP (50%). Je maakt deel uit van een interdisciplinair onderzoeksteam, draagt bij aan het onderwijs van de vakgroep Strafrecht en begeleidt in het kader van dataverzameling stagiairs die werkzaam zijn bij het NIFP. Het project zal worden uitgevoerd onder supervisie van prof.mr. J. (Joeri) Bemelmans (Tilburg University), prof.dr. Maaike Kempes (NIFP) en mr.dr. L.E. (Laura) van Oploo (Tilburg University; NIFP) en wordt mede mogelijk gemaakt door subsidie van Stichting Koningsheide.

jobs.title: PhD position: High-voltage power conversion for electric-propulsion spacecraft
jobs.description_html:
BESCAPE (Advanced Wide Bandgap-based Power Processing and Management for Future Space Exploration) is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network – Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement 101312786). It trains 11 doctoral candidates in power conversion, control and electrical power distribution for future space exploration, together with European universities, ESA and leading space companies.

High-power spacecraft with electric propulsion need highly efficient battery discharge regulators (BDRs) that deliver a regulated 300 V secondary bus from a 48 V battery. Your research will find the best converter solutions for this, and prove them in hardware.

Your research activities:
  • Investigate isolated and non-isolated high step-up DC/DC converter topologies for 48 V to 300 V conversion.
  • Benchmark converter designs for efficiency, specific power, reliability and cost, including multi-objective optimisation.
  • Design, build and experimentally validate a hardware demonstrator against the project’s performance targets.
  • Perform several months secondments at ESA and at UMH, and take part in the network’s training events and conferences.

jobs.title: PhD position: Ultra-high-current power supplies for AI processors in satellites
jobs.description_html:
BESCAPE (Advanced Wide Bandgap-based Power Processing and Management for Future Space Exploration) is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network – Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement 101312786). It trains 11 doctoral candidates in power conversion, control and electrical power distribution for future space exploration, together with European universities, ESA and leading space companies.

Future satellite AI processors need efficient conversion from 48 V distribution rails to about 1 V at currents of 100 A or more, under strict spacecraft mass, thermal and reliability constraints. Your research will push the limits of efficiency and power density for this extreme step-down ratio.

Your research activities:
  • Explore modular series/parallel, hybrid and multiphase converter architectures for high step-down ratios.
  • Investigate advanced magnetic structures and GaN semiconductor technology to maximise efficiency and gravimetric power density.
  • Develop digital-twin models and circuit design tools, and build a hardware demonstrator targeting 48 V to 1 V, 100 A and at least 92% efficiency under the specified conditions.
  • Perform several months secondments at Leonardo and at KU Leuven, and take part in the network’s training events and conferences.

jobs.title: PhD position: Smart latching current limiters with AI-based anomaly detection for spacecraft
jobs.description_html:
BESCAPE (Advanced Wide Bandgap-based Power Processing and Management for Future Space Exploration) is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network – Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement 101312786). It trains 11 doctoral candidates in power conversion, control and electrical power distribution for future space exploration, together with European universities, ESA and leading space companies.

Spacecraft DC distribution requires highly reliable current limitation and fault management. This project develops switching latching current limiters (swLCLs) with intelligent health monitoring and fault detection.

Your research activities:
  • Study switching LCL circuits that modulate semiconductor switches to reduce power dissipation during current limitation.
  • Investigate intelligent anomaly detection, health monitoring, predictive maintenance and potential autonomous recovery.
  • Design, manufacture and experimentally validate a swLCL module that integrates protection, monitoring and fault-management functions.
  • Perform several months secondments at OHB and at UNIOVI, and take part in the network’s training events and conferences.

jobs.title: PhD: Lensless 3D optical imaging
jobs.description_html:
Work Activities
Computational optical imaging is a powerful tool to recover object structure from diffraction patterns without relying on conventional high-quality optics and microscope objectives. While many lensless approaches already work well for 2D imaging, achieving high-resolution volumetric reconstruction of complex structures in compact fiber-based format remains a major challenge.

In this project you will push the boundaries of optical microscopy and develop new approaches for 3D lensless imaging based on ptychography, structured illumination, fiber-based detection and physics-informed computational reconstruction. The work will combine optical experiments with algorithm development. On the experimental side, you will build and optimize ptychography setups using visible light, spatial light modulators, and multimode fibers. You will investigate optimized illumination and detection schemes that maximize information content and imaging performance. On the computational side, you will develop reconstruction algorithms based on compressive sensing and data-driven machine learning approaches for depth-resolved 3D imaging. You will exploit the diversity provided by structured speckle illumination together with sparsity priors to reconstruct complex optical fields and depth-dependent sample structure from a limited set of measurements.

The project includes the development of a compact all-fiber 3D imaging demonstrator aimed at applications in semiconductor metrology. You will therefore collaborate with ASML research on wafer metrology.

Qualifications
You have a MSc degree in physics, optics, photonics or a related field.

Work environment
ARCNL performs fundamental research, focusing on the physics and chemistry involved in current and future key technologies in nanolithography, primarily for the semiconductor industry. While the academic setting and research style are geared towards establishing scientific excellence, the topics in ARCNL’s research program are intimately connected with the interests of the industrial partner ASML. The institute is located at Amsterdam Science Park and currently employs about 100 persons of which 65 are ambitious (young) researchers from all over the globe. www.arcnl.nl

Working conditions
The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment in the service of the Netherlands Foundation of Scientific Research Institutes (NWO-I) for the duration of four years, with a starting salary of gross € 3.115 per month and a range of employment benefits. After successful completion of the PhD research a PhD degree will be granted at a Dutch University. Several courses are offered, specially developed for PhD-students. ARCNL assists any new foreign PhD-student with housing and visa applications and compensates their transport costs and furnishing expenses.

More information?
For further information about the position, please contact Lyuba Amitonova: l.amitonova@arcnl.nl

Application
You can respond to this vacancy online via the button below.

Online screening may be part of the selection.

Diversity code
ARCNL is highly committed to an inclusive and diverse work environment: we want to develop talent and creativity by bringing together people from different backgrounds and cultures. We recruit and select on the basis of competencies and talents. We strongly encourage anyone with the right qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, gender, origin, sexual orientation or physical ability.

Commercial activities in response to this ad are not appreciated.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'STRONGER2GETHER | Van schoolplein tot sportveld: hoe positieve relaties jongeren laten floreren'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Hoe dragen positieve sociale relaties in verschillende leefwerelden bij aan het welzijn en floreren van jongeren? Hoe beïnvloeden sociale relaties op school en in de klas, thuis, online, in de natuur, tijdens sport en in de buurt elkaar? En hoe kunnen we zorgen dat positieve relaties in de ene omgeving bijdragen aan het floreren in andere omgevingen?

Binnen het landelijke onderzoeksprogramma STRONGER2GETHER ga jij als promovendus onderzoek doen naar positieve sociale relaties, welzijn en floreren in het voorbereidend en middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (vmbo en mbo).

Achtergrond en doel van het onderzoek
Positieve sociale relaties vormen een belangrijke basis voor het welzijn en floreren van jongeren. Jongeren groeien op in verschillende, met elkaar verbonden sociale en fysieke omgevingen, zoals school, thuis, sport, buurt en online omgevingen. Hoe deze omgevingen sociaal én fysiek zijn ingericht, kan mede bepalen waar en hoe jongeren elkaar ontmoeten en positieve relaties ontwikkelen. Relaties en ervaringen in deze omgevingen kunnen elkaar beïnvloeden: een jongere kan bijvoorbeeld moeite hebben om aansluiting te vinden op school, maar binnen een sportomgeving juist positieve en ondersteunende relaties ervaren.

Tegelijkertijd is nog onvoldoende bekend hoe positieve sociale relaties van jongeren zich over verschillende sociale omgevingen heen tot elkaar verhouden, welke sociale en fysieke kenmerken van deze omgevingen daarbij een rol spelen, hoe ervaringen in de ene omgeving doorwerken in andere en wat dit betekent voor hun welzijn en floreren.

Binnen dit promotietraject onderzoek je daarom positieve sociale relaties binnen en tussen verschillende sociale en fysieke omgevingen van jongeren. Je onderzoekt welke patronen, mechanismen en kenmerken van de sociale en fysieke leefomgeving bijdragen aan positieve sociale relaties en hoe deze samenhangen met mentaal welzijn en floreren. Daarbij werk je samen met jongeren en professionals, en draag je bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van het CARES-framework (Child & Adolescent Relationships & Ecological Support).

Jouw taken en verantwoordelijkheden
  • Organiseren en uitvoeren van focusgroepen met jongeren en professionals.
  • Uitvoeren van een cross-context DEEP-analyse binnen Research & Development Communities.
  • Uitvoeren van kwalitatief, kwantitatief en/of mixed-methods onderzoek naar sociale relaties over verschillende sociale contexten.
  • Bijdragen aan de verdere ontwikkeling van het CARES-framework.
  • Schrijven van een proefschrift op basis van 3 à 4 Engelstalige wetenschappelijke publicaties.
  • Schrijven van 2 à 3 praktijkgerichte publicaties.
  • Presenteren van onderzoeksresultaten op nationale en internationale conferenties.
  • Samenwerken met andere promovendi, postdocs en praktijkpartners binnen STRONGER2GETHER.
  • Bijdragen aan een documentaire, handboek en andere kennisproducten voor professionals.

Wat bieden wij jou?
STRONGER2GETHER biedt een rijke onderzoeksomgeving met ruimte voor wetenschappelijke ontwikkeling, maatschappelijke impact en persoonlijke groei. Je maakt deel uit van een landelijk consortium waarin onderzoekers, jongeren, professionals en opleidingen samenwerken aan één gezamenlijk doel: het versterken van sociale relaties zodat jongeren kunnen floreren.

Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om innovatieve onderzoeksmethoden toe te passen, samen te werken met jongeren als co-onderzoekers en een zichtbare bijdrage te leveren aan zowel de wetenschap als de praktijk.

Samen willen we bijdragen aan de mogelijkheid dat alle jongeren kunnen floreren doordat hun relaties floreren.

jobs.title: PhD in System Dynamics modelling for resilience in pharmaceutical supply chains
jobs.description_html:
Are you worried about the ever-increasing medicine shortages in Europe? Are you passionate about understanding how we can maximize drug availability to patients in a sustainable and resilient way? Do you want to apply System Dynamics simulation techniques to develop supply chains that support a sustainable availability of critical medicines? If you have experience with System Dynamics modeling and are eager to unravel the complexity of pharmaceutical supply chains this PhD position could be a good fit!

Your contribution and responsibilities include:
  • Map and analyse the global supply chains of selected critical medicines from active ingredients to finished dosage products in the Netherlands.
  • Build multi-echelon simulation models using both qualitative and quantitative modelling techniques in System Dynamics to stress test the global pharmaceutical supply chain for a selected set of drugs.
  • Evaluate strategies to maximise drug availability and resilience sustainably, while considering stock strategies for finished products as well as intermediates and active ingredients, taking manufacturing capacity into account.

For this position we also request the successful candidate to be active in education and providing project management support for the overarching project (including project admin, meeting organisation, etc) for about 20% of her/his time.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Immunology & Hematology
jobs.description_html:
Are you eager to unravel how red blood cells are cleared and recycled, and how the immune system regulates these processes? Then this PhD opportunity could be the perfect next step in your scientific career.

In this project, you will investigate how red blood cells are removed under both physiological and pathological conditions, how neutrophils contribute to transfusion-related immune responses, and which mechanisms regulate the balance between red blood cell clearance and recycling.

Working at the interface of immunology, hematology, and transfusion medicine, you will be part of a dynamic and multidisciplinary research team tackling fundamental questions with direct clinical relevance.

The department
You will be embedded within the Anemia research priority, a vibrant and collaborative research environment that brings together several groups studying blood biology in health and disease. Research within the program spans topics ranging from erythropoiesis and iron homeostasis to transfusion medicine and immune-mediated blood disorders.

A central theme of the program is understanding how senescent or damaged red blood cells are recognized and removed by the immune system, and how the iron recovered from these cells is efficiently recycled to support the production of new red blood cells. By combining expertise in hematology, immunology, iron metabolism, and stem cell biology, the Anemia research priority offers a unique environment for tackling fundamental questions with direct clinical relevance.

What will you do?

  • Design and perform innovative experimental studies.
  • Work with advanced mouse models and cutting-edge immunological techniques.
  • Investigate how neutrophils and phagocytes regulate red blood cell clearance and iron recycling in health and disease.
  • Study the mechanisms underlying hemolysis, alloimmunization, and immune-mediated red blood cell destruction.
  • Analyze, interpret, and present complex experimental data.
  • Publish your findings in leading international scientific journals.
  • Present your work at national and international conferences.


Who are you?

  • You hold an MSc degree in Biomedical Sciences, Immunology, Life Sciences, or a related field.
  • You are curious, motivated, and passionate about solving fundamental biological questions.
  • You have a strong interest in experimental research; experience with immunological, hematological, or cell biology techniques is an advantage.
  • You can work independently while also thriving in a collaborative environment.
  • You have excellent communication skills and are proficient in English.


What we offer

  • A fully funded 4-year PhD position;
  • Comprehensive training and supervision by experienced researchers;
  • Access to state-of-the-art research facilities and technologies;
  • An inspiring, international, and collaborative research environment;
  • Opportunities to build a strong academic network through collaborations and conferences;
  • Excellent opportunities for scientific and personal development;
  • This PhD position is remunerated according to the CAO UMC salary scale for PhD candidates, increasing annually from €3,217 to €4,077 gross per month (full-time);
  • 8.33% year-end bonus and 8.33% holiday allowance, flexibly payable;
  • 201 vacation hours with a full-time (36 hours) contract, of which 7 vacation days are part of your individual choice budget;
  • Generous travel reimbursement, starting from the first kilometer;
  • Every 3 years, €2,000 development budget for your professional ambitions;
  • Collective agreements with various insurers;
  • Flexible benefits system where you can tailor your employment conditions;
  • Pension plan with Pensioenfonds Zorg en Welzijn. We contribute 65%.


More about our terms of employment can be found here.

Excited?
Would you like to contribute to groundbreaking discoveries in red blood cell biology, immune regulation, and transfusion medicine? Join us and become part of a research program that will advance our understanding of hematological and immune-mediated diseases while helping to shape the future of patient care. Please submit your CV, academic transcripts, a motivation letter and contact details for at least two references.

More Information:
Are you interested and do you have questions about the position? Please reach out to dr. Hanke Matlung, Groupleader Iron Homeostasis, Sanquin Amsterdam (h.matlung@sanquin.nl).

A pre-employment screening is part of the process.

Acquisition is not appreciated. Sanquin does not accept unsolicited help from agencies for this vacancy. Resumes sent by agencies (in any form) to any employee of Sanquin without a valid written search request are considered the property of Sanquin, for which no compensation is owed in any way.

Address details
Plesmanlaan 125
1066 CX, Amsterdam

jobs.title: PhD-student IC-you project (1fte)
jobs.description_html:
Een op de drie jongeren (12 tot 25 jaar) ervaart emotionele problemen, zoals depressie en angst. Binnen het IC-YOU project onderzoeken we of en hoe gesprekken met mensen die je vertrouwt kunnen bijdragen aan het welzijn van jongeren – of juist onbedoeld schadelijk kunnen zijn. Als PhD-student richt je je op het versterken van die communicatie. Je onderzoekt samen met jongeren waarom, wanneer en met wie jongeren hun gevoelens delen én welke barrières hen daarbij in de weg staan. Ben jij geïnteresseerd in het welzijn van jongeren? Ben jij geinteresseerd in wetenschappelijk onderzoek in het dagelijkse leven van jongeren? Dan nodigen we je uit om te solliciteren.

Functieomschrijving
Steeds meer jongeren ervaren emotionele problemen. Een gesprek met iemand die je vertrouwt – zoals een docent, sportcoach of buur – kan hen helpen zich beter te voelen. Maar niet alle jongeren hebben iemand bij wie ze terechtkunnen, en het delen van gevoelens is vaak lastig. In dit PhD-project onderzoek je hoe we de communicatie tussen jongeren en vertrouwde volwassenen kunnen versterken en welke barrières we daarbij moeten doorbreken.

Je zult verder bouwen op wetenschappelijk onderzoek met participatieve methoden en focusgroepen met jongeren, een nationale survey, en intensieve longitudinale data, zoals experience sampling methodes (ESM). Met statistische analyses (in R en Mplus) onderzoek je met wie, wanneer en waarom jongeren hun dagelijkse zorgen of ernstigere problemen delen, en wat hen daarin belemmert of juist helpt. Met hulp van twee senior begeleiders schrijf je op basis van deze data vier wetenschappelijke artikelen die samen een proefschrift vormen.

Dit PhD-project maakt deel uit van het IC-YOU onderzoeksproject, gefinancierd door de Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO-VICI). Je werkt nauw samen met collega’s (twee postdocs) én hebt ook contact met maatschappelijke partners zoals De Kindertelefoon en MIND Us. Jouw theoretische inzichten vormen een sleutel in het verbeteren van de communicatie tussen jongeren en hun omgeving.

Naast je onderzoek besteed je een deel van je tijd (10%) aan onderwijs binnen de opleiding Pedagogische Wetenschappen aan de Erasmus Universiteit Rotterdam. Dit kan bijvoorbeeld bestaan uit het begeleiden van scripties of het verzorgen van werkgroepen. De voertaal van het onderwijs is Nederlands.

jobs.title: PhD candidate: Cardiac electrophysiology during ex situ heart perfusion
jobs.description_html:
How can we better assess and preserve donor hearts before transplantation? Join the RRESHAPE-HTx project to investigate how monitoring and controlling cardiac electrical function during ex situ heart perfusion can improve donor-heart preservation and transplantation outcomes.

Funded by a Dekker grant from the Dutch Heart Foundation, the project takes a translational approach, spanning preclinical research in large-animal models and clinical research on human donor hearts. You will help explore whether electrophysiological monitoring can support the quality assessment of donor hearts before transplantation, and whether targeted control of electrical function can improve preservation of donor hearts. Ultimately, the project aims to help expand the donor pool and improve outcomes after heart transplantation.

As a PhD candidate, you will be part of an interdisciplinary team advancing ex-situ heart perfusion towards clinical application. Working alongside technicians, fellow PhD candidates, scientists and clinicians, you will contribute to both preclinical and clinical studies.

Your work will include:
  • Conducting studies of ex situ perfusion in isolated hearts, including large-animal hearts and human donor hearts.
  • Investigating cardiac electrophysiology during perfusion, including approaches to monitor and control electrical function.
  • Conducting studies in a clinical setting in collaboration with thoracic surgeons and clinical perfusionists.
  • Analysing and presenting research findings and writing scientific publications that will form the basis of your PhD thesis.
  • Developing your research skills through relevant courses at the Graduate School of Life Sciences.

jobs.title: PhD Position Biomolecular Ultrasound Imaging
jobs.description_html:
Advance biomolecular ultrasound imaging and enable new non-invasive ways to observe and understand the cellular activity in living biological tissues. In this interdisciplinary Vici-funded project, you will develop cutting-edge, fully noninvasive imaging methods with real scientific and societal impact. This new investigative tool will be used to discover how organ function emerges from cellular activity. You will work at the frontier of ultrasound technology, molecular engineering and neuroscience, in an international research team.

Job description
As a PhD candidate, you develop and validate fully noninvasive volumetric ultrasound imaging of cells expressing sound-scattering proteins, with a focus on improving image resolution. You design and implement ultrasound sequences, build experimental setups, and develop advanced reconstruction and signal processing pipelines and use 3D cell culture models. Your work contributes directly to enabling new ways to study brain function in health and disease.

You are part of the Maresca Lab within the Imaging Physics department at TU Delft, an ambitious and rapidly growing research group at the forefront of ultrasound imaging. The team currently consists of researchers with interdisciplinary expertise spanning physics, engineering, and bioengineering of proteins and cells. With the recent acquisition of major research grants, the lab is expanding significantly, including new postdocs, PhD candidates, and engineering support, offering a dynamic environment with opportunities to shape its future direction.

You work closely with colleagues in Delft and become part of a collaboration research effort with partners at UMC Utrecht and in the USA. This international network gives you direct access to complementary expertise, unique research perspectives, and high-impact collaborations at the forefront of ultrasound neuroimaging.

At TU Delft, you have access to state-of-the-art imaging facilities and technical support. You will publish in leading journals, present at international conferences, and contribute to grant activities. The role offers opportunities to further develop your scientific profile, supervision skills, and independence as a researcher.

Job requirements
  • You hold a MSc degree in nanobiology, or a closely related field.
  • You have solid hands-on experience in experimental ultrasound imaging via your Master’s internship or previous work-experience. This is a must-have.
  • You have at least 6 months experience with nonlinear ultrasound sequence programming, ultrasound image reconstruction and signal processing.
  • You have strong bioengineering skills – including protein and cellular engineering.
  • You communicate clearly in English, both orally and in writing, in scientific contexts.
  • You work effectively in interdisciplinary and international teams, and manage your own research progress independently.
  • Experience with genetically encoded gas vesicles is a must have.
  • Experience with optical microscopy theory is a must have.
  • You show motivation to contribute to collaborative research on brain imaging and neuroscience applications.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.

These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.

Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty Applied Sciences
With more than 1,100 employees, including 150 pioneering principal investigators, as well as a population of about 3,600 passionate students, the Faculty of Applied Sciences is an inspiring scientific ecosystem. Focusing on key enabling technologies, such as quantum- and nanotechnology, photonics, biotechnology, synthetic biology and materials for energy storage and conversion, our faculty aims to provide solutions to important problems of the 21st century. To that end, we educate innovative students in broad Bachelor's and specialist Master's programmes with a strong research component. Our scientists conduct ground-breaking fundamental and applied research in the fields of Life and Health Science & Technology, Nanoscience, Chemical Engineering, Radiation Science & Technology, and Engineering Physics. We are also training the next generation of high school teachers.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Applied Sciences.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information
Are you excited about advancing cellular ultrasound imaging and contributing to understanding the human brain? We warmly encourage you to apply. Diverse perspectives strengthen our research, and we are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive academic environment.

For questions please email recruitment-tnw@tudelft.nl.

Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 2 December 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents:
  • Motivation letter (max. one page). We value authentic, personally written letters. Please explain what attracts you to this specific project, how your background connects to the requirements, how you see yourself contributing to the team, and what motivates you to pursue a postdoc within our mission and research context.
  • Detailed CV, clearly highlighting your relevant skills and experience in experimental ultrasound imaging, sequence programming and image reconstruction and signal processing.
  • A detailed list of your bachelor and master reports as well as key initiatives and contributions in other areas such as communication, personal leadership, teaching, entrepreneurship, and societal impact.

jobs.title: PhD student (m/f/x)
jobs.description_html:
Quantum computing devices are rapidly increasing in scale and complexity. However they are still very far away from the abstract ideal of a computer, and an important part of making them better is designing procedures that characterize errors and noise in an efficient and robust. Do you enjoy working at the intersection between physics and computer science? Are you comfortable with mathematical work and interested in applying those skills in a practical setting? Then CWI invites you to apply for a PhD position where you will research testing and learning algorithms for fault-tolerant quantum computers in the context of the EQUATE ERC starting grant project, supervised by Dr. Jonas Helsen.

Job description
As part of your PhD project, you will develop and mathematically analyze new methods for extracting information from quantum computers, with a focus on testing and learning algorithms and their interactions with quantum error correction.

Possible research directions include (but are not limited to):
  • Testing and learning under resource restrictions (specifically the “low-magic” setting)
  • Testing and learning of QEC relevant properties such as membership of the Clifford hierarchy
  • The interaction of (logical) noise with learning algorithms

You will:
  • Research fault-tolerant quantum computing, developing new testing and learning algorithms and analyzing their properties.
  • Work with colleagues on translating these theoretical algorithms to a more practical setting, perhaps even all the way down to real experiments.
  • Publish and present your work in international conferences and journals.
  • Be an active part of the local research groups at CWI and QuSoft.

jobs.title: PhD student (m/f/x)
jobs.description_html:
Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) has a vacancy in the Computer Security research group for a talented PhD student (m/f/x) on the subject of formal methods and design automation for cryptography and hardware security

Job description
Cryptographic protocols and secure hardware are increasingly deployed in settings where mistakes are costly and hard to detect, yet designing, optimizing, and verifying them still relies heavily on manual expert effort. In this PhD project, you will develop formal methods and design automation techniques for cryptography and hardware security, making secure systems both more efficient and more trustworthy. The position is part of the NWO Gravitation program Challenges in Cyber Security (CiCS), which brings together leading security research groups across the Netherlands.

Possible research directions include (but are not limited to):
  • Logic synthesis for secure computation. Paradigms such as multi-party computation (MPC) and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) have cost models very different from conventional hardware. You will develop new cost metrics for specific paradigms and platforms, together with synthesis methods that optimize circuits toward them.
  • Computer-aided cryptography and hardware security. Security arguments for cryptographic protocols and their hardware implementations are still largely constructed and checked by hand. You will explore how formal methods and automated reasoning tools can support the design, analysis, and verification of cryptographic constructions, as well as hardware security properties such as resistance to side-channel leakage.
  • Privacy-preserving formal verification. In many settings, a party needs to convince others that a hardware or software design meets its specification without disclosing the design itself. You will study how verification techniques can be combined with cryptographic tools such as zero-knowledge proofs to establish correctness and security properties of confidential designs.

The exact focus will be shaped together with you, based on your interests and background. Examples of our recent related work include “Proving Circuit Functional Equivalence in Zero Knowledge” (ACM CCS 2026) and “Think Locally Before Computing Jointly: Efficient Secure Multi-Party Computation via Maximizing Local Processing” (IACR TCHES 2027).

As a PhD student on this project, you will:
  • develop the theoretical foundations of new methods, such as formal models, algorithms, and security proofs;
  • implement prototype tools and evaluate them on realistic benchmarks;
  • collaborate with researchers in the CiCS consortium and with international partners;
  • present your results at international conferences and publish them in leading venues.

You will be part of the Computer Security group at CWI, headed by Prof. Marten van Dijk, and supervised by Dr. Chenglu Jin.

jobs.title: PhD Position on Safe Experience-Based Learning for Autonomous Drone Flight Control
jobs.description_html:
Join TU Delft's MAVLab as a PhD candidate and develop safe learning methods that allow autonomous drones to improve their flight control through their own flight experience.

Job description
PhD on Safe Experience-Based Learning for Autonomous Drone Flight Control – TU Delft MAVLab

Conventional autopilots rely on fixed control laws and do not improve through accumulated flight experience. Human pilots, in contrast, become more capable as they gain experience. This project investigates how autonomous drones can similarly improve their flight control over time, based on their own flight experience, while remaining safe and reliable from day one.

The central research challenge is to learn and adapt flight-control laws without allowing the learning process to compromise the safety or performance of the drone. You will investigate approaches to safe learning and adaptation, including whether updates should take place during flight or between flights, and how the system can detect and handle potentially unsafe changes. The specific methods and safeguards remain open to research.

The research will be developed and evaluated on real flying drones (quad copters and VTOL winged drone, like the Rotating Wing Drone). The drone must be capable of autonomous flight from the outset, with its performance and learning progress assessed through real flight experiments. The project may also explore how experience-based learning can be extended to recognising and responding to dangerous situations.

You will join the Micro Air Vehicle Lab (MAVLab) in the Control and Simulation group of the Department of Control and Operations at TU Delft's Faculty of Aerospace Engineering. MAVLab has extensive experience in developing, building and testing autonomous aerial vehicles, including rotating-wing drones and projects such as NederDrone, which focuses on drone operations from ships. The lab combines fundamental research with a hands-on experimental approach, where new ideas are implemented and validated through real-world flight tests. You will work alongside researchers with complementary expertise in autonomous flight, vehicle design and control.

jobs.description_html:
Join TU Delft's MAVLab as a PhD candidate and develop fast, fully onboard autonomy that lets lightweight drones perceive, predict and overtake other drones in real flight.

Job description
Autonomous drones are becoming increasingly capable of flying at high speeds, but enabling them to interact reliably with other drones remains a major challenge. When drones fly in close proximity, they must rapidly perceive the motion and orientation of other vehicles, predict their future trajectories, and adapt their own flight paths accordingly.

In this PhD project, you will investigate new methods for fast autonomous navigation and close-range drone-to-drone interaction. You will develop and investigate sensing, state estimation, motion prediction, and guidance, navigation and control strategies that enable drones to interact reliably while flying at high speeds.

A central challenge is to achieve this with extremely lightweight and computationally efficient onboard systems. All essential perception, estimation, prediction, planning and control must run onboard the drone in real time, without relying on offboard computation, and within the strict size, weight and power (SWaP) constraints of small flying platforms.

The project will explore different approaches to sensing and autonomous control, including conventional cameras and potentially event-based vision sensors. You will investigate how drones can estimate the relative state of other drones, anticipate their motion, and use this information to plan and control their own trajectories. The specific sensors, algorithms and hardware solutions remain open to investigation.

The research aims to make an original scientific contribution to fast autonomous navigation, balancing reliable high-speed performance with the limited computational resources of lightweight drones. A key objective is to demonstrate reliable overtaking in real flight. The project therefore combines scientific research with implementation and experimental validation on real flying drones.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate: Reconstructing Environmental Intermittency in Early Bronze Age southeast Arabia (1.0
jobs.description_html:
The Department of world Archaeology, Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, is looking for a PhD candidate in the field of Archaeology to join the Precarious Landscapes project funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) and carried out at the Faculty of Archaeology of Leiden University.

Project description
The Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, seeks to appoint a full-time PhD candidate to investigate the relationship between environmental intermittency, human-landscape interaction, and the emergence of social complexity in Early Bronze Age (EBA; 3200-2000 BCE) southeast Arabia. The project is based at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Bat, Oman, and examines how ancient communities navigated unpredictable environmental conditions through mobility, resource use, and social interaction across a dispersed landscape. The successful candidate will work closely with the project leader and an international network of collaborators specialising in archaeology, paleoenvironmental reconstruction, and geochemistry. Isotope research will be conducted under the supervision of specialist collaborators at the Sorbonne University’s ISTeP geoscience laboratory in Paris. The project also builds on the established Bat Archaeological Project (BAP), providing access to extensive archaeological collections, spatial datasets, and fieldwork infrastructure in Oman. The research should lead you to obtain a PhD within a four-year timeframe (1.0 FTE). Candidates with a good knowledge of southeast Arabian prehistory and isotope methodologies are especially encouraged to apply. The PhD candidate will be supervised by Dr. Jennifer Swerida (the project leader) and Dr. Bleda Düring.

Desert landscapes are characterised by extreme environmental intermittency, where prolonged periods of hyper-aridity are punctuated by episodic inundations. These events rapidly redistribute water, sediments, vegetation, and other resources, creating localised and short-lived opportunities for human activity. Despite these challenging conditions, complex societies emerged in southeast Arabia during the Early Bronze Age. However, the short-term environmental fluctuations that structured human behaviour in these landscapes remain largely invisible in archaeological records, limiting our understanding of how social complexity developed under conditions of environmental uncertain.

The NWO Vidi project Precarious Landscapes addresses this gap by combining landscape-scape archaeological investigation with a developing method for producing high-resolution paleoenvironmental reconstructions. The project employs stable isotope (δ¹⁸O and δ¹³C) analysis of incremental growth rings in terrestrial and aquatic gastropod shells to reconstruct localised environmental conditions at temporal scales of weeks to years, rather than centuries. This approach provides a unique opportunity to investigate how episodic flooding and fluctuating resource availability influenced human activity and movement across the landscape. The project focuses on the Wadi al-Hijr of Oman, which contains multiple Early Bronze Age Archaeological sites, including the major oasis settlement of Bat and smaller, intermittently occupied locations. The project investigates how these locations functioned as interconnected components of wider, multi-sited communities rather than as isolated settlements.

The PhD candidate will be primarily responsible for reconstructing short-term environmental conditions through stable isotope analysis of gastropod shells. The research will involve the analysis of approximately 250 specimens form secure Early Bronze Age archaeological contexts and geomorphological profiles. These specimens will be sampled along successive shell growth bands to reconstruct localised environmental variability. The resulting data will be integrated with archaeological, spatial, and chronological datasets to investigate the relationship between environmental intermittency and patterns of human activity.

The research will contribute to the development of a new Precarious Landscapes model, which understands social complexity as emerging through the organisation of mobility, resource use, and social interaction across environmentally variable landscapes.

Key tasks
  • Conduct independent and collaborative research in the field of paleoenvironmental reconstruction through isotope analysis and the archaeology of southeast Arabia;
  • Contribute to the overall aims of the Precarious Landscapes project, particularly the reconstruction of localised paleoenvironmental conditions across the Wadi al-Hirj;

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Philosophy of Physics
jobs.description_html:
PhD Candidate in Philosophy of Physics
The Faculty of Humanities, Leiden Institute for Philosophy (IPH), invites applications for a fully funded PhD position (1.0 fte) in Philosophy of Physics.

What you will do
The PhD candidate will be working within the project REALDIMENSIONS: Realism About Dimensions, Units, and their Interrelations with Constants, an EU-funded European Research Council (ERC) Starting Grant project running from 2027 through 2031. This research project, directed by Dr Caspar Jacobs (assistant professor in Theoretical Philosophy at Leiden University), investigates the nature of dimensions, constants, and units.

Dimensions, constants and units are all crucial to contemporary physics, yet these concepts have barely received attention from philosophers, even within the tradition of naturalised metaphysics that tries to extract metaphysical content from physical theories. The dominant approaches in physics either see them as merely human conventions, or consider only pure dimensionless numbers as ultimately real. This has left a core part of our physical theories unexamined. The overall aim of the REALDIMENSIONS project is to propose a new, realist framework in which dimensions and units track genuine features of reality, and dimensional constants are as real as directly measurable quantities such as mass or charge.

You can find some more detail about the project here.

Potential research topics for the PhD candidate include (but are not restricted to): (i) whether the dimensions of a quantity indicate its nature or essence; (ii) the fundamentality of dimensionless quantities and constants; (iii) the metaphysics of universal constants such as c or h; (iv) the role of constants in laws and intertheoretic reduction; (v) the absolutism-comparativism debate in the context of special relativity and quantum mechanics.

Your key tasks are
  • Completing an English-language doctoral dissertation within the period of appointment;
  • (Co-)authoring a number of peer-reviewed publications on the topics of the project;
  • Presenting research results at national and international conferences and workshops;
  • Contributing to the organisation of conferences, workshops and seminars;
  • Actively participating in meetings and research activities organised by your research group at the Institute for Philosophy;
  • Participating in relevant PhD courses and workshops, organised in accordance with the guidelines of the Faculty of Humanities and the Institute for Philosophy.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Humanities at Leiden University is a unique international centre for the advanced study of languages, cultures, arts, and societies worldwide, in their historical contexts from prehistory to the present. Our faculty is home to over 7,000 students and 800 staff members. For more information see: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/humanities.

The Leiden Institute for Philosophy (IPH) is one of the seven institutes of the Faculty of Humanities. The institute conducts research and offers teaching in the standard areas of philosophy in analytic and continental traditions and in intercultural philosophy as well as their history. With around 40 employees and over 600 students, the institute offers an innovative, collegial, and international working environment. The Institute for Philosophy has cultivated a broad and inclusive research profile that is unique in the Netherlands. It developed a structure that promotes interactions across systematic and historical approaches, attempted to bridge analytical and continental traditions, and integrated global and comparative perspectives. IPH's research is organized into five flexible research groups, allowing for interdisciplinary participation and collaboration. This position falls within the Theoretical Philosophy Group, which has a particular focus on topics at the intersection of metaphysics and the philosophy of science.

Leiden University is also a member of the History and Philosophy of Physics in the Netherlands (HPP-NL) network. HPP-NL organises a twice-yearly workshop which rotates between the different universities in the Netherlands.

jobs.title: PhD position: Visualization and comparison of pangenomes
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in bioinformatics or computational genomics and are you curious and eager to learn more about comparative genomics? Do you have a background in bioinformatics, computer science, or statistical genetics? And are you enthusiastic to pursue a PhD at one of the leading international universities in the fields of healthy food, the living environment and agriculture? Then you are the candidate we are looking for!

You will be employed for four years to work on a new project, “Comparative genomics and structural variant visualization in pangenome graphs of animal species”. This project will be funded as a partnership between Hendrix Genetics B.V. and Wageningen University to improve livestock genome resources to benefit academic research and industrial application. One of the major goals of this project will be to design new methods to visualize pangenomes and to compare the topologies of different pangenome graphs for comparative genomics discoveries. You will be located at the Animal Breeding and Genomics group of Wageningen University & Research in Wageningen, and will have close associations with other Universities and livestock breeding companies.

The creation of a reference-quality genome assembly no longer requires large teams of experts or substantial funding from government agencies. The democratization of the process has even enabled small groups to generate high-quality assemblies for non-model organisms at fractions of a percent of the time and cost of the original human genome project. In this new phase of the post-genome era, consolidation of individualized genome assemblies into graph-based structures called “pangenomes” has enabled fast reconciliation of the structural variations found in individuals or even breeds. However, the analysis of pangenome graphs beyond the species taxonomic level is hindered by a paucity of visualization tools, and an absence of tools that allow for graph topology comparisons. A methodology is needed that enables comparisons of different pangenome graphs and can visualize the differences/syntenies among them.

This project will develop methods to enable the comparison of different pangenome graphs to identify shared regions of conservation or synteny that are important indicators of selection in agricultural species. By providing associated visualization tools, complex structural variants can be properly represented and compared across populations. The developed methods will be applicable to other plant and animal species and will also be useful in comparing recently developed conservation wildlife pangenomes designed to catalogue and compare genetic variation in endangered species.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Performing graph synteny analyses on pangenome graphs of chicken (Gallus gallus) and turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) to confirm chromosome synteny and structure that will improve variation maps made for both species.
  • Predicting the functional effects of observed graph variation to help identify differences in orthologous genes that may drive phenotypic differences among breeds or species.
  • Extending existing methodologies for identifying selective genome sweeps or population fixation events to enable comparative genomics analysis within pangenome graphs.
  • Developing methods to visualize genome graph synteny to highlight complex structural variations within or between populations.

You will work here
The research is embedded within the chair Animal Breeding and Genomics (link internet page Chairgroup), which is led by Prof. Mario Calus. You will be supervised by Dr Derek Bickhart and Dr Sandra Smit.

jobs.title: PhD Position Operations Management
jobs.description_html:
PhD position in Operations management for E-commerce logistics: leading the transition to reusable packages

Job description
E-commerce has become a strong component of our daily lives. The rise of webshops and platform technology gives us the opportunity to have the desired products at home in no time. However, the ease of this process, its increased adoption during COVID times, along with policies to guarantee consumer satisfaction, has been generating a massive volume of parcels around the globe and, very frequently, consequent returns of products to the seller. Although the logistics service providers around these transport flows have reacted with heavy process optimization, the waste generated is substantial and inevitable when the loading unit is a carton box (CB).

The use of CBs has several financial and environmental drawbacks. First, CBs cannot be reutilized, and because of this, they are continuously produced and not entirely made with recycled material. Secondly, from a logistical standpoint, the rigid composition of these boxes, which cannot always perfectly fit the product inside, inevitably causes the shipping of air. In turn, this causes an inefficient utilization of the capacity of the means of transport. Thirdly, the waste management of papers affects municipalities due to the extra handling costs, sometimes increased by wrong recycling behaviors. Consumers' satisfaction, experience, and environmental perception are not fully positive when dealing with a single-use box that needs to be torn and thrown at the end of the life cycle. In response to this, the European Commission has only recently launched an action plan to limit these drawbacks, a sign that while the problem is acknowledged, we are still far from globally implementable solutions.

The development and the adoption of flexible, durable, reusable, and smart packages, which we define RELABELs, can solve the aforementioned problems generated by single-use carton boxes. Digital features can favour tracking and autonomous decisions, which depend, for example, on the recipient's availability, in line with the Physical Internet guidelines. For example, a RELABEL could autonomously suggest a slower mode of transport if the recipient is unavailable in a close time window, relieving the pressure on the transport system. RELABELs can substantially reduce the CO2 footprint, improve customer satisfaction, generate better value for transport capacity, and improve the efficiency of packing procedures. Their reusable nature has the potential to reduce packaging expenditures, while their adaptable dimensions can contribute to lowering transportation costs. Furthermore, environmental benefits may be realized through the reduction of packaging waste and decreased transportation-related emissions.

Within the NWO-funded project, named in short "Relabel it", the PhD candidate is expected to research several logistics challenges ineherent to a full adoption of the reusable packages.

There are several aspects that require attention to exploit the features of flexible packages.
  1. Packing Model: The model will be developed for LSPs and used for packing RELABELs into transport units, e.g., trucks, whilst minimizing the required size of the fleet that carries out transportation.
  2. Storage Location Model: The model will be used to determine the number and the geographical locations of RELABELs' return and pickup points in a city.
  3. RELABELs Collection Model: We study how RELABELs are collected and repositioned to their storage locations, and the frequency of the collection to make sure that empties are readily available. Moreover, it is relevant to investigate how the LSP could integrate the return of empties into its schedule.
  4. Return Mechanism Design Model: We aim to study the mechanisms that can incentivize swift returns; we will learn lessons from the sea container shipping industry and current deposit system in the food industry
  5. Manufacturing, filling and refurbishing: several challenges related to production, the filling process and refurbishment can be expected

Job requirements
We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic researcher with strong analytical skills. The candidate should also feel at ease in interdisciplinary environments, since the Relabel it project embraces a wide range of disciplines (e.g., circular economy, product design, simulation) and collaboration is expected with practitioners, given the presence of important stakeholders in the project.

  • Good programming skills (e.g., C/C++, Python).
